Kuta, Indonesia Collector Series (#455136 · Indonesia Collector Series (2011)Kuta is Bali's famous surf-and-sunset beach town, and fittingly this 2011 piece breaks the usual white mold with a green-inside, green-outside body showing a traditional Balinese woman dancing. That dancer nods to Bali's living temple culture, think Legong and Barong performances rather than just the beaches. The full-color green treatment and dated 2011 release make this a more distinctive Indonesia mug than the standard white Collector Series format.
Balikpapan, Indonesia Collector Se#455137 · Indonesia Collector Series (2011)This is from the 2011 Indonesia Collector Series, also called the Indonesian Dancer Series, where each city gets a single traditional dancer in a tone-on-tone wrap, here in green. Balikpapan is the oil-rich port on Borneo's east coast, gateway to Kalimantan. The eleven-city dancer set, Bali through Yogyakarta, is a known target run, and collectors hunt these because they shipped only within Indonesia.
Batam, Indonesia Collector Series#455138 · Indonesia Collector Series (2011)Batam is the duty-free industrial island in the Riau Archipelago, a quick ferry hop from Singapore, and here it gets the 2011 Indonesia Collector Series treatment, a traditional dancer rendered tone-on-tone in dark blue. It is one of the eleven cities in the Indonesian Dancer set. Because Batam itself is more workaday port than tourist icon, this dancer-format mug is the kind of completist piece that mainly turns up through Indonesia-based sellers.
Ubud, Indonesia Collector Series (#455139 · Indonesia Collector Series (2011)From 2011, this mustard-toned Ubud mug breaks the white-inside norm with a dancing woman, evoking the Legong and Barong dances of Bali's cultural heart. Ubud is the island's arts capital, ringed by rice terraces and the Sacred Monkey Forest, and a later wave of fame followed Eat Pray Love. The dated 2011 series and the warm color make this one of the more distinctive pieces in the collection.
Indonesia, Indonesia Collector Ser#455140 · Indonesia Collector Series (2011)This belongs to the 2011 Indonesia Collector Series, the all-brown run featuring traditional dancers, with cities like Bali, Bandung, Makassar, Solo and Yogyakarta each getting a regional dance figure. The woman dancing outside celebrates Indonesia's classical court dance, an art of slow precise hand and eye movement carried down through the royal Javanese and Balinese traditions. A distinctive, cohesive series that some editions originally shipped with a batik card, so collectors prize the complete sets.
Puerto Rico#455171 · City Mug Collector SeriesOld San Juan rendered in purple is the heart of this one, the walled colonial quarter founded in 1521, making San Juan one of the oldest European-established cities in the Americas. The blue cobblestones and the fortresses of El Morro and San Cristóbal define it. A City Mug that represents the whole island commonwealth, and a personal favorite for its rich colonial palette.
London#455307 · City Mug Collector SeriesLondon goes for the ornate gilded gates of Buckingham Palace rendered in a grey-blue photo, the official London residence of the British monarch since 1837 and the backdrop to the Changing of the Guard. Choosing the palace gates over the usual Big Ben or Tower Bridge is a more intimate, less clichéd take. As a flagship world city, London is one of the most produced and collected pieces in the entire series, but this gates version stands a bit apart.
Dublin#455308 · City Mug Collector SeriesThat green photo of a bridge over the river is the Liffey, the waterway that splits Dublin and is crossed by the beloved cast-iron Ha'penny Bridge of 1816, named for the toll once charged to walk it. Capital of Ireland and a UNESCO City of Literature, Dublin gave us Joyce, Wilde and Yeats, plus the black stuff brewed at St James's Gate since 1759.
Cardiff#455310 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe grey castle is Cardiff Castle, layered from a Roman fort to a Norman keep to the lavish Victorian Gothic rebuild by architect William Burges for the 3rd Marquess of Bute. Its 40-meter Clock Tower, finished in 1873, was the tallest thing in Cardiff and hides jewel-box smoking rooms inside. A handsome mug for the Welsh capital.
Edinburgh#455314 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe grey-blue photo is Edinburgh Castle, perched on Castle Rock, an extinct volcanic plug that has been fortified for over a thousand years and still fires its One O'Clock Gun daily. Scotland's capital and a UNESCO World Heritage city, Edinburgh splits between its medieval Old Town and Georgian New Town, and it hosts the world's largest arts festival, the Fringe, every August.
CymruWales#455423 · City Mug Collector SeriesCymru is simply Wales in Welsh, and this red Y Ddraig Goch, the red dragon, is the heart of the national flag, claimed to be the oldest flag still in use and officially adopted in 1959. The legend, told by Geoffrey of Monmouth, has a red dragon and a white one battling beneath Dinas Emrys, with the red one winning, which is why the bilingual CymruWales branding on this City Mug feels so loaded with myth.
Luzern#455426 · City Mug Collector SeriesLuzern, or Lucerne, puts its single most famous sight on the cup in light blue, the Kapellbrucke, the covered wooden Chapel Bridge first built around 1365 with its octagonal stone water tower, the oldest surviving truss bridge in Europe. A 1993 fire destroyed much of it before it was painstakingly rebuilt. A gorgeous, instantly identifiable Swiss landmark and one of the more beautiful entries in the European City Mug Collector Series.
Sofia#455427 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe brown famous building on this Sofia mug depicts the Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, the gold-domed Bulgarian Orthodox basilica finished in 1912 to honor the Russian soldiers who died freeing Bulgaria from Ottoman rule. Bulgaria never had a large Starbucks footprint, so Sofia is a genuinely scarce City Mug and a prize for anyone chasing complete Balkans coverage. I love that such a young coffee market produced a mug centered on a century-old monument to liberation.
England#455429 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe coat of arms here is the heraldry of England, three gold lions passant on red, the royal arms first borne by Richard the Lionheart in the late twelfth century and still seen on the national football and cricket badges. Choosing the arms rather than a single landmark gives the England country mug a stately, regal feel distinct from the London-focused pieces in the series.
Barcelona#455430 · City Mug Collector SeriesThose flowing green motifs are pure Antoni Gaudi, the Catalan architect whose undulating Modernisme defines Barcelona, from Casa Batllo to the still-unfinished Sagrada Familia. The 2002 Collector Series Barcelona is a genuinely desirable European piece; I have seen Spain Global Icon Barcelona cups listed around 80 to 150 dollars depending on condition. A Gaudi mug is one of the few where the art alone carries the city.
Argentina#455431 · City Mug Collector SeriesThis is a country mug, and it leads with Argentina's most jaw-dropping natural wonder, the Perito Moreno Glacier in Patagonia's Los Glaciares National Park. Unlike most of the world's ice, Perito Moreno is famously stable and periodically advances, calving huge blue blocks into Lake Argentino with thunderous cracks that draw crowds to its viewing walkways. A striking choice over the usual tango or Iguazú imagery, and a standout in the country-level City Mugs.
Buenos Aires#455436 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe dancing couple and the Obelisco nail the two things Buenos Aires is truly known for. Tango was born in the working-class barrios and port districts in the late 1800s, and the 67-meter Obelisco was raised in just 31 days in 1936 to mark the city's 400th anniversary. Together they make this one of the more expressive City Mugs to hold.
Jordan#455438 · City Mug Collector SeriesJordan puts its rightful star on the cup, the rose-red rock city of Petra carved straight into sandstone cliffs by the Nabataeans over two thousand years ago and named one of the New Seven Wonders of the World in 2007. The image shows Al-Khazneh, the Treasury facade made famous worldwide by Indiana Jones. A clean, classic City Mug Collector Series piece, and Petra makes it one of the more visually striking Middle East entries in the line.
Jerusalem#455440 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe light-yellow dove on the Jerusalem mug is the peace dove, a fitting symbol for a city sacred to three faiths. This is one of the holy grails of the hobby, because Starbucks closed all its Israel stores in 2003, leaving only a handful of these 2002 mugs in the wild. Verified sales have run into the hundreds, with examples changing hands around the $500 to $750 range, so this quiet little dove is one of the most valuable pieces I own.
Tel-Aviv#455444 · City Mug Collector SeriesThis is one of the genuinely scarce ones. Starbucks opened in Israel in 2001 and pulled out completely in 2003, so the Tel-Aviv mug, with its warm sunset over a red ground, had a tiny production window. Collectors treat surviving mint examples as among the rarer City Mugs, with unused pieces changing hands well into the low hundreds of dollars, and a blue prototype variant is whispered about. A short-lived market makes for a long-lived collectible.
Kingdom of Saudi Arabia#455448 · City Mug Collector SeriesRather than naming a single city, this one represents the whole Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, with green palm trees on the body echoing the date palm at the center of the national emblem above its two crossed swords. Saudi Arabia became one of Starbucks' early and large Gulf markets, which is why country-level mugs like this exist alongside the city pieces. A solid, understated entry in the Middle East run of the Collector Series.
Potsdam#455476 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe purple palace is Sanssouci, Frederick the Great's rococo summer retreat built in the 1740s in Potsdam, just outside Berlin. The name means without cares in French, and the palace and its terraced vineyard gardens are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. A regal German City Mug that I rank among the more elegant in the series.
Hangzhou#455477 · City Mug Collector SeriesHangzhou is famous for West Lake, the UNESCO-listed scene of causeways, willows and arched stone bridges that inspired Chinese poets for a thousand years, so the turquoise river-and-bridge design is exactly the right hook. Marco Polo reportedly called it the finest city in the world. A lovely City Mug Collector Series piece, with the cool water tone capturing the misty, painterly calm that West Lake is celebrated for.
Vienna#455479 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe green cathedral is St. Stephen's, the Stephansdom, whose patterned tiled roof and soaring south tower have defined Vienna's skyline since the Middle Ages. Capital of the old Habsburg empire, Vienna gave us Mozart, the waltz, coffeehouse culture, and the world's first true café society, which makes a Starbucks mug here quietly ironic. A grand Gothic silhouette done in classic City Mug green.
Venezia#455480 · City Mug Collector SeriesBlue canals and palazzi for Venice, the city of 118 islands stitched together by some 400 bridges, where the Grand Canal does the work of a main street. The Italian spelling Venezia on a City Mug is a nice authentic touch. With overtourism and acqua alta in the headlines, a mug celebrating Venice's serene waterfront image feels almost like a keepsake of a fragile place.
Cancun#455481 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe purple Mayan statue ties Cancun to the Yucatan's deep Maya heritage, with El Rey ruins inside the resort zone and Chichen Itza and Tulum within reach. Cancun itself is young, a fishing sandbar the Mexican government chose by computer in 1970 to engineer into a megaresort. The contrast of ancient stone and built-from-nothing beach city makes this a fun one.
Scotland#455484 · City Mug Collector SeriesA country rather than a city, marked by the only image that could stand in, a piper in purple working the Great Highland bagpipe. Scotland gave the world tartan, whisky and golf at St Andrews, and the bagpipe is the sound of its clan history and military regiments. I always enjoy the rare national mugs in the series, they break the city-by-city rhythm in a satisfying way.
Merida#455485 · City Mug Collector SeriesMerida, the white city capital of Yucatan, gets blue Mayan ruins, a nod to its role as the modern hub for visiting Chichen Itza and Uxmal in the surrounding jungle. The city itself was founded by the Spanish in 1542 atop the Maya city of Ticho, recycling its limestone into colonial mansions along the Paseo de Montejo. A handsome regional Mexican piece that pairs naturally with the rest of my Yucatan mugs.
Istanbul#455486 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe Turkish evil eye, the nazar boncuk, is the blue-and-white glass amulet that hangs in doorways and on babies across Turkey to ward off ill fortune. Putting it on the Istanbul City Mug Collector Series rather than the Blue Mosque or Hagia Sophia is a wonderfully local touch. Collectors note an early-2000s Made-in-England Istanbul version, so there is variant lore here, and the talisman makes this one of the more charming Turkish pieces.
Kuwait#455487 · City Mug Collector SeriesKuwait's mug shows the blue Kuwait Towers, the trio of slender spires on the Gulf shore completed in 1979, the largest crowned with two great spheres holding a water reservoir and a revolving observation deck. They are the defining symbol of Kuwait City and even appear on the local currency. A clean, recognizable Gulf landmark and a natural companion to the other Middle East City Mug Collector Series pieces.
Playa Del Carmen#455488 · City Mug Collector SeriesPlaya del Carmen sits on Mexico's Riviera Maya, and the orange lighthouse points to its role as the gateway to the island of Cozumel just across the water. Once a sleepy fishing village, it boomed into a Caribbean beach destination anchored by the pedestrian Quinta Avenida. A warm, resort-toned addition that rounds out my Mexican coastal pieces.
Hong Kong#455489 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe pink orchids outside are the Bauhinia blakeana, Hong Kong's official emblem and the flower on its flag and coins, a sterile hybrid first found in the territory in the 1880s. The classic City Mug Collector Series Hong Kong appeared in several years, including a 2002 red-orchid version. A smart choice of motif, since the orchid is a uniquely Hong Kong symbol rather than the obvious harbor skyline everyone else uses.
Greece#455492 · City Mug Collector SeriesRather than a single city, this one takes the whole country, with a big light-blue sailing boat outside echoing Greece's identity as a seafaring nation of thousands of islands. The blue-and-white palette is no accident, it is the exact color scheme of the Greek flag and of the famous Cycladic houses. A simple, elegant country mug from the older flagship line that leans on the Aegean and its sails rather than the Acropolis.
Athens#455494 · City Mug Collector SeriesAthens gives us the cradle of Western democracy and the Acropolis crowning it, with the Parthenon temple to Athena built between 447 and 432 BC. This brown rendering sets the Acropolis above scattered ruins, the exact view that has defined the city for two and a half millennia. A cornerstone subject for any collection, since few City Mugs carry as much weight of history as the birthplace of philosophy and theater.
Egypt#576715 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe Pyramid and Sphinx on this one point straight to the Giza plateau, where the Great Pyramid of Khufu, the only surviving Wonder of the ancient world, has stood for roughly 4,500 years beside the lion-bodied Sphinx. A country mug like this leans on the single most recognizable monument on earth, the sort of universal hook that makes the Egypt piece an easy favorite in any City Mug run.
Qatar#576716 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe purple finjan, more precisely the dallah coffee pot, is a brilliant choice, since the long-spouted dallah is the enduring symbol of Arab hospitality across the Gulf. Qatar even built a giant dallah sculpture on Doha's Corniche. Mine is the standard copyright-era City Mug Collector Series piece, made by Rastal, a clean and very giftable design.
The Sultanate of Oman#576718 · City Mug Collector SeriesOman wears green here, a fitting color for a sultanate known for frankincense trails, the grand Sultan Qaboos Mosque, and the forts that guard Muscat's harbor. The catalog calls the motif Sheberiya, the dhow-and-desert imagery tied to Oman's seafaring and Bedouin heritage. Gulf country mugs like this are a satisfying regional cluster to chase, since Arabian-market pieces did not flood the secondhand market.
Bahrain#576719 · City Mug Collector SeriesBahrain's blue pearls on this mug honor the island's defining trade, pearl diving, which made it the Gulf's pearling capital and accounted for three-quarters of its exports as far back as 1877. The natural pearl beds collapsed only after Japan perfected cultured pearls in the 1930s, and the legacy earned UNESCO recognition via the Muharraq Pearling Path in 2012. To be clear, ours is the standard copyright-2000 City Mug Collector Series piece, not the rumored first version, and the pearl theme makes it one of the more meaningful Gulf mugs.
Lebanon#576721 · City Mug Collector SeriesLebanon's piece is built around the green cedar tree, the Cedrus libani that sits at the dead center of the national flag and has symbolized the country for millennia, prized for its timber as far back as the Phoenicians and the temples of antiquity. Representing the whole nation rather than a single city, it is one of the more elegant emblem-driven mugs in the Middle East run, and a meaningful one given how deeply the cedar is tied to Lebanese identity.
United Arab Emirates#576722 · City Mug Collector SeriesLight orange camels carry the UAE here, a deliberately heritage-leaning image for a country better known today for Dubai's Burj Khalifa and Abu Dhabi's Sheikh Zayed Mosque. The choice of camels over skyscrapers is telling, leaning on Bedouin roots rather than the glass towers. Gulf country mugs travel less than Western city pieces, so they reward patient collectors.
Aguascalientes#576729 · City Mug Collector SeriesAguascalientes means hot waters in Spanish, named for the thermal springs that have drawn bathers to Baños de Ojocaliente since 1831. The purple park and statue on this mug evoke the city's heart, the San Marcos gardens or Plaza de la Patria, where the Baroque cathedral from 1738 still presides. A quieter central-Mexico City Mug that rewards anyone who knows the town beyond its famous April San Marcos fair.
Ciudad Juarez#576730 · City Mug Collector SeriesCiudad Juarez sits right on the Rio Grande across from El Paso, one of the busiest border crossings between Mexico and the United States. The dark blue statue and monuments include the Benito Juarez monument, honoring the reformist president the city is renamed for. A border-city mug that is far less common to find than the big tourist names.
Monterey#576731 · City Mug Collector SeriesMonterey wears a green lady statue, a nod to the old California fishing town that John Steinbeck immortalized in Cannery Row, once the sardine capital of the world. Today its waterfront is anchored by the world-class Monterey Bay Aquarium built right inside a former cannery. The first capital of California under Spanish, Mexican and American rule, it carries far more history than its sleepy size suggests, and this is a pleasant, less common West Coast piece.
Ensenada#576732 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe light purple whale and dolphins celebrate Ensenada's biggest natural draw, the gray whales that migrate past this Baja California port each winter from Alaska's icy seas to the warm lagoons to calve. A cruise stop on the Pacific south of Tijuana, Ensenada is also the gateway to the Valle de Guadalupe wine country and the birthplace of the modern Caesar salad, invented there in the 1920s.
Saltillo#576734 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe pink church is Saltillo's Cathedral of Santiago, an 18th-century Churrigueresque beauty whose tower rises about 81 meters, one of the tallest in northern Mexico. But Saltillo's real claim is the sarape, the finely woven striped blanket considered Mexico's best, a craft brought by Tlaxcaltecan weavers in the late 1500s. Coahuila's capital wears both its faith and its loom with pride.
Puebla#576737 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe light blue church speaks to Puebla, Mexico, a colonial city renowned for its Talavera tile and dozens of ornate baroque churches, its historic center a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Puebla is also where the Battle of Puebla took place on the fifth of May 1862, the origin of Cinco de Mayo. A handsome City Mug that captures the tiled, churchy character of the place.
San Luis Potosi#576738 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe light brown church is the Metropolitan Cathedral of San Luis Potosí, built between 1730 and 1854 with Solomonic columns of spiraling Carrara marble. The colonial silver-mining city's historic center is a UNESCO World Heritage site, part of the Camino Real de Tierra Adentro royal road north into New Spain. Founded on the gold and silver that funded much of Mexico, it earns its grand Baroque face.
Mexico City#576739 · City Mug Collector SeriesMexico City wears the light green Aztec Sun Stone, the famous carved basalt disk often miscalled the Mayan calendar that was unearthed in the Zocalo in 1790 and now anchors the National Museum of Anthropology. The capital is built atop Tenochtitlan, the old Aztec island city, which makes that stone exactly the right emblem. One of the more iconic and instantly readable designs in the whole Latin American City Mug run.
Torreon#576740 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe light green open-armed Jesus is the Cristo de las Noas, perched atop Cerro de las Noas above Torreon in Coahuila. Built between 1973 and 2000, the figure stands nearly 22 meters and is the largest Christ statue in North America, surpassed in Latin America only by Rio's Redeemer and Bolivia's Cristo de la Concordia. A lesser-known Mexican city mug carrying a genuinely monumental landmark.
Puerto Vallarta#576741 · City Mug Collector SeriesLight blue dolphins set the tone for Puerto Vallarta, the Pacific resort town on Mexico's Banderas Bay, whose waters genuinely draw dolphins and wintering humpback whales. The town shot to fame in 1964 when Richard Burton filmed The Night of the Iguana there with Elizabeth Taylor nearby. A breezy, oceanic City Mug that complements my Playa del Carmen and other Mexico pieces.
Leon#576743 · City Mug Collector SeriesLeon in Guanajuato, Mexico, gets its true emblem, the orange Arco de la Calzada, the neoclassical triumphal arch rebuilt in stone in 1896 and crowned in 1943 with a lion sculpture honoring the city's name, lion in Spanish being leon. Leon is Mexico's leather and footwear capital. A specific, well-chosen landmark that rewards anyone who recognizes it, and a less obvious Mexico mug than the Mexico City or Cancun entries.
Acapulco#576744 · City Mug Collector SeriesAcapulco's signature image is right here, a diver plunging off the cliffs of La Quebrada into a narrow inlet barely thirteen feet deep. The tradition began in 1934 when two fishermen dared each other to leap, and Swiss hotelier Teddy Stauffer later turned the boys into stars, cementing Acapulco as a jet-set resort. The 1963 Elvis film Fun in Acapulco carried the divers worldwide, which makes this light blue cliff scene a perfect shorthand for the city.
Cozumel#576745 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe lime-colored fish is exactly right for Cozumel, the Caribbean island off Quintana Roo that sits on the Mesoamerican Reef, the second-largest barrier reef on Earth. Jacques Cousteau helped make Palancar Reef world-famous in the 1960s, and it remains a top scuba and cruise destination. A cheerful diving mug rather than another skyline.
Morelia#576747 · City Mug Collector SeriesMorelia gives me a yellow butterfly beside a church, and both are spot-on. The capital of Michoacan is a UNESCO World Heritage city of pink quarry-stone baroque, crowned by its twin-towered cathedral, and it sits at the doorstep of the monarch butterfly reserves where millions overwinter each year after migrating from Canada. That pairing of architecture and the monarchs makes it one of the more thoughtful Mexican designs in the series.
Bahamas#576748 · City Mug Collector SeriesThis Bahamas country mug shows sailing ships in light blue, a fitting nod to an archipelago of seven hundred islands whose history runs through Columbus's 1492 landfall at San Salvador and a golden age of piracy out of Nassau. The tall ships evoke that seafaring past on waters now famous for their impossibly clear turquoise shallows. A breezy, nautical entry that captures the maritime soul of these Atlantic islands.
Guadalajara#576749 · City Mug Collector SeriesGuadalajara is the capital of Jalisco and the cradle of mariachi and tequila, and the brown church outside nods to its grand cathedral with twin neo-Gothic spires that dominate the historic center. As Mexico's second city it carries deep colonial heritage, and the warm earthy tone suits a place built from cantera stone. A handsome City Mug Collector Series piece that captures the old-world Catholic architecture at the city's heart.
Tijuana#576752 · City Mug Collector SeriesA dark red city skyline for the busy border town just south of San Diego, famous for Avenida Revolucion and being one of the most crossed land borders on earth. This 2007 City Mug came in the larger 20oz format, and while not rare, the Mexican border-city pieces sell steadily to collectors filling out their north-of-Mexico runs. A workmanlike mug with real geographic character.
Brasil#576753 · City Mug Collector SeriesRather than a single city, this one represents the whole country with a tucano, the toucan, that big-billed icon of the Amazon rainforest. Country-level mugs are unusual in a line built on cities, which gives this Brasil piece a distinct character on the shelf. The white-on-white treatment is subtle and easy to overlook, the kind of restrained design collectors come to appreciate once it is in hand.
Tuscany#576756 · City Mug Collector SeriesNot a city but a whole region, Tuscany earns its mug with a stone farmhouse and a single sunflower, shorthand for the rolling hills, cypress rows, and vineyards between Florence and Siena. The region birthed the Renaissance and gave us Chianti, so the sunflower-and-villa imagery is pure idealized countryside. A romantic outlier among the more architecture-driven City Mugs.
Milano#576758 · City Mug Collector SeriesMy Milano mug shows the green cathedral and a statue, that cathedral being the Duomo di Milano, the colossal Gothic marble pile that took roughly six centuries to finish and bristles with thousands of statues and spires. Crowning it is the gilded Madonnina. Milan is Italy's fashion and design capital, so it is fitting the mug leans on its single most overwhelming monument rather than anything on the runway.
Dalian#576759 · City Mug Collector SeriesDalian is the coastal jewel of Liaoning in China's northeast, nicknamed the Hong Kong of Northern China and famous for its squares, fountains, beaches and surviving European and Russian architecture from its colonial past. The light blue buildings on this mug nod to that distinctive cityscape, and locals are so devoted to the game that Dalian earned the title of China's Football City.
Mexicali#576761 · City Mug Collector SeriesMexicali, the Baja California capital sitting right on the US border across from Calexico, gets a purple monument and church here. It is a desert city famous for its Chinese-Mexican fusion cuisine, born of early Cantonese settlers who worked the Colorado River delta, so its Chinatown is unlike anywhere else in Mexico. Border-state Mexican mugs like this tend to be harder to find stateside than the resort cities.
Chile#576762 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe blue melting glacier points to Chilean Patagonia, where the Northern and Southern Ice Fields feed dramatic glaciers like Grey and Perito-region ice in Torres del Paine. Chile is one of the world's longest, thinnest countries, stretching over 4,300 kilometers from the Atacama Desert to Antarctic fjords. A striking country mug with a quietly climate-aware image.
Roma#576763 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe grey Colosseum is the only landmark Rome needed, and it is the right call. Finished around 80 AD under Emperor Titus, the Flavian Amphitheatre held some 50,000 spectators for gladiatorial games and remains the largest amphitheater ever built. I like that the Italian spelling Roma is kept on the mug rather than the anglicized Rome, a small authenticity touch that matters to me.
Italia#576765 · City Mug Collector SeriesItalia takes the whole boot, with a map of Italy and a soccer ball outside, a nod to a country where calcio is close to a religion and the national side has lifted four World Cups. The white-on-white styling is clean and restrained. A neat country-level entry in the City Mug Collector Series that picks football over the predictable Colosseum or Tower of Pisa, which I appreciate for its cheek.
Lima#576766 · City Mug Collector SeriesLima, the Peruvian capital founded by Pizarro in 1535 and once the seat of all Spanish South America, is represented by a red church, its colonial-era Cathedral of Lima or the famous yellow-and-ochre Iglesia de San Francisco on the Plaza Mayor. The historic center is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. A handsome South America entry that captures Lima's deep Spanish colonial bones rather than its modern coastline.
Firenze#576768 · City Mug Collector SeriesFirenze is Florence in Italian, the cradle of the Renaissance, and the grey skyline is crowned by Brunelleschi's terracotta Duomo dome, an engineering marvel completed in 1436 that still defines the city. The statue is Michelangelo's David, carved 1501 to 1504, whose original lives in the Accademia while a copy stands in the Piazza della Signoria where the marble once stood.
Wuxi#576769 · City Mug Collector SeriesWuxi sits on Lake Taihu in Jiangsu, and the green roaring turtle is Yuantouzhu, or Turtle Head Isle, the peninsula whose rocks jut into the lake like a swimming turtle tossing its head. The park, established in 1916, is also one of the world's great cherry-blossom spots, with tens of thousands of trees, so this mug captures a genuinely specific local icon rather than a generic motif.
Shenzhen#576770 · City Mug Collector SeriesThere is a lovely irony to a red temple on the Shenzhen mug, since Shenzhen is China's youngest megacity, a fishing village turned Special Economic Zone after 1980 and now a tech giant facing Hong Kong. The temple references one of the surviving older sites near the border, a reminder of what predated the skyscrapers. I keep this one for the story it tells, a City Mug honoring a place that essentially had no city to memorialize a generation earlier.
Foshan#576771 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe grey gate is the Foshan Ancestral Temple, or Zu Miao, a Daoist temple in Guangdong founded in the Northern Song dynasty and rich with Lingnan wood and stone carvings, ceramic figures and iron castings dating back over 600 years. Foshan is also the home of Cantonese kung fu legends, the birthplace of Wong Fei-hung and the martial home of Ip Man, Bruce Lee's teacher.
Shanghai#576772 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe red Bund on mine is the real thing, Shanghai's historic waterfront where the Huangpu River fronts a wall of 1920s and 30s European banking palaces, the most famous colonial-era skyline in Asia. China City Mugs were sold heavily in domestic stores, so Shanghai is common, but it remains a cornerstone piece because almost every collector starts a China run here. I love how the deep red ink turns those staid old trading houses into something almost cinematic.
Manila#576774 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe grey figure on my Manila mug is the Rizal Monument, the marble and bronze memorial in Luneta Park honoring national hero Dr. Jose Rizal, executed in 1896, with his remains actually interred at its base and guarded around the clock. The monument's Latin motto Stella means guiding star. A clean, dignified pick for the Philippine capital, and the same hero anchors the later Relief and Been There Manila pieces too.
Qingdao#576775 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe light brown Chinese temple points to Qingdao, the breezy coastal city in Shandong famous for its German colonial old town and, above all, Tsingtao beer, the brewery founded by German settlers in 1903. Its Zhanqiao Pier and red-roofed European architecture make it unmistakable. A lovely China City Mug that hints at the city's unusual East-meets-Bavaria heritage.
Wuhan#576776 · City Mug Collector SeriesWuhan straddles the Yangtze in central China, and the pagoda with a bird depicts the Yellow Crane Tower, the legendary riverside pavilion immortalized in classical Tang poetry by Li Bai and Cui Hao. The crane is the whole point, since legend says an immortal flew off from the tower on a yellow crane, so this design is leaning on poetry, not just a skyline.
Cebu#576777 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe guitars are spot on. Cebu, specifically Opon on Mactan Island, is the Philippines' guitar-making heartland, a craft seeded by Spanish friars and carried on by families like the Alegres for generations. The instruments are hand-built from jackfruit, narra, and ebony and exported worldwide for their sweet, mellow tone. One of the more delightfully local City Mugs in the line.
Surabaya#576778 · City Mug Collector SeriesThis older Surabaya City Mug shows the Suro and Boyo, the shark and crocodile locked in combat that form the city's emblem and the folk etymology of its name, sura for courage and baya for danger. The legend says the two beasts fought over territory, sea against land, and the city statue immortalizes the brawl. I find this one of the most striking City Mug designs anywhere, a violent local myth rendered as civic pride.
Singapore#576780 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe green Merlion is Singapore's official mascot, a lion's head on a fish's body designed in 1964, the lion for the Sanskrit name Singapura and the fish for its origins as a humble sea port. This is the older City Mug version, before the You Are Here and Bearista Merlions that the Singapore stores leaned into. I like the restraint here, a single emblematic creature instead of the usual landmark pile-up, which makes it instantly readable on the shelf.
Taiwan#576782 · City Mug Collector SeriesWhere the Taipei mug zooms in, this one pulls back to the whole sweet-potato-shaped island, rendered as a light green map of Taiwan. The country-level City Mugs are a quieter sub-thread of the line, and the green-on-white map style is a recognizable Starbucks treatment for whole nations. I like owning the macro and the micro of the same place side by side.
Suzhou#576784 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe purple Chinese courtyard on mine is exactly right for Suzhou, the canal city near Shanghai famous for its classical scholar gardens, nine of which are UNESCO World Heritage sites, and often called the Venice of the East. Those whitewashed walls, moon gates, and koi ponds are the soul of the place. I love that the mug skips a skyline entirely for a garden, honoring a city whose genius was always intimacy and water rather than height.
Xian#576785 · City Mug Collector SeriesXian was the ancient capital of China and eastern terminus of the Silk Road, and the grey soldiers are unmistakably the Terracotta Army, the thousands of life-size clay warriors buried with the first emperor Qin Shi Huang around 210 BC and rediscovered by well-diggers in 1974. Few city mugs get to feature one of the greatest archaeological finds in history, which makes this an easy favorite to display.
Bangkok#576786 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe two guardian statues on this Bangkok mug are the yaksha demon giants who stand watch at Wat Phra Kaew, the temple of the Emerald Buddha inside the Grand Palace. These towering, fanged tutelary figures are one of the most photographed sights in Thailand. A clean older Bangkok Collector Series piece is a solid Southeast Asia anchor that collectors are always happy to slot in.
Hobart#576787 · City Mug Collector SeriesHobart is the capital of Tasmania and Australia's second-oldest city, a deepwater port that the blue ships-in-port design captures perfectly. It is the gateway to the Antarctic, the home harbor for research vessels heading south and the finish line of the legendary Sydney to Hobart yacht race every December. A handsome maritime City Mug Collector Series piece from one of the more far-flung corners of the line.
Nanjing#576788 · City Mug Collector SeriesNanjing, the former imperial capital whose name literally means southern capital, gets orange steps leading to a temple, the grand stairway up Purple Mountain to Dr. Sun Yat-sen's Mausoleum, a 392-step climb that is the city's defining pilgrimage. Nanjing served as capital for six dynasties and briefly for the Republic of China. A solid second-tier Chinese city piece beyond the usual Beijing and Shanghai.
Ningbo#576789 · City Mug Collector SeriesNingbo is an ancient port city in Zhejiang province, and the turquoise pagoda rooftop nods to its deep history. The city is home to Tianyi Ge, founded in 1561 by Fan Qin, which is the oldest surviving private library in China and one of the oldest in the world. A genuinely undersung Chinese City Mug that collectors do not chase as hard as Shanghai or Beijing.
Shenyang#576790 · City Mug Collector SeriesShenyang anchors China's old northeast, the Manchu capital before the Qing took Beijing, home to the Mukden Palace, a smaller cousin of the Forbidden City. The catalog notes a skyline with two wooden sticks, which read to me as chopsticks, a sly nod to the city's hearty Dongbei food culture. Less-traveled China mugs like this one are harder to find outside the country, which makes Shenyang a satisfying deep cut for a serious China shelf.
Chongqing#576791 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe red pagoda evokes Chongqing's striking riverside temples, most famously the red Shibaozhai pavilion built against a cliff above the Yangtze. This mountainous megacity at the meeting of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers is a starting point for Three Gorges cruises and is famous for searingly spicy hotpot. A bold mug for one of the largest urban areas on the planet.
Hawaii#576792 · City Mug Collector SeriesHawaii gets the whole island chain rather than one city, and the light-blue men rowing a boat outside depict an outrigger canoe, the va'a that is central to Polynesian and native Hawaiian seafaring tradition. Outrigger paddling remains a serious competitive sport across the islands. A breezy City Mug Collector Series piece that reaches past the obvious palm-and-surf cliche to honor the deeper Pacific voyaging culture.
Jakarta#576793 · City Mug Collector SeriesJakarta is Indonesia's sprawling capital, and the light-blue statue of a couple holding flowers is the Selamat Datang (Welcome) Monument, the bronze pair raised in 1962 for the Asian Games who still wave above the Hotel Indonesia roundabout. It was commissioned by President Sukarno as a greeting to arriving athletes and guests. A warm, friendly City Mug Collector Series choice that puts the city's literal welcome gesture front and center.
Seoul#576794 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe light purple pagoda on mine nods to Seoul's royal palaces, Gyeongbokgung or its Gwanghwamun gate, the seat of the Joseon dynasty from 1395. I love that this older City Mug line keeps the design quiet and architectural rather than loud, a white interior letting that single tiered roof carry the whole city. Korea mugs from this series turn up steadily on the secondary market but the early Seoul stays a clean, well-priced way into the line.
DongGuan#576795 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe bridge in grey-green is Dongguan's Humen Bridge, completed in 1997 as the first large suspension bridge China designed and built entirely on its own, with a main span of 888 meters that was the country's longest at the time. Dongguan sits in the Pearl River Delta manufacturing belt of Guangdong, and this span over the river estuary is its proudest landmark.
Gold Coast#576796 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe Gold Coast is Australia's surf capital, a strip of Queensland coastline where the white inside gives way to a surfer riding a wave above the high-rise skyline of Surfers Paradise. This is the classic flagship City Mug Collector Series, and the lone-surfer-over-towers motif nails exactly what the place sells itself on, golden beaches backed by a wall of glass apartment blocks. A clean, instantly readable design that I love for how literally it pictures the city's name.
Baguio#576797 · City Mug Collector SeriesBaguio is the summer capital of the Philippines, a cool mountain city in the Cordilleras famous for its flowers, which is exactly what this light blue mug shows. The blooms tie to the Panagbenga Festival, a month-long flower celebration launched in 1995 to help the city heal after the devastating 1990 Luzon earthquake. A gentle, pretty City Mug from a hill town built by Americans as a highland retreat from the tropical heat.
Tagaytay#576798 · City Mug Collector SeriesTagaytay is the Philippines' breezy ridge town overlooking Taal, one of the world's smallest active volcanoes sitting in a lake inside a larger caldera, and the light green mountains over river on mine capture exactly that famous view. It is a beloved cool-weather escape from Manila's heat. Philippine City Mugs are popular and Tagaytay stands out for picturing a natural wonder, the rare City Mug whose star is a volcano rather than a building.
Kuala Lumpur#576799 · City Mug Collector SeriesKuala Lumpur's mug puts the unmistakable Petronas Towers in light blue, the twin 88-story skyscrapers that were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004 and remain the tallest twin towers ever built. Their Islamic-geometry floor plan and the sky bridge linking the two are instantly recognizable. Malaysia's capital is a strong Southeast Asia entry, and the Petronas silhouette makes this an easy, satisfying skyline piece to spot.
Bali#576800 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe light green art on this City Mug Collector Series piece is the Barong, the lion-like mask spirit who battles the witch Rangda in Bali's most sacred dance-drama, a symbol of good against evil. I love that Starbucks reached past the obvious beaches and rice terraces for a piece of living ritual. Indonesian mugs like this trade steadily among collectors who chase the full archipelago set.
Sabah#576801 · City Mug Collector SeriesSabah is the Malaysian state on the northern tip of Borneo, and the light brown monkey here points to its wildlife fame, home to the Bornean orangutan rehabilitated at Sepilok and the big-nosed proboscis monkey found nowhere else. Crowning it all is Mount Kinabalu, Southeast Asia's highest peak at 4,095 meters. Collectors note the Sabah icon mug runs on the harder-to-find side, a nice quiet score.
Macau#576802 · City Mug Collector SeriesMacau's mug shows a blue cathedral that can only be the Ruins of St. Paul's, the towering stone facade of the 17th-century Jesuit church of Mater Dei, all that survived an 1835 fire and now the defining icon of this former Portuguese colony. Macau blends that Catholic heritage with its identity as the gambling capital of the world. Part of the historic center inscribed by UNESCO, it makes for one of the most evocative East Asian pieces in the series.
Chengdu#576803 · City Mug Collector SeriesA panda munching bamboo is exactly right for Chengdu, home of the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding and the gateway to Sichuan's panda reserves. The Sichuan capital is also famed for tongue-numbing mapo tofu and hotpot, plus laid-back teahouse culture. A genuinely charming mug, and pandas tend to be among the more popular China-series designs with collectors.
Taipei#576804 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe magenta pagoda on this Taipei mug nods to the city's temple and tower silhouette, the genre that culminates in Taipei 101, which held the world's tallest building title from 2004 to 2010. Taiwan's night markets, bubble tea birthplace, and the National Palace Museum's imperial treasures all live in this one city. A clean older City Mug Collector Series piece that I am glad sits beside its Taiwan country mate.
New Zealand#576805 · City Mug Collector SeriesThis one stands in for a whole country rather than a city, and the kiwi on the outside is the perfect shorthand. The flightless bird is so beloved that New Zealanders call themselves Kiwis, and it is a national emblem and a protected taonga. A clean, white-lined City Mug Collector Series piece that I am always happy to find with crisp printing.
Guangzhou#576807 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe orange statue with horns is the Five Rams (Five Goats), Guangzhou's beloved granite emblem erected in 1959 in Yuexiu Park. The legend says five celestial beings rode goats bearing rice stalks into the city and promised it would never know famine, which is why locals call Guangzhou the City of Rams. A great City Mug Collector Series piece, because the imagery is pure local folklore rather than a generic skyline.
Adelaide#576808 · City Mug Collector SeriesAdelaide is South Australia's elegant capital and the gateway to the Barossa Valley, one of the world's oldest and most prestigious wine regions just to its northeast. The pink barrels on this mug nod straight to that heritage, where wineries like Seppeltsfield hold an unbroken line of single-vintage tawnies dating back to 1878. Paired with the city skyline, it captures a planned colonial city that has always poured its identity into the glass.
Waikiki#576809 · City Mug Collector SeriesBlue shoreline for Waikiki, the legendary Honolulu beach beneath Diamond Head crater where Duke Kahanamoku helped carry surfing to the world. The neighborhood is the engine of Hawaii tourism, all high-rise hotels fronting that famous curve of sand. A breezy, color-forward City Mug that stands apart from the architecture-heavy entries in the series.
Maui#576810 · City Mug Collector SeriesMaui gets a blue surfer, fitting for the Valley Isle, where Jaws at Peahi draws big-wave riders and the Road to Hana and Haleakala's sunrise crater define the island. I appreciate that Starbucks went with surf culture rather than a generic palm tree. As a US destination piece this one turns up reasonably often, which makes it an easy and affordable entry in any City Mug run.
Kauai#576811 · City Mug Collector SeriesKauai is Hawaii's oldest main island, nicknamed the Garden Isle for its drenched green ridges, and this mug leans into exactly that with a light green shoreline and palm trees wrapping the body. The island's Na Pali coast and Waimea Canyon, the so-called Grand Canyon of the Pacific, are its real draws. Hawaii city mugs are perennial favorites among collectors since the islands punch above their weight in Starbucks output, and Kauai is less common than the Honolulu and Maui pieces.
Canberra#576812 · City Mug Collector SeriesCanberra is a rarity, a purpose-built capital chosen as a compromise between rival Sydney and Melbourne and laid out by American architect Walter Burley Griffin after a 1912 design competition. The grey building is Parliament House on Capital Hill, famously built into the hill with a grassy roof you can walk on. A planned-city mug for one of the few cities designed from scratch.
Taichung#576813 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe blue statue on this Taichung mug points to the city's Buddhist heritage, the great Maitreya or one of the temple figures Taiwan's cultural capital is known for, in a city also famous as the birthplace of bubble tea in the 1980s. Taiwan City Mugs are a tidy collecting subset, and Taichung rounds out a run alongside Taipei and Kaohsiung. I like the cool blue palette here, calmer than the usual warm city tones.
Bogor#576814 · City Mug Collector SeriesBogor, just south of Jakarta, is the rainy hill town built around the world-famous Kebun Raya botanical gardens, so the grey flower on this Collector Series mug fits perfectly, a nod to the corpse flower or the gardens' orchids. The Dutch called it Buitenzorg, without a care. This is the older single-city Bogor, the counterpart to the 2011 dancer version below.
Brisbane#576815 · City Mug Collector SeriesBrisbane is the subtropical Queensland capital wrapped around a looping river, so the light brown city bridges fit, the 1940 Story Bridge, Australia's longest cantilever span. The Brisbane River's hairpin bends mean bridges genuinely define the skyline here. Australian Collector Series mugs are a tidier, less-crowded subset, which makes a sharp Brisbane a pleasant addition rather than a grind to find.
Melbourne#576816 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe Cable Car 35 on my Melbourne mug is its beloved City Circle tram, the free heritage W-class trams that loop the central business district in burgundy and gold. Melbourne runs the largest urban tram network in the world, so the streetcar is the perfect shorthand for the city. A smart, specific design choice that any Aussie collector recognizes instantly over the usual Flinders Street or skyline cliche.
Wellington#576817 · City Mug Collector SeriesWellington is New Zealand's compact, hilly capital, and the skyline on this mug rightly centers on the Beehive, the round, tiered Executive Wing of the Parliament Buildings designed by British architect Basil Spence and completed in 1979. It is one of the most recognizable government buildings in the Southern Hemisphere, and putting it on a City Mug instead of a generic harbor view tells me the design team did their homework on what locals actually point to.
Invercargill#576819 · City Mug Collector SeriesInvercargill is the southernmost city in New Zealand and was long home to the southernmost Starbucks in the world, which is exactly why this skyline mug is so coveted. Collectors flag the 2005 edition as very hard to find, a true VHTF piece that surfaces only occasionally on the secondary market. A genuine trophy of the City Mug Collector Series, prized less for its design than for marking the literal end-of-the-earth outpost of the company.
Yogyakarta#576820 · City Mug Collector SeriesYogyakarta is the cultural heart of Java and the gateway to Borobudur, the colossal 9th-century Buddhist temple, so the bell-shaped architecture here is the temple's distinctive perforated stupas that crown the monument. Borobudur is the largest Buddhist temple in the world and a UNESCO site, and a mug that distills it down to that one iconic bell silhouette is the design team showing restraint and good taste.
Medan#576821 · City Mug Collector SeriesMedan, the bustling gateway city of North Sumatra, gets an orange equestrian statue here, the kind of civic monument that anchors an Indonesian city square. This is the standard International style Medan, distinct from the dancer version below. Medan is known as the jumping-off point for Lake Toba, the giant volcanic crater lake, so any Sumatran piece is a slightly off-the-beaten-path catch for a collection.
Christchurch#576823 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe cathedral and tram capture old Christchurch perfectly. The Gothic Revival ChristChurch Cathedral lost its spire in the devastating February 2011 earthquake that killed 185 people, and is only now being reinstated. The heritage tram still loops the city center. That makes this mug a small time capsule of the Garden City before the quake.
Kona#576824 · City Mug Collector SeriesKona on Hawaii's Big Island is hallowed ground for anyone who loves coffee, so the light brown coffee beans circling this mug are perfectly on theme, this is one of the few places on US soil where coffee is commercially grown. Kona's volcanic slopes and ideal climate produce one of the world's priciest beans, and Starbucks itself sells a 100 percent Kona roast. These run roughly 10 to 25 dollars used, and a coffee-bean design on a coffee mug makes it a fun thematic grab.
Sydney#576828 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe light brown design pairs Sydney's two icons, Jorn Utzon's sail-shelled Opera House, a 1973 UNESCO masterpiece, and the 1932 steel arch of the Harbour Bridge that locals call the Coathanger. Together they are the most recognizable harbor in the world. Australian City Mugs are a steady favorite, and Sydney is the keystone, the one piece nearly every Oceania collector wants before chasing Melbourne or the rest.
Queenstown#576829 · City Mug Collector SeriesQueenstown bills itself as the adventure capital of the world, and the bungee jumper on the front is no accident. The modern commercial bungee was born here in 1988 when AJ Hackett opened the Kawarau Bridge jump, the first of its kind anywhere. The light blue scene wraps lake and mountain around the leaper, a fitting souvenir from the town that turned a Vanuatu vine-jumping ritual into a global industry.
Auckland#576830 · City Mug Collector SeriesAuckland is New Zealand's largest city, a sprawl of harbors and extinct volcanoes nicknamed the City of Sails for having more boats per capita than almost anywhere. The light purple skyline and bridge on this mug point to the Sky Tower, the Southern Hemisphere's tallest free-standing structure, and the Auckland Harbour Bridge spanning the Waitematā. A scenic Pacific entry that captures a city wrapped on every side by water.
Bandung#576831 · City Mug Collector SeriesBandung is the cool, highland capital of West Java, famous for Dutch colonial Art Deco architecture, which is surely the light grey building on this Collector Series mug. The city was the Paris of Java in the 1920s and hosted the 1955 Asian-African Conference. This is the older single-city design, distinct from the 2011 dancer version, a useful split to know when you are completing the Indonesia shelf.
Cologne#576833 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe brown bridges span the Rhine, but Cologne's true icon is its twin-spired Gothic Cathedral, begun in 1248 and not finished until 1880, which survived WWII bombing that flattened much of the old city around it. The Hohenzollern Bridge beside it now groans under hundreds of thousands of lovers' padlocks. A handsome mug for one of Germany's oldest cities.
Stuttgart#576836 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe brown architecture on this Stuttgart mug captures the Swabian capital, home of Mercedes-Benz and Porsche and cradle of the modern automobile, where Gottlieb Daimler built his first engine. The design features the city's landmarks like the Schlossplatz palaces or the rocket-like 1956 television tower, the world's first concrete TV tower. German City Mugs sold widely at home but are less common abroad, making Stuttgart a clean, characterful addition to a Europe shelf.
Rotorua#576837 · City Mug Collector SeriesRotorua sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire and smells of it, the sulphur steam earning it the nickname Sulphur City. The light green thermal landscape on this mug captures the geysers, mud pools and silica terraces that draw visitors, plus it is the heartland of Te Arawa Maori culture. Pohutu, the geyser at Te Puia, can erupt over 20 times a day to heights above 30 meters.
Patra#576839 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe grey-blue bridge is the Rio-Antirrio, officially the Charilaos Trikoupis Bridge, one of the world's longest multi-span cable-stayed bridges, opened in 2004 to span the Gulf of Corinth near Patras. Patra is Greece's third-largest city and famous for its enormous pre-Lenten Carnival. A nice, less-common Greek entry that I value for choosing an engineering marvel over the usual ancient ruins.
Brussels#576840 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe light brown city square is the Grand-Place, Brussels's UNESCO-listed central square ringed by ornate guildhalls and the Gothic Town Hall, which Victor Hugo called the most beautiful square in Europe. It is the heart of the Belgian capital and the EU. A Grand-Place mug is one of those pieces where the chosen landmark is unimpeachable, and Brussels rounds out the Low Countries nicely on the shelf.
Kocaeli#576841 · City Mug Collector SeriesKocaeli, whose seat is the port city of Izmit on the Sea of Marmara, gets its true landmark here, the neoclassical Izmit Clock Tower built in 1901 to mark the 25th anniversary of Sultan Abdulhamid II's accession. The light blue skyline framing that clock tower is the giveaway. As the ancient Nicomedia and a heavy Turkish industrial hub, Kocaeli is an unusually specific pick, which makes it a quieter, more interesting Turkey mug than the obvious Istanbul.
Antalya#576843 · City Mug Collector SeriesAntalya is the jewel of Turkey's Mediterranean coast, where Roman ruins meet turquoise water along the so-called Turkish Riviera. The light blue skyline with ruins on this mug captures that blend, Hadrian's Gate from 130 AD or the old Kaleiçi harbor district below the fluted Yivli Minaret. A handsome City Mug from a sun-soaked resort city that locals and Europeans flock to every summer.
Queensland#576844 · City Mug Collector SeriesQueensland is the only place on earth where you can fly to the Great Barrier Reef for breakfast and the rainforest for lunch, so the blue reef diver on this mug is exactly right. The reef is the largest living structure on the planet, visible from space, and Queensland's coast is its launching point. A clean, single-image City Mug, restrained the way I like the older line to be.
Crete#576849 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe brown Greek ruins surely nod to Knossos, the labyrinthine Bronze Age palace of the Minoans, Europe's oldest known civilization, tied to the legend of the Minotaur and controversially restored by Arthur Evans. Crete is the largest Greek island and the birthplace of the painter El Greco. A satisfyingly ancient mug for the Greece run.
Australia#576850 · City Mug Collector SeriesA country mug that leans straight into the cuddliest icon Australia has, a purple koala, the marsupial found nowhere else on earth that survives almost entirely on eucalyptus leaves. Sometimes wrongly called a bear, the koala became a global emblem of Australian wildlife, which makes it a warmer, friendlier choice than the usual Opera House or Uluru. An easy crowd-pleaser among the country-level City Mugs.
Mykonos#576857 · City Mug Collector SeriesMykonos earns a light blue windmill, the Kato Mili row of whitewashed 16th-century windmills above the harbor that are the Cycladic island's signature image, built by Venetians to grind grain for passing ships. The island is famous for its labyrinthine Chora and Little Venice waterfront. Greek island mugs are popular crossover pieces, and Mykonos exists in both this Collector style and a later You Are Here version for set-builders.
Rhodes#576858 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe light brown castle towers on this mug are the Palace of the Grand Master, the medieval fortress the Knights Hospitaller raised on Rhodes after 1309. The whole walled Old Town is a UNESCO site and one of the best-preserved medieval cities in Europe. Rhodes also once hosted the Colossus, a vanished Wonder of the Ancient World, so the island has been minting iconic landmarks for over two thousand years.
Cyprus#576859 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe olive branch in light green on this one is no accident, Cyprus is one of the oldest wine and olive cultures in the Mediterranean and the olive tree is woven through its identity. Mythology places the birth of Aphrodite at Petra tou Romiou on the island's southwest coast, so a Cyprus mug carries goddess lore along with the copper that gave the island its very name.
Ankara#576860 · City Mug Collector SeriesAnkara became Turkey's capital in 1923 under Atatürk, replacing Istanbul, and its defining monument is Anıtkabir, the founder's imposing mausoleum completed in 1953 with its lion-lined ceremonial road. The light brown map and tower on this mug fit a capital better known for statecraft than tourism, with the modern Atakule observation tower a second city landmark. A worthy Turkish entry that captures a purpose-built seat of government.
Izmir#576861 · City Mug Collector SeriesIzmir is Turkey's third city and main Aegean port, and the light-green clock tower is the Saat Kulesi in Konak Square, an ornate Ottoman tower from 1901 that is the undisputed symbol of the city. Often shown framed by palms with sea waves and gulls, it captures Izmir's breezy seaside character. A lesser-seen Turkish City Mug Collector Series piece that collectors call somewhat hard to find.
Thessaloniki#576862 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe light brown fort on this mug is the White Tower of Thessaloniki, the city's most iconic monument, a cylindrical Ottoman bastion built after 1430 that once earned grim names like the Blood Tower when it served as a prison. A convict whitewashed it in 1883 in exchange for his freedom, giving it the name it carries today. Greece's second city, beautifully reduced to its single defining shape.
Aydin#576863 · City Mug Collector SeriesAydın in western Turkey holds Aphrodisias, one of the best-preserved ancient cities anywhere, a marble town dedicated to Aphrodite that grew rich on its quarries and renowned school of sculptors. The ruin steps and statue face on this mug fit perfectly, as the site earned UNESCO World Heritage status in 2017 and rivals Ephesus without the crowds. A deep-cut Turkish City Mug for collectors who appreciate a genuinely off-the-beaten-path subject.
Warsaw#576864 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe red lady with sword and shield is the Syrenka, the Mermaid of Warsaw and the city's official symbol for some five centuries. Legend has her swimming up the Vistula and pledging to defend the city, which is why she is armed rather than serene, with her most famous statue standing in the Old Town Market Square. A great mug because the imagery rewards anyone who knows the myth.
Bursa#576865 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe cable car here is the Bursa Uludag Teleferik, which climbs Mount Uludag and at 8.8 kilometers ranks among the longest gondola lines in the world. The little dolls nod to Bursa's Karagoz shadow-puppet tradition, said to have originated in this old Ottoman capital. A nicely specific mug for Turkey's first capital and silk-road center.
Corfu#576866 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe dark blue shoreline fits Corfu, the lush Ionian island whose Venetian-built Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site crowned by two seaside fortresses. Less arid than the Aegean isles, it was a long-favored retreat of European royalty and the boyhood home of writer Gerald Durrell. A breezy island mug for the Greece series.
Lisboa#576867 · City Mug Collector SeriesLisboa, Lisbon to most of us, shows a blue fort that is surely the Belem Tower, the early-16th-century Manueline fortress on the Tagus that launched and guarded Portugal's Age of Discovery voyages and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Using the Portuguese spelling Lisboa is a nice authentic touch. One of the more storied landmarks in the European run, tied directly to the era of Vasco da Gama and global exploration.
Amsterdam#576870 · City Mug Collector SeriesAmsterdam is built on a ring of seventeenth-century canals, a UNESCO-listed Golden Age engineering feat that gives the city more bridges than Venice and over a hundred kilometers of waterway. This older flagship City Mug renders those gabled merchant houses leaning over the canal in light blue, the exact postcard view from a bridge in the Jordaan. A timeless subject and one of the more universally recognized cities in the whole series.
Berlin#576871 · City Mug Collector SeriesThis Berlin mug pairs the Reichstag, the 1894 parliament crowned with Norman Foster's glass dome since 1999, with an angel that is the Goldelse atop the Victory Column in the Tiergarten. Two icons of German democracy and history on one cup. Berlin is one of the more available German Collector Series mugs, which makes it an easy, handsome cornerstone for the Germany shelf rather than a chase piece.
Lyon#576872 · City Mug Collector SeriesLyon's brown design of a horseman gazing toward a castle evokes the city's Renaissance and royal heritage, France's historic capital of silk and gastronomy where the Saone meets the Rhone. The scene nods to the Fourviere hill and its basilica overlooking Vieux Lyon, a UNESCO World Heritage old town. A more painterly, narrative design than the typical skyline, which gives this French entry an unusually classical, storybook feel.
Zurich#576873 · City Mug Collector SeriesZurich is Switzerland's banking and lake city, and the green man over a horse statue is the equestrian monument of Hans Waldmann, the 15th-century mayor and military leader, which stands by the Fraumunster church on the Limmat. The Fraumunster is itself famous for its Marc Chagall stained-glass windows, so this riverside corner packs more history than a quick glance at the mug suggests.
Madrid#576875 · City Mug Collector SeriesMy Madrid mug carries a green building rendered in the classic City Mug Collector style, white inside, the city's emblem outside. Spain's capital is the country's geographic bullseye, home to the Royal Palace, the Prado, and the grand Plaza Mayor. I like that this older flagship line kept things to a single bold motif rather than the busy landmark bands the later Global Icon series leaned into.
Paris#576876 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe red Eiffel Tower needs no introduction, Gustave Eiffel's 1889 iron tower built for the World's Fair and nearly torn down before radio saved it. There are many Paris Starbucks mugs across the years, so the older City Mug Collector Series version with the simple red tower has a real vintage charm. A cornerstone city that no serious collection should be without.
Prague#576877 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe red bridge over the river is the Charles Bridge, begun in 1357 under Charles IV and lined with thirty baroque statues, crossing the Vltava in the heart of Prague. The Czech capital is one of Europe's best-preserved medieval cities, its castle the largest ancient castle complex in the world. A gorgeous City Mug for one of the most photogenic skylines anywhere.
Cluj Napoca#576878 · City Mug Collector SeriesCluj-Napoca is the unofficial capital of Transylvania, a lively Romanian university city whose street scene of pastel buildings and cars suits this design. Its centerpiece is St. Michael's Church, a soaring Gothic landmark on the main square. A nice pull for collectors chasing Romania's secondary cities rather than just Bucharest.
Lausanne#576879 · City Mug Collector SeriesLausanne on Lake Geneva is best known as the Olympic Capital, permanent home of the International Olympic Committee since 1915 and of the Olympic Museum. The red city skyline on this mug would feature its Gothic cathedral, Notre-Dame de Lausanne, one of Switzerland's finest. Swiss city mugs tend to be sought after by European collectors, and Lausanne is a less common pick than Zurich or Geneva, making it a nice catch.
Valencia#576880 · City Mug Collector SeriesBlue architecture for Spain's third city, Santiago Calatrava's futuristic City of Arts and Sciences, the white sculptural complex that redefined Valencia's image. The city is also the birthplace of paella and home to the riotous Las Fallas festival. The blue-on-white architectural treatment is the City Mug line at its most elegant.
Wroclaw#576882 · City Mug Collector SeriesWroclaw, in Polish Silesia, is one of Europe's great market-square cities, and the dark red buildings here evoke the candy-colored merchant townhouses ringing the Rynek and the soaring brick Gothic of the Old Town Hall. The city is also beloved for its hundreds of tiny bronze dwarf statues hidden in the streets, a whimsical detail that makes a Wroclaw mug feel like a little treasure hunt.
Copenhagen#576884 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe skyline and boats evoke Nyhavn, the postcard canal lined with gabled merchant houses where Hans Christian Andersen once lived. Copenhagen is also home to the Little Mermaid statue and ranks among the world's most bike-friendly and livable capitals. A clean, very Scandinavian City Mug for the Danish capital.
Basel#576885 · City Mug Collector SeriesBasel sits in the corner where Switzerland, France, and Germany meet, and this green skyline-from-the-river view captures its Rhine waterfront, the red sandstone Munster cathedral towers above the old town. It is Switzerland's cultural capital, home to Art Basel and a famous Carnival. Swiss city mugs run small in number, so a river-view Basel is a quietly rewarding find.
Germany#576886 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe grey gate is the Brandenburg Gate, Berlin's neoclassical 1791 arch topped by the Quadriga chariot, which stood marooned in the death strip beside the Berlin Wall and became the emblem of German reunification in 1989. Picking this single monument for the whole-country mug is fitting, since no structure better tells the story of Germany's division and its joining back together.
Bonn#576887 · City Mug Collector SeriesBonn was West Germany's modest provisional capital from 1949 to 1990, and the dark purple building is its Romanesque Munster or the old Town Hall. It is also Beethoven's birthplace, which is the city's real claim to fame. Bonn is one of the scarcer German cities in the Collector Series since it lost national prominence after reunification, a nice underdog pickup for the Germany set.
Moscow#576888 · City Mug Collector SeriesMoscow comes rendered in brown with Red Square, the historic heart fronting the Kremlin, with St. Basil's onion domes and Lenin's Mausoleum lining its edges. The square's name comes from the old Russian krasnaya, meaning beautiful as much as red, predating any Soviet association. A cornerstone capital piece, and the muted brown palette gives it an older, almost sepia feel that I like in the early Collector Series.
Hamburg#576889 · City Mug Collector SeriesHamburg is Germany's largest port and second city, and the grey buildings over a bridge outside fit a place laced with more bridges than Venice and Amsterdam combined. The classic City Mug Collector Series Hamburg was made by Rastal in Germany, with known variants including a China-made version and Germany-marked versions, so collectors do hunt for the backstamp. A restrained, architectural piece that suits Hamburg's brick-warehouse Speicherstadt mood.
Malaysia#576890 · City Mug Collector SeriesThis is the Malaysia entry, and the red kris on the outside is the giveaway, the wavy double-edged dagger that is a genuine national symbol woven into Malay heraldry and even the coats of arms of several states. It is a country mug rather than a single city, which the older Collector Series did for places where Starbucks wanted one piece to stand for the whole nation. A nice symbolic choice over the obvious Petronas Towers.
Wiesbade#576891 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe name is clipped on the catalog but this is Wiesbaden, the elegant spa city and capital of Hesse, long famous for its hot springs and Belle Epoque grandeur. The light grey building is almost surely the Kurhaus, the columned 1907 spa and casino hall where Dostoevsky once gambled, a fact I love because it ties a coffee mug to a literary legend's roulette habit.
Aachen#576892 · City Mug Collector SeriesAachen sits on Germany's western border and is forever tied to Charlemagne, who made it his imperial seat and was buried in Aachen Cathedral in 814. The statue holding a cross on this mug points to that legacy, as the cathedral became Germany's first UNESCO World Heritage site in 1978 and crowned thirty-one German kings between 936 and 1531. A satisfying old City Mug from a town most travelers overlook despite its outsized history.
Bucharest#576893 · City Mug Collector SeriesBucharest's grey building on this mug is the colossal Palace of the Parliament, the heaviest building on Earth and the largest administrative structure in Europe, built by Nicolae Ceausescu's regime. It is so vast that whole historic neighborhoods were razed to clear its footprint, and it still sits largely empty. A quietly heavy piece for a city nicknamed Little Paris.
France#576894 · City Mug Collector SeriesRather than reach for the Eiffel Tower, this France mug chose a light blue château, evoking the fairy-tale Renaissance estates of the Loire Valley like Chambord and Chenonceau that draw millions to the French countryside. It is a quieter, more rural face of France than the Paris-centric pieces, which makes the country mug feel like a deliberate nod to the nation's deep love of its land and wine.
Geneva#576895 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe blue lake and fountain depict the Jet d'Eau, Geneva's signature water plume that shoots 140 meters into the air over Lake Geneva and started life as a simple pressure-release valve for the city waterworks. A global diplomatic hub home to the UN's European seat and the Red Cross, Geneva is also the cradle of fine Swiss watchmaking, which suits a city obsessed with precision.
Bern#576896 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe red figure holding a flag is the Vennerbrunnen, the Banner Carrier Fountain on Bern's Rathausplatz, a 1542 Hans Gieng statue of an armored Venner, a powerful medieval military-political officer. A French soldier snapped off its forearm in 1798, and it was later restored. Bern's arcaded old town is a UNESCO site, and this is a deeper-cut Swiss design that rewards anyone who knows the fountains.
Ruhrgebiet#576898 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe Ruhrgebiet is Germany's old industrial heartland, and this brown mug of buildings and bridge mechanics honors exactly that, coal and steel rather than a single pretty cathedral. The icon version of this design pairs the Zollverein Coal Mine, now a UNESCO World Heritage site, with the Krupp family's Villa Hügel in Essen. A regional rather than a single-city mug, which makes it a slightly unusual catch for the series.
Switzerland#576900 · City Mug Collector SeriesRather than a single city this is a whole-country mug, with a green photo of edelweiss, the white star-shaped alpine flower that is Switzerland's unofficial national emblem and a symbol of rugged mountain devotion. Country-level mugs are unusual in the City series and tend to draw extra interest from collectors who like the oddities. I keep this one for that quirk, a Starbucks mug that reaches for a flower instead of the obvious Matterhorn or a clock.
Munich#576902 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe light blue twin onion-domed towers on my Munich mug are the Frauenkirche, the Cathedral of Our Lady, whose distinctive copper-capped domes are a protected silhouette no nearby building is allowed to exceed. Munich is of course the Oktoberfest and Bavarian capital, but Starbucks wisely chose its enduring church over a beer stein. The pale blue and white even echo Bavaria's flag colors.
Starbucks Stamps (Germany Edition)#576903 · City Mug Collector SeriesThis is the playful odd one out, a Germany-edition mug wrapped in postage stamps from around the world rather than a single city skyline. It belongs to a small philatelic theme Starbucks Germany ran, turning the mug into a passport of imaginary travel, which fits the brand's whole around-the-world conceit. I love it precisely because it breaks the City Mug rules, a conversation piece that rewards a close look at every printed stamp.
Braunschweig#576906 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe green lion is the Brunswick Lion, cast in bronze in 1166 by order of Henry the Lion, the first free-standing monument north of the Alps and a Romanesque masterpiece; the original lives in Dankwarderode Castle with a replica on Burgplatz. Collectors note Braunschweig as one of the harder-to-find German icons. A medieval lion older than most cathedrals is a great story to tell when you pick it up.
Frankfurt#576907 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe green skyline is the giveaway, Frankfurt is the only German city with a true cluster of skyscrapers, earning it the nickname Mainhattan as the financial capital of continental Europe and home to the European Central Bank. Beyond the banks it is the birthplace of Goethe and the historic coronation city of Holy Roman Emperors, so the modern towers sit atop a very long history.
Ireland#576908 · City Mug Collector SeriesInstead of a landmark, Ireland gets a green portrait of James Joyce, the Dublin-born author of Ulysses and one of the towering figures of modern literature. It is a bold, unusual choice for the City Mug Collector Series, putting a writer's face where most mugs show a bridge or a cathedral. Dubliners still mark Bloomsday every June 16th, retracing Ulysses through the city, which makes the Joyce tribute feel exactly right for literary Ireland.
Düsseldorf#576909 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe dark blue tower is the Rheinturm, Düsseldorf's 240-meter concrete Rhine Tower built from 1979 to 1982, which carries what is billed as the world's tallest digital clock spelled out in light dots up its shaft. Capital of North Rhine-Westphalia and a fashion and art hub, the city is also famed for the Königsallee shopping boulevard and its dark, malty Altbier brewed in the Old Town.
Northern Ireland#576911 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe light green beach with rocks is unmistakably the Giant's Causeway, Northern Ireland's only UNESCO World Heritage Site, where roughly 40,000 interlocking basalt columns step out into the sea. Legend says the giant Finn McCool built it, though it actually formed from cooling lava about 60 million years ago. Like the New Zealand piece, this one represents a region rather than a single city.
Sevilla#576912 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe red tower on this Sevilla mug is the Giralda, the bell tower of the cathedral that began life as the minaret of the city's great Almohad mosque around 1198, later crowned with a Renaissance belfry and the bronze Giraldillo weathervane. Spanish City Mugs were never made in huge numbers for the US, so Sevilla is a quietly desirable one. I like that the design honors a tower that is literally half Moorish, half Christian, the whole layered history of Andalusia in one silhouette.
Nürnberg#576914 · City Mug Collector SeriesNürnberg, in Bavaria, wears its old half-timbered houses in dark green here, the kind clustered below the Kaiserburg castle in the medieval old town. The city was a powerhouse of the German Renaissance, home to Albrecht Dürer, and later gave its name to the postwar Nuremberg Trials. A solid German entry in the City Mug Collector Series that pairs nicely with my other Bavaria pieces.
Austria#576916 · City Mug Collector SeriesThis country mug trades the expected Vienna waltz imagery for Austria's natural side, a light purple photo of the Alps rising over green meadows. Roughly two-thirds of Austria is mountainous, with the Eastern Alps dominating Tyrol and Salzburg, the Sound of Music country. A refreshing landscape take that captures the alpine heart of a nation as famous for its peaks and skiing as for Mozart and Klimt.
Leipzig#576917 · City Mug Collector SeriesLeipzig wears a sepia-toned photo of its old architecture, fitting for a German city steeped in music and history, this is where Bach served as cantor at St. Thomas Church and where the peaceful Monday Demonstrations of 1989 helped bring down the Berlin Wall.
