2006 Monkey BearThe Long TailA 2006 Monkey Bearista, part of the costumed-mascot bear run where the plush bear wears a full animal getup rather than seasonal clothing. The Bearista program turned out a steady stream of these character bears, and the playful animal-costume ones are some of the most photogenic on a shelf. Complete with its original hang tag is the difference between a keeper and a thrift-bin find with this whole family of bears.
2006 Valentine's Day BearThe Long TailA 2006 Valentine's Day Bearista, the February sweetheart entry in the annual bear program, typically turned out in reds and hearts for the holiday. Valentine bears are a recurring fixture of the Bearista line and tend to surface every winter on the resale market. As with all of them the original tag and clean plush are what separate a collectible from a stuffed animal, and the holiday-dated ones hold their appeal year after year.
2007 Black Cat BearThe Long TailA 2007 Black Cat Bearista, the Halloween entry in that year's bear program, the plush bear dressed in a black cat costume for the season. Halloween Bearistas are among the more characterful of the costumed bears and a natural target for collectors who chase the holiday-themed releases. As ever the original tag and unfaded plush are what hold the value, and a sharp black cat bear is a small October trophy on the shelf.
2007 Halloween Bat BearThe Long TailOne of the seasonal Bearista spinoffs Starbucks rolled out for autumn 2007, this little guy comes dressed as a bat with wings rather than the usual scarf or sweater. Halloween bears were never the marquee annual editions, so they slipped out in smaller numbers and tend to surface only around October, which is exactly why a costumed novelty like this is a fun, low-key catch for a serious shelf.
2007 Vacation BearThe Long TailA 2007 Bearista in travel mode, one of the themed yearly bears Starbucks dressed for an occasion rather than the plain annual editions. Vacation and holiday-costumed bears were store novelties that depended on what the season called for, so they did not all see equal print runs. For a bear-focused collector the appeal is completing the costume parade, and a travel-dressed bear fills an oddly specific gap.
2008 Blue Yellow Butterfly BearThe Long TailA 2008 Bearista in a blue and yellow butterfly getup, one of a small spring-themed butterfly pair Starbucks issued that year. The matching pink and yellow version makes the two a natural set to hunt together. Butterfly bears are minor entries in the long Bearista run, which is exactly what makes tracking both color variants a satisfying completist chase.
2008 Bunny BearThe Long TailA 2008 Easter-season Bearista dressed as a bunny, part of the spring holiday rotation that gave the bears rabbit ears and pastel trim. These seasonal costume bears appeared briefly each spring and were never the flagship annual editions, so they are scarcer in the wild. For a bear collector the bunny is a charming, instantly readable addition to the costume lineup.
2008 Pink Yellow Butterfly BearThe Long TailThe pink and yellow counterpart to the 2008 blue butterfly Bearista, the two together forming that year's small spring butterfly pair. Owning both colorways is the point, since Starbucks often split a seasonal idea across two palettes to nudge collectors toward buying twice. A cheerful, light entry in the bear archive and a tidy way to close out a 2008 spring set.
2009 Hawaii BearThe Long TailA 2009 Bearista tied to Hawaii, part of the regional Bearista offshoots sold mainly in their home market rather than nationwide. Place-specific bears like the Hawaii edition are harder to find on the mainland and carry the same destination-collector appeal as a city mug. For a bear shelf it doubles as a travel souvenir, a bear you essentially had to be in the islands to grab.
2009 Pumpkin Trick or Treat SweateThe Long TailA 2009 Halloween Bearista in a pumpkin trick-or-treat sweater, continuing the autumn costume tradition that ran alongside the brand's pumpkin-spice season. The knit-sweater treatment is a sweeter take than the previous bat bear. These October-only costume bears slipped out quietly each fall, so a well-kept pumpkin-sweater example is a nice seasonal anchor in a bear collection.
2009 Sakura Blossom, MugThe Long TailA 2009 cherry blossom mug from Starbucks Japan, tied to the spring sakura season that the brand has turned into one of its most fervently collected annual events. Japan releases a fresh sakura lineup every spring and the pieces routinely sell out fast, with older years like 2009 commanding real attention and steep prices on the secondary market. A genuinely desirable Japan-market grab for anyone chasing the sakura tradition.
2010 Las Vegas BearThe Long TailA 2010 Las Vegas Bearista from the Destination Series, the city-bear line Starbucks has run since the late 1990s to mark places, holidays and even ballteams. Ours is the beige plush with the souvenir hangtag, a Sin City souvenir you grabbed near the Strip. Destination bears trade actively on eBay and bearista.org tracks the whole catalog, so collectors hunt the city ones by name.
2010 Trick or Treat Halloween WolfThe Long TailA 2010 Halloween Bearista dressed in a wolf costume for trick-or-treat, part of the seasonal costumed-bear runs Starbucks issued alongside the annual holiday bears. Costume Bearistas are a fun niche, the werewolf-wolf getup making this one a Halloween-specific grab rather than a year-round bear. Holiday and costume bears draw their own collectors hunting complete seasonal sets.
2010, Long Blue and Purple FeatherThe Long TailA 2010 decorative mug featuring a bird with long blue and purple plumage, part of Starbucks' everyday nature-pattern run rather than any city series. The trailing peacock-like feathers give it a lush, ornamental look. A pretty wildcard from the long tail, the kind of one-off design that fills the gaps between the named collectible lines.
2011 Green Puffer Jacket BearThe Long TailA 2011 Bearista zipped into a green puffer jacket, one of the costumed winter bears from Starbucks' long-running annual bear program that started in 1997. The puffy cold-weather coat marks it as a holiday-season bear meant to look ready for snow. Costumed Bearistas like this draw collectors building out complete seasonal sets year by year.
2012 Nutcracker BearThe Long TailA 2012 Nutcracker-themed Bearista, the little plush-style bear dressed as the toy soldier from the Christmas ballet. Starbucks issued an annual run of costumed Bearista bears, and holiday editions like this Nutcracker are among the most collected. The Tchaikovsky-ballet styling, with the tall soldier's hat and uniform, makes this one of the more characterful entries in the bear lineup.
2012, Tohoku, MugThe Long TailA 2012 regional mug for Tohoku, the rugged northeast of Japan covering all six prefectures from Aomori down to Fukushima. Released the year after the 2011 earthquake and tsunami, these Tohoku-limited pieces carried real weight for the region's recovery. It is a genuinely scarce Japan-area exclusive, sold only up north, and collectors prize it precisely because it never circulated nationwide.
2013 Gyeongju Korea, Drive-ThruThe Long TailMy second Gyeongju Drive-Thru piece, the regional store exclusive for Korea's old Silla capital. Drive-Thru and store-specific Korean mugs were never widely distributed, which is exactly what makes the doubles worth keeping. Gyeongju itself is sacred ground for Korean history, its royal tomb mounds and Buddhist temples earning UNESCO World Heritage status, and a mug from there carries more story than most city pieces.
2013, Chinese Circular Motives, 14The Long TailA 14oz mug patterned with circular Chinese motifs, the kind of roundel designs drawn from traditional auspicious symbols and lattice work. Rather than naming a city, this one celebrates Chinese decorative art itself, an elegant pan-China design from the China market. It sits nicely beside my named Shanghai mugs as the abstract, pattern-driven counterpart in the collection.
After Coffee Mint, Tin BoxThe Long TailA small hinged tin of After Coffee mints, the sort of impulse object Starbucks tucked by the register so you left with fresh breath after your espresso. No catalog detail survives on mine, but these little tins are pure period merchandising, throwaway by design and therefore scarce intact. I keep it for the completeness, the supporting cast around the mugs.
America Scores BearThe Long TailA Bearista tied to America SCORES, the after-school program that pairs youth soccer with poetry and service learning in underserved schools. Starbucks made charity and cause bears alongside its city and holiday ones, and this is one of the do-good ones rather than a souvenir. I keep it for the story, a plush mascot standing in for a kids' program rather than a skyline.
Arizona Diamond Backs BearThe Long TailOne of the MLB Bearistas, this one in Arizona Diamondbacks colors, from the era when Starbucks dressed its bear in ballclub gear. Starbucks started Bearistas in 1997 and at their peak put out more than sixty a year, including team tie-ins. I have two Diamondbacks variants, so the small differences in jersey and tag are part of the fun of the chase.
Arizona Diamondbacks BearThe Long TailThe companion to my other Diamondbacks bear, the second of the pair, which is exactly why MLB Bearistas are a collector rabbit hole, the same team turning up in slightly different outfits or tag years. Snake red and Sedona accents for Arizona's club. Holding both side by side is the only way to read the variation, and that is half the reason I keep doubles.
Atlanta Braves BearThe Long TailAn Atlanta Braves Bearista from the MLB run, the bear kitted in Braves colors for the team that has called Atlanta home since 1966. These club bears sat in a corner of the late-2000s Bearista boom alongside the city and holiday editions. I keep it with my other ballpark bears, a soft, tomahawk-era souvenir of a franchise rather than a city skyline.
Awareness (2002), MugThe Long TailA 2002 mug built around the word Awareness, part of Starbucks early-2000s push to tie coffee buying to social and environmental causes like fair trade and conservation. These message mugs sit apart from the city line, which makes them easy to overlook and undervalue. I keep mine because the cause-marketing language is a genuine time capsule of how the company talked to customers two decades ago.
Barista (With Green Apron) BearThe Long TailA Bearista in the working green apron, the everyday face of the Starbucks bear mascot line that has run as annual and themed editions since the late 1990s. The plain green-apron barista is the baseline of the whole series, the one every special edition riffs on. I treat it as the anchor of my bear shelf, the reference point that makes the seasonal and country bears make sense.
Barista Bear (With Brown Apron ofThe Long TailThis Bearista wears the brown apron, a direct callback to Starbucks earliest baristas at the original 1971 Pike Place store before the green apron became standard. That heritage detail is the whole point of the bear, a wearable bit of company origin story. Brown-apron variants are scarcer than the green and quietly nod to the 1971 founding date the brand still prints on its cups.
Bear in PJ's with little BearThe Long TailA Bearista tucked into pajamas cradling a tiny cub, one of the bedtime-themed editions in the long-running bear line. The parent-and-baby pairing is a recurring sentimental motif Starbucks revisits, and the little bear is the easy piece to lose. A complete set with the cub still present is what makes this one worth grabbing over the loose adult bears you see far more often.
Bear, 2010 MugThe Long TailA 2010 mug from the Bearista world, carrying the bear mascot onto ceramic rather than plush. Crossovers where a plush-line character jumps to a mug are a nice bridge between two parts of the collection. Dated 2010, it pins down exactly which year's bear styling it represents, which is the kind of anchor I value when the bear runs blur together.
Blue Rocket, 14oz, Frappuccino CupThe Long TailPart of the Blue Rocket Frappuccino line, this 14oz double-walled plastic cold cup with its own reusable straw was Starbucks' answer to the blended-drink craze. The deep blue body, striped throughout with those long racing lines, signals speed and summer. These were everyday merchandise rather than collector pieces, so finding one complete with the matching straw is what actually makes it worth shelving.
Blue Rocket, 16oz, Frappuccino CupThe Long TailThe 16oz grande sibling in the Blue Rocket family, same bright blue plastic and the streaking line motif that runs the full height of the cup. Frappuccino debuted as a Starbucks product in 1995, and this reusable cold cup rode that wave for years. Straw intact is the detail collectors look for, since the loose straws almost always went missing first.
Boston Red SoxThe Long TailA Boston Red Sox co-branded piece tying Starbucks to one of baseball's most storied franchises, founded in 1901 and home to Fenway Park, the oldest ballpark in the majors since 1912. Team-licensed Starbucks merchandise was always regional and limited, sold near the ballclub's market. That narrow distribution is exactly why sports tie-ins like this are tougher to track down than standard city mugs.
Boston Red Sox BearThe Long TailA Bearista bear decked out in Red Sox colors, marrying Starbucks' annual collectible mascot with Fenway loyalty. The Bearista line ran as themed and seasonal bears, and sports versions were sold into a single team's regional market, so they did not circulate widely. For a collector this is a crossover piece, valued as much by Red Sox memorabilia hunters as by Starbucks people.
Chinese Bear with Little BearThe Long TailA tender momma-and-cub pairing from the Bearista family, the larger bear cradling a small one, exactly the kind of nesting-pair piece that Starbucks loves to issue around gifting season in Asian markets. I keep the two together as a set, because once a little bear wanders off it almost never comes back to its partner, and split pairs are the bane of every Bearista collector trying to reassemble a family.
Chinese New Year 2006 Dog BearThe Long TailThe Bearista released for the 2006 Year of the Dog, part of the Lunar zodiac bear run that Starbucks Asia issued annually from the mid-2000s. Each bear wears or carries the year's animal, and the dog year ties to loyalty and steadfastness in Chinese tradition. Collectors who chase the full twelve-animal cycle treat these early issues as the foundation stones of the set.
Chinese New Year 2010 Tiger BearThe Long TailThe 2010 Year of the Tiger Bearista, one of the more dramatic animals in the zodiac cycle and a favorite among collectors for that reason. The tiger sign carries connotations of bravery and power, and 2010 was a metal tiger year in the sixty-year ganzhi calendar. As part of the annual Asia-market Lunar bear series, these survive in fewer numbers outside their home markets than most people assume.
Chinese New Year Dragon BearThe Long TailThe Year of the Dragon Bearista, the 2012 issue, and the dragon is the single most coveted animal in the entire zodiac. It is the only mythical creature among the twelve, a symbol of imperial power and luck, and dragon-year babies and dragon-year merchandise both spike in demand. Of all the Lunar bears, the dragon is the one collectors fight hardest to land.
Chinese New Year Pig BearThe Long TailThe Year of the Pig Bearista, the pig being the twelfth and final animal of the zodiac cycle and a sign tied to prosperity, generosity, and abundance. In Chinese tradition the pig year is considered fortunate for wealth, which is why pig-themed gifts circulate heavily at New Year. Closing out the twelve-animal sequence, this bear is the one that lets a completist finally say the set is whole.
Chinese New Year Rabbit BearThe Long TailThe Year of the Rabbit Bearista, the 2011 issue from the Asia Lunar series. The rabbit is the gentlest sign of the zodiac, linked to grace, calm, and longevity, and it is one of the more charming animals to render in plush bear form. Sandwiched between the dramatic tiger and dragon years, the rabbit bear is easy to overlook, which is exactly why it sometimes turns up cheap.
Chinese New Year Rooster BearThe Long TailThe Year of the Rooster Bearista, the rooster being the tenth zodiac sign and a symbol of punctuality, honesty, and confidence. Starbucks issued rooster-year merchandise in both 2005 and 2017, so dating these bears comes down to styling cues and packaging. As part of the annual Lunar bear run, it slots neatly into the twelve-animal lineup that defines this corner of the Asia collection.
Clouds in the Coffee MugThe Long TailA whimsical conceptual mug riffing on the image of clouds drifting across the surface of a coffee, the sort of art-driven novelty piece Starbucks slipped into its lineup outside the city-souvenir lines. The name nods to the everyday poetry of watching cream swirl into a fresh cup. Pieces like this fall well off the beaten collector path, which is part of why I enjoy tracking them down.
Coffee Harvest Truck, Tin BoxThe Long TailA decorative tin box illustrated with a coffee-harvest truck, the workhorse vehicle that hauls ripe cherries down from the slopes to the mill during picking season. Starbucks issued tins like this as gift packaging and standalone collectibles, and the harvest imagery ties straight to origin and the human labor behind every bean. Tins survive unevenly because most were tossed once empty, so an intact one is a small find.
Doubleshot Plastic Cups(s)The Long TailPromotional plastic cups tied to Starbucks Doubleshot, the canned espresso-and-cream beverage the company launched commercially in 2002. These are merchandising throwaways rather than ceramic collectibles, the kind of branded plastic that almost never survives in good shape. That very disposability is what makes a clean surviving example mildly interesting, an everyday artifact of the Doubleshot push that most people simply recycled.
Flowers behind the back / ValentinThe Long TailA Valentine Bearista caught mid-gesture, hiding a bouquet behind his back, the bashful romantic pose Starbucks loved for its February bears. These seasonal Valentine Bearistas were dressed-up annual editions sold only in the short pre-holiday window, so they vanished fast from shelves. I keep him with the rest of the bear lineup because the storytelling pose makes him one of the most charming of the romantic releases.
Frappuccino, Black MugThe Long TailA black mug branding the Frappuccino, the frozen blended drink Starbucks did not actually invent but acquired in 1994 when it bought Boston's Coffee Connection, then launched nationwide in 1995 with just coffee and mocha flavors. The drink became a billion-dollar phenomenon, so merch celebrating it carries real brand history. This darker version is the moodier counterpart to the standard logo mug in my Frappuccino pair.
French Press & Case (8 Cups)The Long TailNot a mug but a working 8-cup French press with its carrying case, the immersion brewer Starbucks long championed as the purist's way to taste a coffee's full body and oils. Pieces of actual brewing equipment are a different kind of collecting, harder to keep complete since the glass carafe and case rarely survive together. I treasure this one as a reminder that Starbucks sold the method, not just the beans.
Green Leaves and Pebbles, MugThe Long TailA nature themed mug built around green leaves and pebbles, a calm organic motif in the spirit of Starbucks' garden and earth toned design phases. With no catalog text to anchor a city or year, it lives happily in the miscellaneous line, a soothing botanical piece for anyone who likes their morning coffee with a touch of the outdoors.
Guatemala, MugThe Long TailA Guatemala mug, fitting given the country's outsized place in coffee itself, its high altitude Antigua and Huehuetenango beans are prized by roasters worldwide and Starbucks has long sourced there. The land of eternal spring is known for the colonial streets of Antigua beneath the Agua volcano and the vivid Mayan textiles of the highlands. A coffee origin country mug always carries extra meaning for a collector, since this is where the cup actually begins.
Hanukiah MugThe Long TailA festival of lights piece centered on the hanukiah, the nine branched menorah lit across the eight nights of Hanukkah, with the central shamash used to kindle the others. The holiday marks the rededication of the Second Temple and the miracle of one day's oil burning for eight. A nicely specific seasonal design, the kind of Judaica themed mug that rounds out a holiday focused shelf.
Hawaii 2009/2010 BearThe Long TailA Destination Bearista from the 2009 to 2010 run, dressed in island theme for Hawaii. This sits in the era collectors nicknamed the recession bear, when the 2009 plush was noticeably slimmer than earlier years before quality rebounded in 2010. Location specific Bearistas like the Hawaii bear are exactly what collectors chase, and tracked sales have placed the Hawaii destination bear in the modest tens of dollars.
Hawaii 2010 BearThe Long TailThe 2010 Hawaii Bearista, from the year the bears regained the plusher, fuller build that fans had missed after the lean 2009 edition. Starbucks has issued Bearistas since 1997 to mark holidays, cities, countries and more, and the place based ones are the heart of the hunt. Having both the 2009 to 2010 and the standalone 2010 Hawaii bears side by side documents that quality turnaround nicely.
Holland America, MugThe Long TailA Holland America piece, tied to the storied Holland America Line, the Dutch shipping company founded in 1873 that carried generations of European emigrants to the New World before becoming a premier cruise brand. That transatlantic heritage links neatly to the Dutch and American themes scattered through this batch. A travel and maritime crossover mug like this is an unusual catch outside the standard city series.
Jaqaytay, Philippine Exclusives (2The Long TailA 2004 Philippine Exclusives mug, named for Tagaytay, the cool ridge city overlooking Taal, one of the world's smallest active volcanoes sitting inside a lake inside a larger caldera. Tagaytay is the Manila crowd's weekend escape for the views and the chilly air, so a coffee mug fits the place perfectly. These early Philippine market exclusives rarely surface outside Southeast Asia, which makes any of them a quiet score for a regional collector.
Kiss Me / Frog Bear / ValentineThe Long TailA Valentine themed Kiss Me piece featuring the frog Bearista, part of Starbucks' long running bear mascot tradition where the bears dress up for seasons and holidays. The frog prince conceit, kiss me to break the spell, is a sweet Valentine's gag, and themed Bearistas like this seasonal valentine run are exactly the kind of cross over collectors of both bears and mugs love to chase down.
Label and Erase CanisterThe Long TailA piece of Starbucks home equipment rather than a souvenir, this ceramic storage canister has a writable surface so you can label what bean is inside and wipe it clean when you switch roasts. It is a practical countertop object aimed at the at-home enthusiast, the kind of utilitarian gear that rounds out a collection beyond the mugs. I keep it because it shows the brand selling a whole coffee ritual, not just cups.
Los Angeles AngelsThe Long TailAn officially MLB-licensed Los Angeles Angels mug, team merchandise rather than a Starbucks travel piece, carrying the Angels' winged-halo "A" identity from Anaheim. These club-branded ceramics live a little outside the core city-mug lines, which is why I file them with the long-tail oddities. It is a fun crossover that shows how far the coffee-and-collectible world overlaps with sports fandom.
Los Angeles Angels BearThe Long TailA Bearista-style plush or figure dressed in Los Angeles Angels colors, the team-licensed cousin to the Angels mug. The Bearista mascot has been Starbucks' annual collectible bear for decades, so a co-branded MLB version is a charming mashup of two separate collecting worlds. I keep the bear and the mug together as a little Angels set within the long tail.
Los Angeles AnglesThe Long TailA misspelled "Angels" entry, this is the same Los Angeles Angels team piece with the typo "Angles" baked into the listing. Catalog slips like this are oddly valuable to a serious collector because they reveal how the inventory was keyed, and they make for a good story. I keep the note honest rather than inventing a separate object that does not exist.
Manila, Philippine Exclusives (200The Long TailPart of the 2004 Philippine Exclusives, this Manila mug celebrates the capital of the Philippines, a city defined by the walled Spanish-colonial district of Intramuros and historic Manila Bay sunsets. The Exclusives line was sold only within the local market, which is what makes these early Philippine pieces harder to find outside the country. I prize regional-only runs like this because they never entered the global distribution that floods the common city mugs.
Muay Thai BearThe Long TailA Bearista dressed for Muay Thai, Thailand's national sport and the ancient eight-limbed striking art known as the art of eight limbs. These market-specific costumed bears were sold mostly in-country, so a Thai-themed fighter bear is a fun travel grab rather than a global release. He stands in my long-tail menagerie as a reminder that Starbucks let local culture climb right onto the mascot.
New York Mets BearThe Long TailA Bearista in New York Mets gear, from Starbucks' run of MLB team mascot bears made for local ballpark and team markets. The Mets, founded in 1962 and playing now at Citi Field, get the orange-and-blue treatment on the little collectible. Team bears were sold regionally and seldom widely, so a specific franchise bear like this is a fun, hard-to-stumble-on cross-collectible for any New York shelf.
New York RangersThe Long TailA nod to the New York Rangers, one of the National Hockey League's Original Six, founded in 1926 and skating out of Madison Square Garden. They ended a 54 year title drought in 1994, the year the modern Starbucks collectible boom was getting going, so a Rangers piece carries that decade's New York energy. Team licensed Starbucks mugs are unusual, which is why a hockey crossover like this catches a collector's eye.
New York Yankees BearThe Long TailA Bearista in Yankees pinstripes, tying Starbucks's plush mascot line to baseball's most storied franchise, 27 World Series titles and counting out of the Bronx. Co branded sports Bearistas were typically sold near the ballparks and team stores rather than nationwide, so they live a little off the main bear checklist. I like this one for the crossover of two collecting worlds, Starbucks bears and Yankees memorabilia.
New Yorker BearThe Long TailA Bearista dressed as the quintessential New Yorker, leaning into the city's worldly, fast paced reputation. Starbucks loved giving its bears a local persona, a beret here, a business suit there, so a New York themed bear fits a long tradition of city specific Bearistas sold as travel keepsakes. These character bears trade steadily among the dedicated Bearista crowd who chase the full annual and themed roster.
Okinawa Mug (2002)The Long TailA 2002 mug for Okinawa, Japan's subtropical southern island chain known for turquoise seas, Ryukyu kingdom heritage, and the world's highest concentration of centenarians. Okinawa sits far from the main islands with its own distinct culture, which Starbucks's regional Japanese line loved to celebrate. As a dated early 2000s prefecture piece, it slots neatly into the year by year Japan run that collectors there pursue.
Penguins with Earmuffs, MugThe Long TailA whimsical winter mug fronted by penguins wearing earmuffs, part of the lighthearted cold weather novelty designs Starbucks slipped in around the holidays rather than a city or series piece. These character mugs lean cute over collectible, but they have a small following among people who chase the playful animal designs specifically. The earmuffed penguin is a recurring bit of Starbucks winter humor, since penguins hardly need the extra insulation.
Pleated Logo Canister, Knob on TopThe Long TailThis is a ceramic storage canister with a pleated ribbed body, the logo on the front and a knob topped lid, made to hold ground coffee or beans on the counter. Starbucks home barware like this rounded out the kitchen lineup beyond mugs, and the pleated column shape is a distinctive period look that pairs with matching sugar and creamer pieces. Canisters survive less often than mugs because the knob lids chip and separate, so a complete one with its original top is the harder half to track down.
Rockies Colorado BearThe Long TailA Colorado themed Bearista style bear tied to the Rocky Mountains, the range that gives the state its identity with more than fifty peaks above 14,000 feet. The Rockies are the defining backdrop of Colorado life, so a mountain bear is the obvious mascot for the region. These character bears were always the playful counterpoint to the serious city ceramics, and a regional one like this leans into local pride.
Roppongi Hills Mug (2003)The Long TailThis mug ties to Roppongi Hills, the massive Tokyo redevelopment anchored by the 54 story Mori Tower that opened in April 2003, so a 2003 dated cup lands exactly on the district's debut year. Roppongi Hills was conceived as a city within a city, mixing offices, the Mori Art Museum near the top of the tower, shops and apartments, and it instantly became a Tokyo landmark. A store or district specific Japan piece like this carries real provenance.
Roppongi Hills Mug (2004)The Long TailThe 2004 follow up to the Roppongi Hills mug, marking the development's first full year as a Tokyo destination after the 2003 opening. Japan Starbucks loved issuing location tied and dated mugs with completely fresh artwork each year, which is part of why the Japanese pieces are prized far above the uniform Western city line. Owning the 2003 and 2004 pair tells the early story of Roppongi Hills one year at a time.
Sakura (2005), MugThe Long TailPart of Starbucks Japan's beloved annual Sakura run, the spring-only cherry blossom collection that drops every February and sells out almost instantly. The 2005 edition is one of the early entries in a tradition that has since become a frenzy, with collectors abroad paying premiums and resale listings appearing within hours. Each year reinterprets the same fleeting hanami theme, so owning an early dated one like this anchors the whole timeline on the shelf.
Sakura (2011), Espresso MugThe Long TailA small espresso-size mug from the 2011 Sakura collection, the demitasse companion to that spring's larger cherry blossom pieces. The little ones are easy to overlook but they are exactly what completists chase, since the espresso format was made in smaller runs and is far harder to find intact years later. 2011 also carries weight in Japan as the year of the Tohoku earthquake, which gives that spring's release a quiet poignancy.
Sakura (2011), MugThe Long TailThe full-size 2011 entry in Starbucks Japan's annual cherry blossom series, released for the spring hanami season. Each year's Sakura design is a fresh take on the same fleeting blossom theme, and the collection is one of the most sought after Starbucks Japan ever does, selling out in days and reselling for multiples abroad. Holding a dated one from 2011 puts a specific spring in your hands, which is exactly why I keep the years separate.
Sakura (2012), MugThe Long TailThe 2012 Sakura mug, that year's installment of the spring-only cherry blossom line Starbucks Japan has run for over two decades. The whole appeal rests on impermanence, the few-week window of hanami when sakura bloom and scatter, and the company reissues a new interpretation every February to ride that wave. These annual drops vanish fast in stores, so a clean dated 2012 is a tidy piece of the timeline.
Sakura (2013), MugThe Long Tail2013's take on the Sakura theme, from the most anticipated seasonal release on the Starbucks Japan calendar. By this point the cherry blossom line had become a true event, with queues, online sellouts and a healthy resale market overseas, so the dated mugs read almost like vintage years of a wine. I value the run precisely because each year stands alone, and 2013 fills its slot.
Sakura (2016), MugThe Long TailThe 2016 Sakura mug continues Starbucks Japan's spring cherry blossom tradition, that annual February drop tied to the country's hanami season. By the mid 2010s the collection had a devoted global following, with items selling out within hours and turning up immediately on the secondary market at a markup. A dated 2016 keeps the modern stretch of the timeline honest on the shelf.
Sakura (2017), MugThe Long Tail2017's entry in the long-running Sakura series, Starbucks Japan's love letter to the fleeting cherry blossom. Every spring brings a fresh palette and motif on the same theme, and the releases are famous for selling out almost instantly while resale listings appear the same day. Owning the dated 2017 alongside the earlier years lets you watch the design language shift over a decade.
Sakura, Hexagon, MugThe Long TailA Sakura mug with a hexagon body, a faceted six-sided shape rather than the standard round wall, from Starbucks Japan's cherry blossom line. The shaped formats are where the spring collection gets playful, and the geometric silhouette makes this one stand out instantly in a row of cylinders. Special-shape Sakura pieces tend to be produced in smaller quantities, which is exactly what makes them worth hunting.
San Diego PadresThe Long TailA San Diego Padres tie-in mug, from the small slice of co-branded sports pieces Starbucks produced for local markets. The Padres have played at downtown's Petco Park since 2004 and are unmistakable in their brown and gold, the throwback colors fans fought to bring back. Team-licensed Starbucks mugs are an unusual niche and far less documented than the city lines, so a clean Padres example is a genuine oddity worth holding onto.
San Francisco GiantsThe Long TailA licensed San Francisco Giants tie-in mug, leaning on the team that brought Barry Bonds, the home run record, and three World Series titles in the 2010s to the bay at Oracle Park. Sports-club Starbucks pieces were usually sold only in the home market, so they tend to circulate in smaller numbers than the city mugs. A fun crossover oddity for a collection.
San Francisco Giants BearThe Long TailA San Francisco Giants Bearista, the plush-look ceramic bear mascot dressed in team colors. The Bearista bears began in 1997 and the sports-licensed editions are among the harder ones to track down because they were tied to single ballpark gift shops and regional stores rather than the national catalog. Cute, niche, and squarely a hunt piece.
Seattle Mariners BearThe Long TailA Seattle Mariners Bearista decked in the home club's colors, tying the mascot bear line to the team of Ken Griffey Jr. and Ichiro at the ballpark now called T-Mobile Park. Like the other sports-licensed bears, it was a regional release sold near the stadium rather than nationwide, which keeps these comparatively scarce. A hometown crossover for the Seattle case.
Snowman Bear with PuppyThe Long TailThis is a Bearista style holiday figure, the snowman costumed bear shown cradling a little puppy, part of Starbucks' long running plush and ceramic bear tradition that began back in 1997. The snowman outfit places it firmly in the Christmas gifting line. Themed Bearistas like this, especially ones with an extra companion character such as the puppy, are the kind of detail collectors prize because the small added figure makes the piece feel one of a kind rather than a generic holiday bear.
Snowman Costume BearThe Long TailAnother entry in the Bearista bear universe, this one dressed head to toe as a snowman for the holidays, continuing the annual collectible bear series Starbucks has issued since the late 1990s. The costume bears are released seasonally, and the snowman getup is a recurring winter favorite. Bearista collectors track these by year and costume, and a clean snowman bear is a staple of any holiday focused shelf, often displayed alongside its mug counterparts from the same season.
Stanley Park, Vancouver, Park SeriThe Long TailPart of the 2007 Park Series celebrating great parks of the US and Canada, this one honors Stanley Park in Vancouver, the 1,000 acre rainforest peninsula ringed by its famous seawall and dotted with totem poles, larger than New York's Central Park and consistently ranked among the world's best urban parks. The Park Series was a focused, short run line, so its individual mugs are tougher to complete than mainstream city series. A Canadian entry like Stanley Park adds cross border depth to a North American park set.
Starbucks and CARE, 14 x 7.5" MetaThe Long TailA 14 by 7.5 inch metal tin from the Starbucks and CARE partnership, one of the oldest threads in the company's philanthropy. Starbucks began working with the humanitarian group CARE back in 1991, funding clean water, health and literacy projects in coffee-growing countries like Indonesia, Guatemala and Kenya, and sold CARE sampler coffees so customers could chip in. A tin like this is a tangible relic of that early do-good era, well before Fair Trade branding existed.
Starbucks Candy / Mints / ChocolatThe Long TailA grouping of Starbucks candy, mints and chocolates collected across the years, the kind of edible ephemera most people threw away. Starbucks ran After Coffee mints, chocolate-covered espresso beans and seasonal truffles, much of it tied to the short-lived Starbucks chocolate line and the Tazo and confection experiments. Surviving sealed or boxed examples are genuinely scarce precisely because they were meant to be eaten, which makes a saved set quietly interesting.
Starbucks Coffee Liquor (Empty) BoThe Long TailAn empty 750ml of Starbucks Coffee Liqueur, and the backstory is great: Starbucks teamed with Jim Beam's Beam Global to launch it in early 2005 at forty proof, sold only in bars and liquor stores, never in the cafes. They pulled the line around 2010, so even an empty bottle is now a genuine collector relic of Starbucks' brief detour into booze. Fans hunt these for the label alone.
State #31, California, MugThe Long TailCalifornia is number thirty-one in the 1997 States of Bean series from Daleet Zigelboim and Jan Belson, the line that gave every US state and several Canadian provinces a fact-covered 20oz mug. As Starbucks' home-coast state and the brand's biggest market, California carries extra collector pull, and assembling the complete States of Bean set remains one of the more ambitious goals in this corner of the hobby.
Team Starbucks - Winning TogetherThe Long TailA Team Starbucks, Winning Together piece, an internal partner and morale item rather than retail stock, the kind of mug handed out at conferences or store openings to reward the green apron crew. These employee only pieces rarely reach the public, which is exactly why collectors prize them. There is no city or landmark here, just company culture made tangible, and that insider provenance is the whole appeal.
To-Go Cup, CanisterThe Long TailA canister shaped like Starbucks' iconic to go paper cup, a piece of merchandising that turns the company's most recognizable object into a storage tin or display item. The disposable cup with its sleeve and siren is as famous as the logo itself, so reproducing it as a keepsake is clever brand play. A novelty form like this is more about silhouette recognition than any landmark or date.
True Love Valentine BearThe Long TailA True Love Valentine Bearista, part of the long running Bearista bear line that Starbucks launched in 1997 and refreshed with seasonal themes year after year. Valentine editions lean into red, hearts, and romance, making them a small but devoted niche within the broader bear collecting world. Holiday and seasonal Bearistas are exactly the kind of dated, themed pieces that bear collectors hunt to complete a calendar of releases.
Turquoise Lip Mosaic, MugThe Long TailA mug finished with a turquoise mosaic detail at the lip, part of Starbucks' decorative tile and mosaic styled ceramics that prize texture and color over logos or geography. Mosaic and hand glazed finishes give these pieces an artisanal, almost Mediterranean feel that sets them apart from the standard printed mugs. The turquoise rim is the whole story here, a tactile design choice meant to be picked up and felt.
Unchain My Heart / Valentine BearThe Long TailA Valentine's Bearista from the holiday-romance run, themed Unchain My Heart after the Joe Cocker and Ray Charles standard. These seasonal bears were short-window releases timed to February, which keeps the genuine vintage ones harder to find than the year-round Bearistas. A sweet, on-theme companion to the Verona Valentine pieces in the collection.
Valentine Bear (1)The Long TailOne of the classic Valentine Bearista bears, a heart-themed entry in Starbucks' long-running annual bear program that began in 1997. Bearistas are sold in costume each season, and the Valentine editions are among the most giftable, which means many got loved hard and survivors in clean shape are the ones collectors chase. A cuddly cornerstone of any bear shelf.
Various Roasts Stickers, MugThe Long TailA playful mug papered in sticker-style labels for different Starbucks roasts, turning the cup itself into a roast guide. It plays on the company's roast spectrum, from Blonde through Medium to Dark, the shorthand the brand still uses today. A fun, informal piece that doubles as a cheat sheet for the coffee wall.
White Polar Bear CostumeThe Long TailOne of the dress-up costume accessories from the Bearista world, a little white polar bear outfit meant to be worn by the plush bear rather than displayed alone. These costume add-ons are easy to lose and were sold separately, so an intact one is harder to find than the bears themselves. I treat it as part of the broader Bearista ecosystem, the seasonal wardrobe that made collecting the bears a deeper game.
White, Short CanisterThe Long TailA plain white short canister from the storage and equipment side of the catalog, made to hold beans or grounds on a counter rather than to be sipped from. Canisters are the unglamorous backbone of any complete collection, the housewares that shared shelf space with the mugs. The short white version is the understated one, easy to overlook, which is exactly why I wanted it logged.
Yellow Rain Coat BearThe Long TailA Bearista in a bright yellow raincoat, one of the themed wardrobe versions of the plush mascot that began in 1997. The slicker-clad bear plays to a rainy Pacific Northwest sensibility, fitting for a Seattle company. These outfitted Bearistas were seasonal, so the costumed editions like the raincoat bear are the ones collectors hunt to round out the annual lineup.
Classification

You Are Here90 pieces

The modern flagship travel line, living inventory since 2013.
Japan#186133 · You Are Here CollectionThe 3oz espresso companion to the Japan mug, shrinking Mount Fuji, sunrise, and sakura onto a demitasse with the same red interior. The little ones are produced in smaller numbers and are tougher to find boxed, so collectors who want the matched full-size and mini pair often hunt a while. A charming pocket-sized version of one of the series' prettiest designs.
Virginia#455661 · You Are Here CollectionVirginia in the You Are Here line, dark blue inside, with drums, the state flag, and a blue crab wrapped around the outside. The drums and flag nod to Virginia as the birthplace of presidents, four of the first five, from Washington at Mount Vernon to Jefferson at Monticello, while the crab is pure Chesapeake Bay, the watermen's livelihood that defines the state's coastal table. It is a tidy little capsule of colonial history and tidewater seafood on one mug.
Texas#576511 · You Are Here CollectionA cow and a farm on an orange interior leans into the ranching mythology of Texas, the cattle country that shaped the cowboy image and still leads the nation in beef production. Texas is so large it spans two time zones and was its own republic from 1836 to 1845. The warm orange glaze suits the wide-open plains and big sky, a friendly statewide companion to the San Antonio city mug.
Animal Kingdom#576512 · You Are Here CollectionA Disney-park You Are Here mug for Disney's Animal Kingdom, green inside with the giant Tree of Life and a Magic Kingdom castle motif. This is the original Tree of Life design, the version later swapped out for an Asia-area edition featuring Expedition Everest, so this earlier print is the one Disney-Starbucks crossover collectors specifically seek. The hand-carved Tree of Life is the park's centerpiece, fourteen stories tall and covered in hundreds of animal sculptures.
St. Louis#576513 · You Are Here CollectionThe Gateway Arch is the whole show here, Eero Saarinen's stainless steel catenary curve that rises 630 feet, the tallest man-made monument in the United States and a perfect single-icon subject for a mug. Completed in 1965, it commemorates the westward expansion and Lewis and Clark. The grey interior matches that gleaming steel skin, and the clean geometry makes this one of the more graphically elegant cups in the series.
Calgary#576514 · You Are Here CollectionCalgary gets a red interior, the downtown towers, and a ferris wheel that nods to the city's signature event, the Calgary Stampede, billed as the greatest outdoor show on earth since 1912. This Alberta boomtown sits in the foothills of the Rockies and rode the oil economy to its glassy skyline. A spirited band for Canada's cowboy-meets-corporate capital.
Istanbul#576515 · You Are Here CollectionIstanbul wraps the Bosphorus and the Hagia Sophia in red, the city that famously straddles Europe and Asia across that strait. The Hagia Sophia has served as cathedral, mosque, museum, and mosque again across nearly 1,500 years. Turkish You Are Here mugs are a deep, collectible sub-series. A striking piece anchored by one of the most history-soaked buildings on the planet.
Hawaii#576516 · You Are Here CollectionHawaii forgoes a skyline entirely for a rainbow arcing over mountains and trees, which is perfect since the Aloha State is literally the Rainbow State, with rainbows on its license plates. The light blue interior reads as sky and sea. A calm, nature-first design that stands apart from the urban entries, and a steady favorite among collectors who chase the island pieces.
Tennessee#576517 · You Are Here CollectionA train and mountains on green is a smart read of Tennessee, with the Great Smoky Mountains being the most visited national park in the country and Chattanooga's famous Choo Choo immortalized in the 1941 big-band hit. The state stretches from the Appalachians to the Mississippi, so a railroad threading the hills captures its breadth. A statewide YAH like this is handy for collectors who fill the map by state rather than city.
California#576518 · You Are Here CollectionThe California state mug goes light blue and skips any one city for the Golden State's wild backbone: mountains, towering trees, and a low sun. Those trees evoke the giant sequoias and coast redwoods, the tallest and most massive living things on earth, sheltered in Yosemite, Sequoia and Redwood parks. A statewide YAH that sells the idea of California as landscape rather than skyline.
Charlotte#576519 · You Are Here CollectionCharlotte takes a green interior with the uptown skyline and a racing car, a direct nod to the NASCAR Hall of Fame that sits downtown and the sport's heartland in the Carolinas. North Carolina's largest city is a banking powerhouse second only to New York, crowned by the crown-topped Bank of America Corporate Center. A clean band that balances finance towers with stock-car heritage.
North Carolina#576521 · You Are Here CollectionNorth Carolina in light blue, a lighthouse and a bird out front. The lighthouse is the black-and-white spiral of Cape Hatteras on the Outer Banks, the tallest brick lighthouse in the United States, and the bird is the cardinal, the state bird. The Tar Heel State design quietly celebrates the wild barrier-island coastline rather than Charlotte or the Research Triangle.
Houston#576522 · You Are Here CollectionHouston with a longhorn bull beside the skyline ties Texas swagger to Space City, home of NASA's Mission Control. The brown interior suits the cattle theme. It is a nice balance, the energy capital of the nation getting both its corporate towers and a nod to ranching heritage. A solid, characterful entry from the Lone Star State.
Singapore#576523 · You Are Here CollectionThe green interior and Changi tower plus skyline capture a city-state that turned its airport into a destination, with Jewel Changi's indoor waterfall now a landmark in its own right. The design also gathers the Merlion, the Raffles statue, and the Marina Bay skyline. Singapore drives hard on the secondary market because the country's Starbucks merchandise has a devoted following, and this YAH is a frequent target for Asia-route collectors.
Vail#576524 · You Are Here CollectionVail in Christmas with pine trees is a resort-town YAH, capturing Colorado's largest ski mountain, which opened in 1962 and was modeled on an alpine Bavarian village right down to the pedestrian streets. The light blue interior and snowy pines lean fully into the winter wonderland pitch. Mountain resort mugs like this come from low-volume stores, so they tend to be a bit harder to find than the big-city entries.
Austin#576525 · You Are Here CollectionAustin gets a red interior and a city center crowned with that unmistakable cowboy boot, a wink at the Texas capital's "Keep Austin Weird" live-music identity. The half moon is a sly nod to the famous moonlight towers, the 1890s carbon-arc lamps that still glow over the city and that no other place in the world kept. Home of South by Southwest and the bats under Congress Avenue Bridge, it earns its quirky band.
The Hamptons#576526 · You Are Here CollectionA seagull, a kite, and a shingled house perfectly evoke the Hamptons, the string of well-heeled beach villages on Long Island's South Fork that empty out Manhattan every summer weekend. The weathered grey-shingle cottage is the regional architectural signature, and the brown interior reads like sand and driftwood. A YAH for a resort area rather than a city is unusual, which makes this one a slightly offbeat pickup for a set.
Orlando#576528 · You Are Here CollectionOrlando in deep yellow, buildings topped with an orange and ringed by palm trees. The literal orange is a pun on the citrus that built Central Florida and gave nearby Orange County its name, while the city itself is of course the theme-park capital, home to Walt Disney World and Universal. A cheerful, sun-baked mug that knows exactly why people fly into Orlando.
Las Vegas#576529 · You Are Here CollectionLas Vegas leads with the iconic Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign and the Strip, in bright red. Betty Willis designed that 1959 sign and never copyrighted it, which is why it appears everywhere. The mug captures Sin City's neon glamour in one glance. A popular, easy-to-love entry that practically every traveler recognizes the moment they pick it up.
Pittsburgh#576530 · You Are Here CollectionPittsburgh earned the nickname City of Bridges with more than 440 of them, more than any other city on earth, so it is fitting that this yellow-lined mug crams the river spans across the outside. The skyline shows off the confluence of the Allegheny, Monongahela, and Ohio rivers at the Golden Triangle. I love that the design leans on infrastructure instead of a single tower, which is honest to how Pittsburgh actually feels when you cross those gold-painted bridges downtown.
New Mexico#576531 · You Are Here CollectionNew Mexico in light blue, adobe old towns under a sky full of hot air balloons. The balloons are unmistakably the Albuquerque International Balloon Fiesta, the largest hot air balloon event in the world, where hundreds launch en masse each October. The adobe nods to Santa Fe and Taos, the Land of Enchantment's distinctive Pueblo Revival architecture. One of the more visually instant state mugs in the series.
Montreal#576532 · You Are Here CollectionMontreal with a red interior, the skyline paired with a guitar. The guitar honors the city's huge live-music reputation, anchored by the Montreal International Jazz Festival, the largest jazz festival on earth, and its long roster of homegrown talent from Leonard Cohen onward. Red is the obvious nod to Quebec's hot summer festival season packing the downtown streets.
Denver#576533 · You Are Here CollectionDenver takes a light blue interior with the city sitting below the Rockies, the Mile High City that sits exactly 5,280 feet above sea level. The Front Range backdrop is the whole point here, gateway to Colorado's ski country and the wide western plains meeting the mountains. A calm, scenic band that lets the mountains do the talking.
Aspen#576535 · You Are Here CollectionThe Aspen entry in the You Are Here series, dated 2017, with mountains and ski gear over a light blue interior. Aspen is the silver-mining town turned world-famous ski resort in Colorado's Rockies, and collectors often pair this with the Vail mug to complete the Colorado ski set. Since the YAH line was retired and replaced by the Been There collection, these 2017-dated pieces are the tail end of the series.
Seattle#576537 · You Are Here CollectionThis is the hometown mug, Seattle being where Starbucks opened at Pike Place in 1971, so the skyline with the Space Needle carries extra weight for any collector. The Needle was built for the 1962 World's Fair and stands 605 feet tall. The light blue interior nods to Puget Sound and those rare clear days when Rainier floats on the horizon. If you build a You Are Here set, this is the spiritual anchor.
Arizona#576540 · You Are Here CollectionThe Arizona mug from the You Are Here line, a saguaro cactus and a blazing Arizona sun over a dark yellow interior. That sun is no accident, Arizona is the sunniest state in the country and the saguaro is the giant cactus found almost nowhere else, growing only in the Sonoran Desert. A warm, instantly readable design that captures the Grand Canyon State without needing the canyon itself.
Detroit#576541 · You Are Here CollectionDetroit earns its dark yellow interior and that wrapped trio of skyline, beer, and a vinyl record, because this is Motown, the birthplace of Berry Gordy's sound and the assembly-line city Henry Ford built. I love that the designers leaned into music here rather than just cars, putting a spinning record front and center. A proper Motor City piece that nails the city's two great exports, automobiles and rhythm.
Phoenix#576542 · You Are Here CollectionPhoenix in orange, a saguaro cactus, a lizard and the sun blazing over mountains. The towering saguaro is the signature of the Sonoran Desert that wraps the Valley of the Sun, and Phoenix is famous for being one of the hottest big cities in America. The orange interior practically radiates that desert heat. A mug that captures the Southwest at a glance.
Dallas#576543 · You Are Here CollectionDallas goes yellow with a football, a longhorn bull, and a sun riding over the skyline, three Texas icons in one band. The football salutes the Dallas Cowboys, "America's Team," while the longhorn is pure Lone Star State. Reunion Tower's geodesic ball anchors the skyline of this oil-and-finance powerhouse, making for a big, brash, unmistakably Texan piece.
New Jersey#576544 · You Are Here CollectionNew Jersey in red, a theme park and a Ferris wheel out front. The big wheel references the Jersey Shore boardwalks and, later, the Dream Wheel at American Dream, while the wider design pulls in Ellis Island, the George Washington Bridge and Atlantic City. A fun state piece that trades a skyline for the boardwalk amusements people actually associate with the Garden State.
Izmir#576546 · You Are Here CollectionIzmir centers the Saat Kulesi clock tower flanked by two palms, with sea waves and seagulls hinting at the Aegean coast. This is Turkey's third-largest city and its second-busiest port, the ancient Smyrna. The 1901 Ottoman clock tower in Konak Square is the city's defining emblem. Part of the well-collected Turkish run, and a graceful, breezy design that captures a Mediterranean port.
Orange County#576547 · You Are Here CollectionOrange County in yellow, a beachfront skyline with palm trees and golf gear. This is the Southern California of Newport and Huntington Beach, the latter trademarked as Surf City USA, paired with the region's famous championship golf. The yellow interior soaks in the perpetual sunshine. A nice example of the series carving out a county rather than a single city.
Cannes#576548 · You Are Here CollectionCannes goes deep blue with the Riviera beachfront, yachts, grand hotels along La Croisette, and a strip of film reel, because the Cannes Film Festival has been the town's identity since 1946. The artists even tucked in the red carpet that marks the stars' walk up the steps of the Palais. Released around 2016, it is a glamorous, instantly legible French piece for the festival faithful.
Vancouver#576549 · You Are Here CollectionThe cityline with an orca is exactly right for Vancouver, where the resident and transient killer whales of the Salish Sea are a regional emblem and a major draw. The skyline sits between ocean and the North Shore mountains, one of the few cities where you can ski and sail in the same day. The light blue interior suits all that water, and it pairs naturally with the Vancouver Island mug for a British Columbia pair.
Japan#576550 · You Are Here CollectionJapan distills the whole country into Mount Fuji rising over a sunrise wreathed in sakura, in deep red. Fuji-san is the sacred 3,776-meter peak, and cherry blossom marks the brief spring hanami season the Japanese treasure. This nationwide piece is a perennial favorite, blending the country's two most beloved natural symbols. A beautifully restrained, instantly recognizable design.
Banff#576551 · You Are Here CollectionBanff carries a green interior, the alpine town nestled below the Rockies, and ski boots for the slopes at Sunshine and Lake Louise. Banff National Park is Canada's oldest, born in 1885 after railway workers stumbled on the Cave and Basin hot springs, which launched the entire Canadian parks system. Collectors note the Banff pieces run somewhat hard to find, a nice catch in any YAH lineup.
Vancouver Island#576552 · You Are Here CollectionMountains, a sailboat, and an orca on green capture Vancouver Island, the rugged Pacific landmass that holds Victoria, the province's capital, and some of the best whale-watching waters in the world. The island is large enough to swallow several countries and is famed for old-growth rainforest and storm-watching at Tofino. This is the natural companion to the Vancouver city mug, and the regional YAH format makes the pair a nice British Columbia bookend.
San Antonio#576553 · You Are Here CollectionRemember the Alamo: the buildings and Texan flag wrapping this red-lined mug honor the 1836 mission siege that became a Texas rallying cry. San Antonio is equally famous for its River Walk, the winding network of stone paths and bridges below street level. The Lone Star flag and bold red interior give it real Texas swagger, and it pairs naturally with the broader Texas mug if you collect by state.
Ohio#576554 · You Are Here CollectionOhio in red, the Capitol building beside a tree and a red bird. That bird is the cardinal, Ohio's state bird, and the building is the Greek Revival Statehouse in Columbus, one of the oldest working state capitols in the country. The Buckeye State piece keeps it civic and simple, a clean little portrait of the heartland.
Nashville#576555 · You Are Here CollectionNashville in grey, the skyline studded with a guitar and stars. This is Music City, home of the Grand Ole Opry and the Country Music Hall of Fame, and the honky-tonks of Lower Broadway. The stars hint at the Nashville flag and the city's status as the recording capital where Music Row's studios shaped American country. The guitar needs no explaining here.
Amsterdam#576556 · You Are Here CollectionThe Amsterdam entry in the You Are Here series, its light blue interior framing the canal boats and gabled canal houses that define the Dutch capital. Those concentric 17th century canals are a UNESCO World Heritage site, and the narrow tilting houses lean because they were built tall and slim to dodge frontage taxes. A clean European YAH that captures exactly what you picture when you think of the city.
Toronto#576557 · You Are Here CollectionThe skyline here is anchored by the CN Tower, which stood as the world's tallest free-standing structure for over thirty years at 1,815 feet, and the hockey stick is a wink at Toronto being home to the Hockey Hall of Fame and the Maple Leafs. The red interior matches the Canadian flag. As the merch hub of English Canada, this is one of the more available Canadian YAH mugs and a natural cornerstone for a Canada subset.
New Orleans#576559 · You Are Here CollectionNew Orleans in brown, the French Quarter with a horse and carriage clip-clopping past. The design captures the wrought-iron balconies and Creole townhouses of the Vieux Carré, the oldest neighborhood in the city, plus the mule-drawn carriages that still tour Jackson Square. Warm brown suits a town that runs on coffee and chicory and the lazy heat of the Quarter.
Indianapolis#576560 · You Are Here CollectionIndianapolis with a racing car is the only sensible choice, since the city is synonymous with the Indianapolis 500 and the Brickyard, run every Memorial Day weekend since 1911. The brown inside reads as track and engine. I appreciate how instantly legible this one is, you do not need the word Indy, the car says it all. A clean motorsport tribute.
New York#576563 · You Are Here CollectionNew York with a bright yellow interior, the obvious nod to the city's taxis, skyline and bridges wrapped around the cup. You get the Manhattan towers, the suspension cables of the Brooklyn Bridge and a yellow cab, the holy trinity of NYC shorthand. The yellow inside is a small designer flourish that makes this one of the most recognizable mugs in the whole line.
Cambridge#576564 · You Are Here CollectionCambridge takes a light brown interior with the city skyline and its punts and spires, home to one of the oldest universities in the world, founded in 1209. The pinnacled chapel that dominates the band is King's College Chapel, the masterpiece of English Gothic fan vaulting begun under Henry VI. Newton, Darwin and the discovery of DNA's structure all trace here, making this a quietly heavyweight English piece.
Quebec#576566 · You Are Here CollectionThe castle here is the Chateau Frontenac, the grand railway hotel towering over Old Quebec and often called the most photographed hotel in the world. The wing-spread owl is a lovely Quebec touch, the snowy owl being the official bird of the province. Quebec City is the only walled city north of Mexico, and the grey interior suits its fortress stone and long winters. A clean, atmospheric Canadian piece.
Florida#576567 · You Are Here CollectionThe whole Sunshine State on one mug, with palm trees, a beaming sun, and a bright orange against yellow. Florida is the citrus capital and famously America's flattest state, which is why the design leans on beaches and produce rather than a skyline. I like that this is the statewide piece rather than a single city, a nice catch-all for the peninsula.
Epcot#576568 · You Are Here CollectionOne of the crown jewels of the series, Epcot wraps Walt Disney World's geodesic Spaceship Earth and the park's World Showcase pavilions in light purple. Collectors prize the early Epcot release with the purple monorail, which Starbucks pulled quickly, and clean examples have fetched well over a hundred dollars on the secondary market. A genuine theme-park grail and a must-have for any You Are Here set.
San Francisco#576570 · You Are Here CollectionThe Golden Gate Bridge through grey clouds is pure San Francisco honesty, since the bridge is famously swallowed by fog the locals nickname Karl. Opened in 1937, its International Orange color was chosen partly to stay visible in exactly that mist. The red interior contrasts beautifully with the moody exterior, and San Francisco is one of the more common and beloved You Are Here mugs, a great everyday cup that still reads as iconic.
Kansas City#576571 · You Are Here CollectionKansas City pairs the skyline with a basketball and a bridge in red, a nod to the city's deep hoops and jazz roots and its many fountains and bridges. KC famously claims more boulevards than Paris and more fountains than any city but Rome. I like that it reaches past barbecue for something less expected. A lively Midwestern entry with real local texture.
Washington, D.C.#576574 · You Are Here CollectionWashington, D.C., grey inside, with the national monuments and the White House marching around the outside. The grey interior is a nice touch, echoing the marble and granite of the Mall, the Washington Monument obelisk, the Capitol dome, and the Lincoln Memorial. This is the capital piece, distinct from the Washington State mug, and the two side by side make a fun teaching moment for anyone who confuses the city with the state.
Canada#576576 · You Are Here CollectionThe Canada country mug runs red, the national color, with wildlife and maple leaves spread over mountains. It trades a single city for the whole vast nation, the maple leaf lifted straight from the flag adopted in 1965. A broad, friendly band that pairs naturally with the city-specific Canadian YAHs like Banff and Calgary in a collection.
Bodrum#576577 · You Are Here CollectionBodrum goes light pink with a sun setting over the waves and the hillside of whitewashed cubic houses tumbling down to the Aegean. This was ancient Halicarnassus, home to the Mausoleum that gave us the very word and counted among the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. The piece centers on Bodrum Castle, the 15th-century crusader fortress on the harbor, and it sells in the 40 to 75 dollar range as part of Starbucks' broad Turkey push.
Los Angeles#576578 · You Are Here CollectionLos Angeles teams the skyline with a film camera, the only honest choice for the home of Hollywood and the global movie industry. The light brown interior reads like California sun. I enjoy that the camera does the heavy lifting, telling you exactly which city this is without a single palm or freeway. A clean, confident tribute to the entertainment capital.
Portland#576579 · You Are Here CollectionMount Hood looming over a green interior with bicycles is exactly right for Portland, a city that consistently ranks as one of the most bike-friendly in America with its protected lanes and bike boulevards. Hood is Oregon's tallest peak at 11,249 feet and a dormant stratovolcano you can see from downtown on a clear day. The green glaze is a nice nod to Portland's relentlessly leafy, keep-it-weird self-image.
Melbourne#576580 · You Are Here CollectionMelbourne with a dark blue interior and a skyline trimmed by a cable car, the artist's shorthand for the city's beloved trams. Melbourne runs the largest tram network in the world, and the free City Circle heritage trams in burgundy and gold are a tourist icon. A quietly clever choice, since the tram, not a tower, is what Melburnians point to first.
Copenhagen#576581 · You Are Here CollectionCopenhagen takes a yellow interior with the Nyhavn canal, its candy-colored 17th-century townhouses, and a wooden boat at the quay. The Danish capital is the home of Hans Christian Andersen, Tivoli Gardens, and the Little Mermaid statue, consistently ranked among the world's most livable and bike-friendly cities. A cheerful, sunlit band that captures Nyhavn, the city's most photographed waterfront.
Paris#576582 · You Are Here CollectionParis in dark blue, the city's famous monuments marching around the cup. Expect the Eiffel Tower, built for the 1889 World's Fair and once meant to be temporary, alongside the Arc de Triomphe and Notre-Dame. The deep blue interior gives it an evening, City of Light feel. A flagship international piece that almost every collector wants in the set.
Philadelphia#576585 · You Are Here CollectionPhiladelphia in red, a cannon set over the city skyline. The cannon and red nod to the city's Revolutionary War heritage, the birthplace of the Declaration of Independence and home to Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell. Philly was briefly the capital of the young United States. A history-forward design that leans on the nation's founding rather than the cheesesteaks.
Chicago#576588 · You Are Here CollectionChicago runs an orange-creme interior with the skyline and an elevated train, the famous "L" loop that gives downtown its name. The towers nod to the city that invented the modern skyscraper after the Great Fire of 1871, from the Willis Tower to the John Hancock. A warm, distinctive band for the Windy City that earns its place in any American YAH run.
Dubai#576589 · You Are Here CollectionThe light blue inside and that palm tree against the skyline point straight at Dubai's signature ambition, the Palm Jumeirah man-made islands and the Burj Khalifa, still the tallest building on earth at 828 meters. This is one of the more sought-after Middle East You Are Here pieces because Gulf-region mugs were sold in fewer stores. A clean, confident desert-glamour design.
Hong Kong#576590 · You Are Here CollectionHong Kong goes full food culture with dumplings, soup, and a boat over the mountains and harbor bridge, in a bold red. This is dim sum territory and Victoria Harbour, one of the world's great deep-water ports. I love that the designers chose the table over the towers, celebrating the city's legendary eating rather than just its famous skyline. A vivid, appetite-stirring piece.
Macau#576591 · You Are Here CollectionMacau combines the skyline, a bridge, and the golden Lotus Flower sculpture in light blue, all spot-on for the former Portuguese colony and the world's biggest gambling hub. The Lotus Flower Square monument commemorates the 1999 handover to China, and the bridge nods to the spans linking the peninsula to its islands. A handsome, layered design celebrating a tiny place with an outsized story.
Pike Place Market#576592 · You Are Here CollectionPike Place Market in brown, fronted by the original Starbucks storefront. This is the holy grail location for the brand, the 1971 first store at 1912 Pike Place beside the famous market sign and clock, the one shop still carrying the old brown siren logo. For a Starbucks collector this is close to sacred ground, the You Are Here mug for the very spot the company was born. Brown suits the heritage perfectly.
Australia#576593 · You Are Here CollectionThe Australia country mug goes green inside and leans into the icons every visitor pictures: a koala hugging a eucalyptus over the red Outback landscape. Starbucks built whole national YAH pieces for the big tourist countries, and this one trades a single skyline for the continent's wildlife and bush. A warm, instantly readable piece that reads as the whole Down Under in one band.
Madrid#576596 · You Are Here CollectionMadrid in the You Are Here series, green inside, wrapped in a skyline that nods to the Spanish capital's grand boulevards. The bear shaking a tree is the city's own emblem, El Oso y el Madroño, the bear and the strawberry tree that stands in bronze at Puerta del Sol and appears on Madrid's coat of arms. A nice example of the designers building a mug around a single local symbol rather than just a generic cityscape.
Miami#576597 · You Are Here CollectionMiami in light blue, all beach, sun and a speedboat skimming the bay. The design leans into South Beach and the Art Deco district along Ocean Drive, the densest concentration of 1920s and 30s Deco architecture anywhere. The speedboat is pure Miami Vice swagger, a fitting wink for a city built on its waterfront and its nightlife.
Edmonton#576600 · You Are Here CollectionEdmonton with band instruments outside is a fun call, nodding to Alberta's capital and its reputation as Canada's Festival City, home to one of the world's largest fringe theatre festivals. The brown interior grounds it. I always smile that Starbucks skipped the obvious West Edmonton Mall reference and went musical instead. A quieter Canadian entry that rewards a collector who knows the city.
Alaska#576602 · You Are Here CollectionFrom the You Are Here travel series launched in 2013, this 14oz Alaska mug sets a moose and a steamboat against mountains over a dark blue interior. The riverboat nods to the gold-rush stern-wheelers that once worked the Yukon, while the moose is the unofficial face of the wild Last Frontier. State-wide YAH mugs are a little unusual since most in the line are single cities, which makes the Alaska piece a satisfying catch.
Waikiki#576603 · You Are Here CollectionWaikiki, not Honolulu, gets its own You Are Here mug, green inside with the beachfront and a green pineapple outside. Waikiki is the legendary crescent of sand below Diamond Head crater where modern surfing went global under Duke Kahanamoku, and the pineapple is Hawaii's enduring plantation emblem. I love that Starbucks singled out a single famous beach rather than the whole island, which makes this one of the more specific destinations in the whole series.
Colorado#576604 · You Are Here CollectionThe Colorado state mug goes green and is one of the busiest YAH bands going: mountains, a campfire, a mountain bike, tents, and jet fighters streaking overhead. Those jets salute the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, while the rest sells the outdoor-recreation paradise of the Rockies. A dense, story-packed piece that rewards a close look around the cup.
Boston#576605 · You Are Here CollectionBoston takes a deep blue interior with a skyline pierced by an obelisk, the Bunker Hill Monument that commemorates the 1775 Revolutionary battle. This is the cradle of American independence, the Freedom Trail city of Paul Revere and the Tea Party, threaded through with the brick rowhouses of Beacon Hill. A dark, dignified band that suits the country's most history-soaked town.
Lake Tahoe#576607 · You Are Here CollectionLake Tahoe loads up on mountains, ski gear, a bike, and the lake with its island and trees, perfect for the alpine playground straddling California and Nevada. Tahoe is the largest alpine lake in North America and famously clear and deep. The lone island depicted is Fannette, the lake's only island. A four-season outdoor scene that makes you want to plan a trip.
Prague#576609 · You Are Here CollectionThe towers and castle over a long bridge are Prague's signature view, the Charles Bridge marching across the Vltava toward Prague Castle, the largest ancient castle complex in the world by area. The bridge dates to 1357 under Charles IV and is guarded by thirty Baroque statues. The red interior plays off the terracotta rooftops of the Old Town, and as a single-store You Are Here from a city with limited Starbucks presence, it is a satisfying one to track down.
Hamburg#576610 · You Are Here CollectionHamburg with a grand train station, a traveler hauling two bags, and the skyline in red is a lovely nod to Germany's biggest port city and its major rail hub. The skyline features the Elbphilharmonie concert hall, Hamburg's wave-roofed landmark that opened in 2017. I enjoy the storytelling here, the wandering passenger giving the mug a sense of motion most city pieces lack.
Gold Coast#576611 · You Are Here CollectionGold Coast pairs a high-rise skyline with a beach scene and a rollercoaster, exactly right for Queensland's tourist playground. This is Surfers Paradise, with world-class breaks and the theme-park cluster of Movie World and Dreamworld inland. Australian You Are Here mugs are harder to source outside the country and command a premium when boxed. A sunny, energetic design that captures the city's holiday spirit.
Thailand#576613 · You Are Here CollectionThis yellow-lined mug gathers the Grand Palace, floating Loi Krathong lanterns on the river, and the Bangkok skyline, a genuinely rich composition. The Grand Palace was the royal residence from 1782 and houses the revered Emerald Buddha. Yellow is the auspicious royal color of Thailand, tied to Monday and the late King Bhumibol, so the interior choice is more deliberate than it first appears. A layered, beautiful country mug.
Brisbane#576614 · You Are Here CollectionBrisbane runs red inside with the river-city skyline and that ferris wheel, the Wheel of Brisbane installed on the South Bank for the 2008 anniversary of the World Expo 88. Queensland's subtropical capital threads its brown river through downtown, and the band captures the riverside parklands and high-rises that define it. A bright, easy Australian piece beyond the usual Sydney suspects.
Berlin#576615 · You Are Here CollectionBerlin runs grey inside with the city's bear mascot posed before the Reichstag, the 1894 parliament building famously crowned by Norman Foster's glass dome after reunification. The bear is no accident: it has been Berlin's heraldic symbol for centuries and even names the Berlinale film festival's Golden Bear. A restrained, history-heavy band for a capital defined by reinvention.
Oregon#576616 · You Are Here CollectionOregon in light blue, a great waterfall over wild scenery with a trail bike. The falls labeled here are Multnomah Falls in the Columbia River Gorge, the state's tallest at 620 feet, crossed by the photogenic Benson Bridge. Worth noting Starbucks once famously botched a separate Oregon travel mug by mislabeling its landmarks, so collectors watch Oregon pieces closely. This You Are Here version leans into the rugged outdoors the state is loved for.
Pretoria#576617 · You Are Here CollectionThis one packs in Pretoria's Union Buildings, the sandstone seat of South Africa's government and the spot where Mandela was inaugurated in 1994, plus a giraffe, a jacaranda tree, and even a tiny rugby goal nodding to the Springboks. Pretoria is famous as the Jacaranda City for the thousands of purple blooms that take over every October, which the purple-cream interior captures perfectly. With only a handful of Starbucks in South Africa, this is a genuinely hard mug to source and collectors pay up for it.
Cyprus#576618 · You Are Here CollectionCyprus runs light blue with beach umbrellas, a dove over a green patch, blue and white being the island's everyday colors. Part of Starbucks' push to cover Europe's countries, this Mediterranean island is steeped in Aphrodite myth, its Paphos sites a UNESCO treasure. Collectors trade Cyprus alongside the rarer Limassol variant, and the design deliberately echoes the Greek YAH look.
Sydney#576619 · You Are Here CollectionSydney's CBD on a light blue interior gives you the harbour city, and while the catalog calls out the business district you can expect the Opera House sails and Harbour Bridge in the lineup, the two most photographed structures in Australia.
