The Opera House opened in 1973 and is a UNESCO World Heritage site. The blue glaze evokes that brilliant harbour water, making this a bright, instantly recognizable Pacific entry.
Wisconsin#576621 · You Are Here CollectionWisconsin, green inside, celebrating exactly what you would hope, the State Capitol, cheeses, and dairy farms outside. America's Dairyland leans hard into its identity here, and rightly so, Wisconsin produces more cheese than any other state and the Capitol in Madison has the only granite dome of any U.S. statehouse. The cheese wedges make this one of the most cheerfully on the nose mugs in my You Are Here run.
San Diego#576622 · You Are Here CollectionThe bridge here is the San Diego to Coronado Bay Bridge, that dramatic curving span rising 200 feet so Navy ships can pass beneath, arcing toward the embarcadero waterfront. San Diego is a Navy town with near-perfect weather year round, and the dark blue interior leans into its Pacific identity. A solid Southern California piece that rewards a closer look at the skyline detail.
Washington#576623 · You Are Here CollectionWashington State, red inside, with mountains, a ferry, a fish, and an apple ringing the outside. Every icon earns its place here, the Cascades and Mount Rainier, the green and white Washington State Ferries that are the largest ferry system in the country, the leaping salmon of the Northwest, and the apple from the orchards that make Washington America's top apple grower. As the home state of Starbucks itself, this one always feels like the company's hometown piece.
Atlanta#576627 · You Are Here CollectionMy Atlanta You Are Here runs a light blue interior and packs in the things the city actually claims: a peach for the Peach State, a stock car nodding to NASCAR's deep Georgia roots and the old Atlanta Motor Speedway, and a skyline anchored by the pointed Bank of America Plaza. It is the city of Coca-Cola and the world's busiest airport, and the YAH artists distilled all that Southern hustle onto one band.
MünchenYou Are HereMünchen, Munich, in the You Are Here series, dated to the 2016 run made for Germany. The design built around the Bavarian capital plays up Oktoberfest themes, the New Town Hall with its famous Glockenspiel on Marienplatz, a Maß stein of beer and the local Weißwurst. A satisfying piece because it commits fully to Munich's beer-hall identity rather than a flat skyline.
Niagara FallsYou Are HereNiagara Falls in the You Are Here series, a wraparound of the cataracts themselves. The art takes in Horseshoe Falls, the largest of the three and shared with Canada, plus Bridal Veil Falls and the Rainbow Bridge linking the two countries. Roughly six million cubic feet of water tip over the crest every minute. A rare mug for a natural wonder rather than a city, which makes it a nice outlier on the shelf.
Classification

The Architecture Series123 pieces

City skylines reduced to a single continuous line, plus the demitasse minis.
Set of Two#186048 · Global Icon SeriesThis three ounce duo brackets two northeastern Chinese cities that rarely share a shelf, Shenyang, the old Manchu imperial capital with its UNESCO listed Mukden Palace, and Qingdao, the seaside brewery town the Germans built and home to Tsingtao beer. China specific demitasse pairs like this skew toward Asian market distribution, so they surface less often in Western collections.
Set of Two#186049 · Global Icon SeriesA boxed pair of 3oz Global Collectible demitasse cups pairing China with Qingdao. Qingdao is famous for the Tsingtao Brewery, founded in 1903 under German rule, and for the Huilan Pavilion at the end of Zhanqiao Pier that still appears on every Tsingtao bottle. Its red roofed German colonial old town and annual beer festival make it one of China's most distinctive coastal cities.
Set of Two#186052 · Global Icon SeriesA scarcer pairing, Sofia matched with Bulgaria, two three ounce espresso cups from the Architecture demitasse line. Sofia is one of Europe's oldest cities, crowned by the gold domed Alexander Nevsky Cathedral, while the national cup nods to Bulgaria broadly. Eastern European demitasse pairs had thin distribution, so a complete Sofia set is a genuinely uncommon find on the secondary market.
Set of Two#186053 · Global Icon SeriesA two cup boxed set of 3oz Global Collectible espresso demitasse, pairing Athens with Greece. Athens is the cradle of Western civilization, crowned by the Parthenon on the Acropolis and the birthplace of democracy, philosophy, and the Olympic Games. These global pairings were sold as matched twos, so an intact box with both cups is what collectors actually chase rather than singles split apart.
Set of Two#186054 · Global Icon SeriesTwo matching Singapore espresso minis, a city state so compact that the city and the country are the same line, which is why both cups read Singapore. Expect the Merlion, the lion headed fish that is the official mascot, and the Marina Bay skyline. I keep the set boxed, because these small format cups chip easily and a clean matched pair holds value far better than a single.
Set of Two#186055 · Global Icon SeriesA pair of three ounce espresso minis pairing Paris with France, part of the Architecture Series demitasse run that boxed two complementary pours together. The city cup leans on Paris staples, the Eiffel Tower and the Seine, while the national mate carries broader French motifs. Collectors prize these sets intact, since a single orphaned mini is far easier to find than the matched two.
Set of Two#186056 · Global Icon SeriesA two cup 3oz Global Collectible demitasse set linking Buenos Aires with Argentina. The Paris of South America is the home of tango, the wide Avenida 9 de Julio with its towering Obelisco, the colorful houses of La Boca, and the pink Casa Rosada. As a matched box of two espresso cups, the appeal for collectors is having the city and country pair survive intact.
Set of Two#186059 · Global Icon SeriesA boxed pair of 3oz Global Collectible demitasse cups joining Beijing with its port neighbor Tianjin. Beijing carries the Forbidden City, Tiananmen Square, the Temple of Heaven, and the Great Wall snaking through its hills, while Tianjin is the historic treaty port and gateway on the Bohai coast. The two city pairing format is a quiet hallmark of the global demitasse line, best kept boxed and together.
Set of Two#186060 · Global Icon SeriesA two cup 3oz Global Collectible demitasse set joining Hong Kong with China. Hong Kong delivers one of the planet's great skylines, the neon crowded harbor of Victoria, the Star Ferry, the tram up to Victoria Peak, and a dense vertical city where East meets West. Sold as a matched pair, these little espresso cups are most desirable as a sealed or complete boxed two.
Set of Two#186061 · Global Icon SeriesSydney paired with Australia in matched three ounce form, the city cup fronted by the Opera House sails and the Harbour Bridge coathanger, the national mate carrying wider Aussie motifs. The Sydney and Australia ornament demi set still trades as a unit among collectors, which tells you the value is in keeping the two together rather than splitting them.
Demitasse United Arab Emirates#186065 · Global Icon SeriesA 3oz Global Collectible espresso mug for the UAE, the federation of seven emirates anchored by Abu Dhabi and Dubai. The country is the home of the Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world at 828 meters, and the sail-shaped Burj Al Arab. Country-level Global minis like this are tidier to collect than the sprawling city series, since one piece stands in for the whole nation.
Demitasse Stanley#186069 · Global Icon SeriesStanley is the seaside village on the southern tip of Hong Kong Island, famous for its waterfront promenade, the lively Stanley Market, and the colonial-era Murray House that was dismantled in Central and rebuilt brick by brick here. This 3oz espresso mini comes from the Hong Kong Collector Series, and the little Stanley, Star Ferry and Peak trio is the one local set Hong Kong collectors hunt to complete intact.
Demitasse Starferry#186070 · Global Icon SeriesThe Star Ferry has crossed Victoria Harbour since 1888, and its green and white double-deckers between Central and Tsim Sha Tsui are still one of the cheapest world-class harbor rides on earth. National Geographic once named it among the planet's most thrilling trips. I love that a working commuter boat earned its own 3oz mini in the Hong Kong demitasse set alongside The Peak and Stanley.
Demitasse The Peak#186073 · Global Icon SeriesVictoria Peak is Hong Kong's highest point and its signature view, reached since 1888 by the gravity-defying Peak Tram and crowned by the wok-shaped Peak Tower lookout. This 3oz espresso piece is part of the Hong Kong Collector Series demitasse run, and on the secondary market the Peak mini tends to be the easiest of the three to find, which makes Stanley the real holdup when you are chasing the full local trio.
Set of Five#186081 · Global Icon SeriesA boxed Indonesian set of five 3oz City Mug Collector Series demitasse cups, a regional grouping rather than a single city. Indonesia matters deeply to coffee history, home to Sumatra and Java, the latter so central that Java became slang for coffee itself. Complete sealed sets of five are far scarcer than loose cups, since the value lives in keeping all five together with the original packaging.
Demitasse Sakura#186084 · The Architecture SeriesA sakura demitasse, two pink cherry blossom leaves inside and a scatter of petals across the outside, the cherry blossom being Japan's most beloved seasonal symbol and the heart of Starbucks' annual sakura craze. Spring sakura releases sell out fast in Japan every year and drive some of the most frantic collecting in the whole hobby. This little espresso piece carries that hanami spirit in miniature and pairs beautifully with any Japan line items.
2000, Blue Espresso#186089 · The Architecture SeriesA 2000 espresso demitasse, white inside with a blue ribbon band, blue outside. These tiny 3oz cups from the turn of the millennium are the quiet workhorses of any serious Starbucks shelf, made for a single pull of espresso the proper Italian way. The simple blue ribbon detailing dates it cleanly to that early-2000s house style before the splashier themed demitasses arrived, and small unfussy pieces like this are easy to overlook and harder to find boxed.
Last Logo#186090 · The Architecture SeriesA quiet oddity in the set, this espresso demitasse drops the city theme entirely and simply carries the Last Logo outside over white. Collectors use Last Logo to mean the final pre-2011 siren wordmark, the green circle that still read Starbucks Coffee around the mermaid before the 2011 redesign stripped the text and freed the siren from her ring. As a plain branded mini it is more of a series anchor than a showpiece, but I like it as a dated marker of exactly when Starbucks changed its face.
Welcome to Hamburg#186091 · The Architecture SeriesA Welcome to Hamburg espresso demitasse, white inside with the city greeting and the red Siren on the outside. The red mermaid finish marks this as a German market piece, and the welcome-and-Siren styling sits apart from the standard skyline minis. Hamburg is Germany's great port city on the Elbe, famous for its sprawling harbor and the Speicherstadt warehouse district, so a quick welcome cup suits a trading town built on coming and going.
Dog On Slay#186094 · The Architecture SeriesThe name is a charming misspelling of "dog on sleigh," and this little espresso piece carries the boy and dog sledding holiday artwork Starbucks ran around 2011. It is a seasonal red holiday design rather than a city mug, which makes it an odd and likable outlier filed into the Architecture demitasse group. I keep it because the typo on the label is exactly the kind of quirk that makes a collection feel alive.
Tuscany#186098 · The Architecture SeriesA three ounce Tuscany demitasse decorated not with a skyline but with a scatter of spots outside, an abstract earthy pattern rather than a single landmark. Tuscany evokes Florence, Siena, and the rolling vineyard hills of Chianti, and the speckled design reads like sun and terracotta rather than a literal building. An unusual regional entry that trades the usual architecture motif for pure texture and color.
Beijing, Dark#186103 · The Architecture SeriesA Beijing demitasse, the dark version, white inside with dark Beijing rooftops outside. The sweeping tiled rooftops evoke the Forbidden City and the imperial hutong courtyards at the heart of China's capital, a UNESCO World Heritage palace complex of nearly a thousand buildings. This dark colorway is the moodier of the pair, all silhouette and shadow, and Beijing demitasses are part of the regional Chinese ceramics that rarely surface in Western markets.
Candy Cane#186105 · The Architecture SeriesThis is the holiday oddball of my Architecture shelf, a tiny espresso demitasse with a red interior, a green logo on creme white, and a striped candy cane handle that is the whole point of the piece. That sculpted handle is the rare bit, ceramic candy cane handles are fragile and the stripes chip, so an intact one stands out. It is the kind of seasonal demitasse that gets bought, used once, and then hunted for years later.
Starbucks Round#186106 · The Architecture SeriesA round three ounce demitasse, white inside with the current siren logo in green on the outside, the everyday face of the brand shrunk to espresso scale. This is the workhorse mini, the one that shows the logo evolution most plainly since it carries the last redesigned mark rather than a city design. A clean baseline piece for dating a shelf of otherwise undated demitasse cups.
First Mug, Brown Logo#186107 · The Architecture SeriesThis little espresso mug wears the original brown Starbucks logo over white, a nod to the 1971 Pike Place mark that was rich coffee brown before the company went green in 1987. A brown-logo demitasse is genuinely uncommon, since almost everything Starbucks produced was post-green-logo, which makes this a quiet bit of brand history in 3oz form. The plain white body lets that first-era mark be the whole point of the piece.
2012, Chinese Themed#186110 · The Architecture SeriesA 2012 Chinese-themed demitasse, red inside with bronze petals scattered over white outside. Red and gold are the auspicious colors of Chinese celebration, and this piece reflects Starbucks' fast-growing China market, where the company has tailored seasonal and regional ceramics heavily. The bronze petals over white give it a quiet, elegant look rather than the loud festive style, the kind of regional demitasse that is hard to track down outside Asia.
Starbucks Coffee, White#186111 · The Architecture SeriesThe white on white twin to the black mini, a three ounce espresso cup that is all clean glaze and a discreet wordmark. Starbucks ran these blank demitasse pieces as the understated companions to the city skylines, equally at home holding a ristretto or standing as a minimalist display piece. Simple, but in a collection of loud cityscapes the blank white one earns its spot by contrast.
Starbucks Coffee, Black#186112 · The Architecture SeriesA pure black on black three ounce espresso mini, no city, no skyline, just the wordmark and a glossy monochrome shell. These plain Architecture demitasse cups were the neutral backbone of the line, sold to round out a set or hold a straight shot without distraction. I like it precisely because it is restrained, a quiet counterpoint to all the busy cityscapes on the rest of the shelf.
Starbucks Taiwan, Set of Two#186113 · The Architecture SeriesA charming Taiwan demitasse pair, one cup carrying a bear and the other a wide eyed screaming girl, a playful departure from the usual skyline formula. Taiwan's Starbucks market has long produced some of the most design forward collectibles, and whimsical character sets like this lean into that reputation. The humor and the matched packaging make it a conversation piece, and intact pairs are the only ones worth chasing.
2015, Hong Kong, Thermo Sensitive#186115 · The Architecture SeriesThe 2015 Hong Kong thermo-sensitive demitasse, white with a black painting of Hong Kong that reveals the word HongKong when a hot drink is poured in. Heat-reactive color-change glaze is the gimmick here, and it is genuinely fun in the hand, the skyline warms up and the city name appears. These boxed Hong Kong heat-sensitive pieces show up on eBay regularly and are prized precisely for the working magic-trick reveal.
Beijing, White#186116 · The Architecture SeriesThe Beijing demitasse in its white version, a red Beijing dragon over white outside. The dragon is the supreme imperial emblem of China, the symbol of the emperor himself, so a red dragon on white is about as concentrated a piece of Beijing iconography as you can fit on a 3oz cup. Paired with the dark-rooftop Beijing demitasse, the two make a deliberate light-and-dark set that I like to display together.
Collezione Caffe#186117 · The Architecture SeriesThis little demitasse comes from Starbucks' Collezione Caffe line, the Italian made espresso ware produced by IPA in Italy, here with green and red swirls on white that nod straight to the tricolore. It sits apart from the city skyline mugs, a genuine Italian porcelain piece rather than a US production mug, which is why it feels different in the hand. Collezione and Passaporto Italian sets are a small, charming corner of the catalog that serious collectors quietly prize.
Chicago#186118 · Architecture SeriesThe City Scenes 3oz Chicago, the espresso mate to the full size, carrying the skyline in the standard light blue and grey on white. Tiny as it is, it still packs the Willis Tower and lakefront into a few centimeters, which is half the charm of these minis. Boxed demitasse pairs from this era are getting genuinely hard to assemble, so a chip free Chicago mini is a keeper.
Washington, D.C#186119 · Architecture SeriesThe Washington D.C. architecture demitasse, 3oz, the same light blue and grey skyline line shrunk onto an espresso cup with a white interior. Because Starbucks issued only a handful of these minis across the series, owning the full mug and the demitasse as a matched pair is a small collector's trophy. The monuments-only profile of D.C. reads clearly even at this miniature size.
San Diego#186123 · Architecture SeriesThe 3oz demitasse companion to the San Diego Architecture Series mug, a tiny espresso cup carrying that same pale blue and grey skyline on white. These minis are the harder half of the line to find intact, since espresso cups got used and broken, and collectors prize them for completing a city pairing. San Diego's slice still shows its Balboa Park and waterfront silhouette in miniature.
New York#186124 · Architecture SeriesA subtle variant worth flagging, the catalog files this espresso mini under a City Scenes Series rather than the main Architecture line, yet it carries the standard light blue and grey city skyline outside. That makes it a useful Rosetta stone for how Starbucks reused and renamed these skyline designs across overlapping small series. For a series collector the naming crossover is the whole appeal, two labels, one familiar skyline.
Boston#186128 · City Scene SeriesThe 3oz espresso companion to my Boston piece, this one trades the skyline line drawing for photographic city scenes in grey and very pale blue, part of the City Scenes demitasse cut of the Architecture family. Demitasse minis from this era are easy to lose track of and hard to find boxed, so a clean one with no chips on the tiny handle is the one to hold onto. It pairs perfectly displayed beside the full size Boston.
2004, Blend Stamps#186132 · Collectible Miniatures Series 2A 2004 demitasse printed with Starbucks blend stamps around the outside. This one wears its coffee identity on its sleeve, decorated with the postmark-style stamps Starbucks used to brand its signature blends like House Blend and Italian Roast. It is a charming bit of coffee-culture graphic design on a 3oz espresso cup, the kind of self-referential piece that makes the brand itself the souvenir rather than any city.
2004, Abbey Mug#186134 · The Architecture SeriesThe 2004 Abbey demitasse, a clean all-white 3oz espresso cup. The Abbey shape is one of Starbucks' classic house silhouettes, a slightly tapered straight-sided form that the company reissued in plain white as an everyday at-home espresso cup. No city, no scene, just porcelain and proportion, which is exactly why minimalists love it and why it reads as the calm anchor amid all my busier painted demitasses.
Japan#186137 · Area Collectible Demi SetA 3oz area-collectible demitasse set covering Nagoya, Kyoto, Osaka, Kobe, Miyazaki and Okinawa, the Kansai and southern Japan cities Starbucks Japan grouped into one regional mini collection. Japanese collectors prize these area sets because they were sold locally and rarely escaped the country intact. Six tiny espresso cups standing in for a whole sweep of Japan is exactly the kind of compact, well-documented set I love owning.
2 x magnets from the Architecture#186209 · Architecture SeriesA pair of 2006 vintage magnets from the Architecture Series, one New York and one Pike Place. These are the flat-fridge offshoots of the 2006/2007 city skyline mug line, the same era when Starbucks rendered cities as blue and grey silhouettes with local stats on the back. Pike Place is the heart of it all, the original 1971 Starbucks store at Seattle's Pike Place Market, so pairing it with New York gives me the company's birthplace and its biggest market in one small set.
Pittsburgh#455001 · Architecture SeriesFrom the 2006 Architecture Series, a soft blue and grey skyline banded across white with city notes on the reverse. Pittsburgh is the City of Bridges, with more of them than any city on earth, sitting where the Allegheny and Monongahela meet to form the Ohio. Once the steel capital of the world, it reinvented itself around medicine and tech, and those golden bridges still define its three rivers point.
Fort Worth#455002 · Architecture SeriesFort Worth is "Where the West Begins," home to the historic Stockyards and the world's only twice-daily longhorn cattle drive down East Exchange Avenue. Rendered in the 2006 Architecture Series style with a pale profile line and city trivia on the reverse. I like that it stands apart from neighboring Dallas, since Starbucks gave both Texas rivals their own mug rather than lumping them together.
Houston#455004 · Architecture SeriesHouston is Space City, home to NASA's Johnson Space Center and Mission Control, the place the word "Houston" carried to the moon. The 2006 Architecture Series captures its glassy downtown towers as a pale skyline on white with Texas facts printed on the reverse. As the fourth-largest US city it was a sure inclusion in the run, and a cornerstone Texas piece for any complete Architecture set.
Fresno#455006 · Architecture SeriesFresno sits in the heart of California's San Joaquin Valley, the gateway to Yosemite, Kings Canyon and Sequoia national parks and the country's most productive farm county. A 2006 Architecture Series mug with the city profile in light blue to grey on white and Fresno facts on the back. As an agricultural mid-size city rather than a tourist magnet, it is one of the quieter California pieces in the series to run down.
Alaska#455007 · Architecture SeriesAlaska in the 2006 Architecture Series, white inside with the skyline rendered in light blue and grey outside. The Architecture line drew each place as a single silhouetted line of buildings with city facts printed on the reverse, a cooler and more graphic look than the painted city mugs. Alaska is an unusual entry since it is a whole state rather than a single skyline, so the profile leans on its rugged frontier identity, the last frontier of mountains and wilderness.
Jacksonville#455008 · Architecture SeriesJacksonville is the largest city by land area in the contiguous United States, sprawling across the St. Johns River near Florida's northeast coast with more shoreline than almost any US city. Part of the 2006 Architecture Series with the familiar pale profile and reverse-side city facts. A less glamorous Florida pick than Miami, which makes it a touch scarcer and a satisfying box to tick.
Portland#455009 · Architecture SeriesA 2006 Architecture Series piece, the line that drew each city as one delicate skyline in light blue and grey on white. Portland is the City of Roses, famous for Powell's City of Books, the old white stag sign, food carts, and the Rose Test Garden. Tucked under Mount Hood with a coffee and microbrew culture as serious as Seattle's, it is the quietly proud Oregon counterpoint to its bigger northern neighbor.
Spokane#455010 · Architecture SeriesSpokane in the 2006 to 2007 US and Canada Architecture Series, a single line skyline in that signature light blue and grey on white with city facts printed on the back. Spokane is the Lilac City, host of the 1974 World's Fair that left behind Riverfront Park and the Pavilion. It is one of the quieter cities in the run, so it rarely commands much, often turning up in mixed lots of five for around twenty five dollars.
Sacramento#455011 · Architecture SeriesA 2006 Architecture Series mug, that quiet line of a single pale skyline wrapped on white porcelain with city facts printed behind. Sacramento is California's capital, born of the 1849 Gold Rush at Sutter's Fort, where the gold domed State Capitol and Old Sacramento's wooden boardwalks recall its frontier and railroad past. It was the western terminus of the Pony Express and the first transcontinental railroad.
Seattle#455012 · Architecture SeriesThe hometown mug of the whole company, Seattle in the quiet 2006 Architecture Series style, a pale blue and grey skyline on white with city notes behind. The silhouette belongs to the Space Needle, built for the 1962 World's Fair, with Pike Place Market, the ferries on Elliott Bay, and Mount Rainier looming behind. For a Starbucks collector this is the spiritual center of any city shelf.
Colorado#455013 · Architecture SeriesA state level Colorado entry, so instead of one skyline you get the Rockies and Denver icons together in blue grey, the Mile High City's profile against mountains. Colorado is defined by the Front Range and the Rockies more than any single building, which makes a state mug the smarter call here. These state editions sit beside the city ones in the Architecture family and round out the US map nicely.
Starbucks Support Center#455014 · Architecture SeriesOne of my favorites in the whole series, the Seattle Support Center, Starbucks' own global headquarters rendered in the Architecture Series blue grey style. The building is the converted 1912 Sears distribution warehouse on Utah Avenue South, still topped by its landmark clock tower. Because it was tied to the corporate campus rather than a tourist city, it surfaces far less than ordinary city mugs, and an extreme oversized two and a half gallon version reportedly exists in only a handful.
Charlotte#455015 · Architecture SeriesCharlotte in the Architecture Series, the Queen City's banking towers, the Bank of America Corporate Center and the uptown cluster, drawn as one crisp line in light blue and grey. Charlotte is the second largest US banking hub after New York and the home of NASCAR's Hall of Fame, both fitting for a skyline built on finance and speed. A tidy mid size city entry that fills a real gap in any Architecture run.
Boston#455016 · Architecture SeriesMy Boston Architecture Series mug reduces the whole city to one clean line in that signature light blue and grey on white, the format Starbucks rolled out in the mid 2000s with a short city profile printed on the back. Look for the Custom House Tower clock and the colonial brick spine of a town that gave America its first subway and the Boston Tea Party. The restrained palette is what collectors like about this run, it photographs like a blueprint.
Las Vegas#455017 · Architecture SeriesPart of Starbucks' Architecture Series, the US and Canada line that debuted around 2006 with a city's skyline rendered as a clean light blue and grey band on white, usually with city facts on the reverse. Las Vegas leans on its instantly readable Strip silhouette, the Stratosphere, the fake Eiffel Tower and the Luxor pyramid all in one stretch of desert boulevard. These Architecture mugs trade as a steady mid-tier collectible, often around twenty to thirty dollars apiece, prized for the restrained monochrome look that ties the whole series together.
Philadelphia#455018 · Architecture SeriesPart of the 2006 US and Canada Architecture Series, the line that rendered each city as a single thin skyline in pale blue and grey on white porcelain, with a few city facts printed on the reverse. Philadelphia gives you the cradle of American independence, where Independence Hall and the cracked Liberty Bell sit blocks from the country's first hospital and the steep steps of the Philadelphia Museum of Art that Rocky made famous.
New Orleans#455019 · Architecture SeriesNew Orleans in the Architecture Series, its skyline in the signature light blue and grey on white. The real draw of the city is the French Quarter's wrought iron balconies, the streetcars and the Superdome rather than tall towers, so the mug's profile is more about character than height. As the home of jazz, Mardi Gras and Creole cooking, it is one of the more storied destinations in the set and a natural keeper.
Atlanta#455020 · Architecture SeriesAtlanta in the 2006/2007 Architecture Series, its skyline drawn in cool blue and grey with city stats on the back. Atlanta is the capital of the New South, home to the world's busiest airport at Hartsfield-Jackson, the birthplace of Coca-Cola, and the cradle of the civil rights movement under Dr. King. The clean silhouette style suits a city that rebuilt itself skyward after the Civil War, and the back-side facts are the quiet collector reward.
Miami Beach#455021 · Architecture SeriesInteresting that the series treated Miami Beach as its own city rather than folding it into Miami, giving it a separate skyline mug in the same light blue and grey style. Miami Beach is really about the Ocean Drive Art Deco Historic District, the largest concentration of 1920s to 1940s Deco architecture in the country, all curves, neon and porthole windows. Having both Miami and Miami Beach is the kind of fine distinction that makes completing a series fun.
Austin#455022 · Architecture SeriesAustin in the 2006 Architecture Series, skyline in light blue and grey with the city profile on the reverse. Austin is the Texas capital and self-styled Live Music Capital of the World, crowned by the distinctive dome of the Texas State Capitol, which stands taller than the U.S. Capitol in Washington. The understated Architecture treatment is a fun contrast to Austin's keep-it-weird reputation, letting the skyline and the back-panel facts do the talking.
San Antonio#455023 · Architecture SeriesFrom the 2006 Architecture Series, San Antonio rendered as a soft blue grey skyline on white with notes on the reverse. The city is defined by the Alamo, the 1836 mission where Texas independence was forged, and by the River Walk, a network of stone paths winding one level below the streets. Add the Spanish missions and the 750 foot Tower of the Americas and you have one of Texas's most history soaked cities.
Whistler#455024 · Architecture SeriesWhistler in the Architecture Series, rendered as the familiar single skyline line in blue and grey. Whistler is unusual here because it is a mountain resort village, not a metropolis, so the profile leans on the twin peaks of Whistler and Blackcomb rather than towers. It hosted the alpine events of the 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics, and as a resort-town entry it is one of the quieter, harder-to-find cities in the run.
Cleveland#455025 · Architecture SeriesCleveland on Lake Erie, rendered as one Architecture line, home of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame designed by I.M. Pei and the Terminal Tower that once ranked among the tallest buildings outside New York. The blue grey palette suits a lakefront industrial city well. Rust Belt entries like this tend to be overlooked, so collectors who chase a complete run learn to grab Cleveland when it surfaces.
Nashville#455026 · Architecture SeriesNashville in the Architecture Series, drawn in the same restrained blue and grey skyline style. The unmistakable piece of its profile is the AT&T Building, universally nicknamed the Batman Building for its twin antenna spires, which dominates the Music City skyline. Add the Ryman Auditorium and Lower Broadway's honky tonks and you have the home of country music distilled into one tidy monochrome band, a quietly desirable mug given how many people make the Nashville pilgrimage.
Denver#455027 · Architecture SeriesDenver is the Mile High City, sitting exactly 5,280 feet above sea level, with the gold-domed Colorado State Capitol gilded in real local gold and the snow-capped Rockies on the western horizon. This is the 2006 US Architecture Series, a single light blue to grey skyline wrapped on white with city facts printed on the reverse. The thin profile line and back-of-mug trivia are the tells that separate this run from the later Skyline Series.
San Jose#455028 · Architecture SeriesA 2006 Architecture Series mug, that quiet pale skyline on white with a short city blurb behind. San Jose is the capital of Silicon Valley and the largest city in Northern California, sitting at the southern end of the bay where the orchards of the Valley of Heart's Delight gave way to chips and code. Founded in 1777 as California's first civilian town, it now anchors the tech world.
Cincinnati#455029 · Architecture SeriesCincinnati in the Architecture line, the Ohio River town with its famous suspension bridge, the Roebling, that was John Roebling's prototype for his Brooklyn Bridge years later. The skyline band in blue grey would carry that riverfront and the Carew Tower, an Art Deco landmark. Cincinnati is one of the less glamorous cities in the series, which is exactly why it can be the harder one to track down.
The Magnificent Mile#455030 · Architecture SeriesThe Magnificent Mile in the Architecture Series, Chicago's grand stretch of North Michigan Avenue rather than a generic city skyline, which makes it a destination specific entry. The Mag Mile runs from the Chicago River up to Oak Street and is studded with landmarks like the historic Water Tower, one of the few buildings to survive the 1871 fire. Naming the corridor rather than the whole city marks this as one of the more sought after neighborhood scale designs for completists.
Raleigh#455031 · Architecture SeriesPart of the 2006 US and Canada Architecture Series, this mug carries Raleigh as a thin blue grey skyline on white with a short fact panel on the back. Named for Sir Walter Raleigh, the North Carolina capital is one point of the Research Triangle alongside Durham and Chapel Hill, a region thick with universities. The City of Oaks earns its tree lined nickname, anchored by the state capitol and the museums of its downtown mall.
Union Square#455032 · Architecture SeriesUnion Square in the Architecture Series, the San Francisco retail and theater heart rather than a whole city skyline, a neighborhood specific entry that makes it a little unusual. The square is anchored by the Dewey Monument column and ringed by department stores and the cable car turnaround nearby. Neighborhood scale designs like this are catnip for completists who want the granular pieces beyond the obvious big city mugs.
New York City#455034 · Architecture SeriesListed as New York City to distinguish it from the plain New York mug, this is another Manhattan skyline in the Architecture Series blue grey band. The doubling of New York and New York City entries is the sort of near duplicate that drives the obsessive side of collecting, two mugs that look almost identical until you compare the wordmarks. Given NYC's pull, both versions stay in steady demand.
Fargo#455036 · Architecture SeriesFargo is North Dakota's largest city, made famous worldwide by the Coen brothers' 1996 film and its neon Fargo Theatre marquee on Broadway. As a smaller-market entry in the 2006 Architecture Series, with the pale skyline and reverse-side city facts, Fargo is genuinely harder to track down than the big metros, since fewer were made and fewer survived. The lesser cities are always where this series gets interesting.
Indianapolis#455039 · Architecture SeriesIndianapolis is the "Racing Capital of the World," home to the Indianapolis Motor Speedway and the Indy 500, the largest single-day sporting event anywhere. This 2006 Architecture Series mug shows the city profile in light blue to grey on white with Indiana facts on the back. A solid Midwest entry, and the Speedway heritage gives the skyline a story beyond the usual office towers.
Tampa#455040 · Architecture SeriesTampa in the Architecture Series, marketed in its day under the America's Next Greatest City banner that the city used to promote itself. The skyline leans on landmarks like the Moorish minarets of the old Tampa Bay Hotel, now part of the University of Tampa. A solid mid tier city in the run, with the factual back panel that makes these eighteen ounce profiles feel like little geography lessons.
Toronto#455041 · Architecture SeriesToronto in the Architecture Series blue grey on white, the skyline crowned by the CN Tower, which stood as the world's tallest free standing structure from 1976 until 2007. As a Canadian entry in the largely US run, Toronto rounds out the small set of cross border cities, with the customary city facts on the reverse. A clean staple of the series and an easy anchor for any North American shelf.
Orange County#455042 · Architecture SeriesOrange County in the Architecture Series, the profile in the standard grey blue line on white. Rather than one downtown, OC reads as the coast and the theme parks, Disneyland in Anaheim, the surf towns of Huntington and Newport Beach, and the namesake citrus groves that once blanketed the region. A regional rather than single city entry, which gives it a slightly different flavor from the towered skylines elsewhere in the set.
Orlando#455491 · Architecture SeriesOrlando in the Architecture Series, its skyline in the familiar light blue and grey band. The city's real identity is theme park country, Walt Disney World, Universal and the Cinderella Castle, so its modest downtown profile undersells what draws tens of millions of visitors a year. As one of the most visited tourist cities in America, it has built in appeal for collectors who pick up mugs from places they have actually traveled.
Japan, You Are Here Collection#455591 · The Architecture SeriesA You Are Here demitasse for Japan, cream-bodied with stars and music notes scattered over the white-cream exterior rather than the usual packed grid of landmarks. The YAH line launched in 2013, and this whimsical, playful take is a softer counterpoint to the busy city-icon mugs the series is known for. A gentle, almost lyrical piece that shows the range Starbucks gave the Japan market.
Japan, 2011#455832 · Japan 2011This 2011 Japan piece carries a gold logo of a bird over a mountain above coffee fields on a dark red ground with a black interior, a striking departure from the usual city-skyline formula. It reads more like a national identity design than a single landmark, which makes it one of the more artful entries in the Japan demitasse run. The dated 2011 marking and the unusual artwork together make it a standout on the shelf.
Bodrum, Blue#576099 · The Architecture SeriesBodrum in the Architecture style, white inside with the city's light blue buildings outside. Bodrum is the Turkish Aegean resort built on ancient Halicarnassus, once home to the Mausoleum, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, and still guarded by the Knights Hospitaller's 15th century Bodrum Castle. The light blue buildings are spot on, since traditional Bodrum houses are famously whitewashed with blue doors and shutters, making this Turkey's yacht-capital playground in ceramic form.
Las Vegas#576575 · You Are Here CollectionThis is the 3oz demitasse cousin to the full Vegas mug, and the catalog confirms it breaks the series formula with a red interior and the actual Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign and Strip outside rather than the standard skyline band. That neon diamond sign, designed by Betty Willis in 1959, was never copyrighted on purpose so the city could share it freely. The little espresso minis are harder to track down than the regular mugs, which makes a matched demitasse a satisfying find.
Demitasse Greece#576897 · City Mug Collector SeriesMy Greece demitasse, white inside with a large light blue sailing boat on the outside, that classic Aegean caique under sail against a whitewashed and blue palette. The boat motif leans on the island image of Greece, Santorini and the Cyclades, rather than a city skyline, which sets it apart in the group. A cheerful, sea minded little cup that reads as Greece at a glance.
New York#576935 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe 3oz New York demitasse, and the catalog confirms it swaps the skyline for the Statue of Liberty in green outside on white, a smart single icon choice for the smaller canvas. Lady Liberty was a gift from France dedicated in 1886, her copper skin weathered to that exact green over decades of sea air. The espresso minis are scarcer than the regular mugs, so a Liberty demitasse is a genuinely nice catch.
Chicago#576942 · City Mug Collector SeriesA Chicago demitasse variant with a light orange trumpet shaped body rather than the standard line drawing, an oddly warm color break from the rest of the cool toned Architecture family. Color variants like this are exactly what makes demitasse hunting fun, the same city can show up in more than one finish across the sub series. Worth keeping next to the blue grey Chicago to show the contrast.
Seattle#576964 · City Mug Collector SeriesA standout in the demitasse run, because instead of the usual pale skyline this Seattle mini shows a green Space Needle on white, a deliberate nod to the company's home tower and its green identity. The 1962 World's Fair landmark gets its own little espresso cup, making this one of the more characterful and recognizable pieces in the small format Architecture line.
Los Angeles#576965 · City Mug Collector SeriesThe 3oz LA demitasse, and the catalog note makes clear it ditches the grey skyline for orange palm trees outside on white, a warmer and more playful take than its full size sibling. Those slender Mexican fan palms lining the boulevards were largely planted ahead of the 1932 Olympics, so the icon itself is a piece of city history. The espresso minis in this series turn up far less often than the regular mugs, so a clean one is worth grabbing.
Los Angeles#576976 · Architecture SeriesThe LA entry in the Architecture Series, its skyline drawn in the same light blue and grey line work on white that unifies the whole 2006 US and Canada run. Downtown's US Bank Tower and the cluster around Bunker Hill carry the profile, the same skyline that doubles for a hundred movie establishing shots. I keep it next to the LA demitasse since the two read as a pair, the big mug doing the serious skyline and the little one going for palm trees.
Chicago#576977 · Architecture SeriesChicago is the dream city for any skyline series, and this Architecture mug delivers the Sears, now Willis, Tower, the Hancock and the lakefront wall in that calm blue grey line. This is the city that invented the skyscraper after the 1871 fire, so a clean architectural reduction of it feels exactly right. Chicago is one of the more sought entries in the line precisely because the city's profile is so recognizable.
New Mexico#576978 · Architecture SeriesA curiosity in the lineup since the series labels this New Mexico rather than a single city, breaking from the usual city skyline format. The state reads as Albuquerque and Santa Fe country, adobe Pueblo Revival architecture, the Sandia Mountains, and the hot air balloons of the famous Albuquerque Fiesta. State level entries in a city focused series are exactly the kind of off pattern piece collectors notice, so it is worth having for that alone.
Pike Place#576979 · Architecture SeriesA genuine sentimental favorite, because Pike Place is where it all began. The original Starbucks opened at 1912 Pike Place in 1971, steps from the public market's neon Public Market Center clock and the brass piggy bank Rachel. This Architecture Series rendering keeps the quiet 2006 styling, a pale skyline on white, but for collectors anything tied to the birthplace store carries extra weight.
St. Louis#576981 · Architecture SeriesSt. Louis rendered as one clean skyline line in the Architecture Series blue grey on white, the Gateway Arch unmistakable even in profile. Eero Saarinen's 630 foot stainless catenary curve is the tallest arch in the world and the centerpiece here. These eighteen ounce city profiles carry factual blurbs on the reverse, a nice touch that makes the line feel like a pocket atlas of America.
Memphis#576982 · Architecture SeriesMemphis in the Architecture Series, the skyline in the familiar light blue and grey band with city facts on the back. The standout shape is the Hernando de Soto Bridge with its twin M shaped arches over the Mississippi, lit at night so the river itself spells the city's initial. Memphis is also Beale Street, Sun Studio and Graceland, the birthplace of so much American music, which makes its understated skyline mug feel almost too quiet for the place.
West Palm Beach#576983 · Architecture SeriesWest Palm Beach in the Architecture Series, the Florida skyline laid out in light blue and grey on white. This is a less obvious city for the line, which makes it a satisfying find, the waterfront condo towers along the Intracoastal Waterway facing Palm Beach island across the lagoon. Built by Henry Flagler as a working town for the wealthy resort across the water, it earns its quiet place in a series otherwise full of marquee cities.
Montreal#576984 · Architecture SeriesOne of the Canadian entries in the Architecture Series, Montreal's skyline in the standard grey blue band on white. The profile is anchored by downtown towers below Mount Royal, with the Olympic Stadium's leaning tower, the tallest inclined structure in the world, often part of the city's recognizable shape. As a Canada mug from a primarily US series, the cross border cities tend to be a little scarcer for American collectors hunting the full run.
Washington D.C.#576985 · Architecture SeriesWashington D.C. in the Architecture Series, the skyline drawn in that signature light blue and grey band on white. By federal law no building may overshadow the Capitol, so the capital has no real skyscrapers, which makes the silhouette here a parade of monuments instead, the Capitol dome, the Washington Monument obelisk, and the Lincoln Memorial. That low, horizontal profile is exactly why the single-line Architecture format suits D.C. so well.
San Francisco#576986 · Architecture SeriesPart of the 2006 Architecture Series, San Francisco drawn as a single blue grey skyline on white porcelain with facts on the reverse. The hooks write themselves, the Golden Gate Bridge in international orange, the clanging cable cars over the hills, Alcatraz in the bay, and the painted ladies of Alamo Square. Built on the 1849 Gold Rush, it remains one of the most photographed skylines in the world.
Twin Cities#576987 · Architecture SeriesTwin Cities, Minneapolis and Saint Paul sharing a single Architecture Series skyline line, a rare two for one in a series usually built around one city. The design spans both downtowns across the Mississippi, the river that divides and defines them. Minnesota collectors prize this one regionally, and it is worth remembering Minneapolis solo holds famous value in the old 1994 City Mug line at roughly two thousand dollars, a different beast entirely.
Dallas#576989 · Architecture SeriesDallas in the Architecture line, that instantly readable skyline with the Reunion Tower ball and the green lit Bank of America Plaza standing over the Texas plains. The city carries heavy associations, the 1963 Kennedy assassination at Dealey Plaza and the oil and finance boom that built those towers. A strong, recognizable big city entry that anchors the Texas end of any Architecture collection.
Calgary#576990 · Architecture SeriesCalgary in the Architecture Series, that famous Calgary Tower spike rising over the Bow River done in the line's cool blue grey on white. The city is best known worldwide for the Calgary Stampede, the self styled greatest outdoor show on earth, and for hosting the 1988 Winter Olympics. Canadian cities in this series turn up less often than the big US ones, which makes the maple leaf entries quietly worth grabbing when you see them.
Palm Springs#576992 · Architecture SeriesPalm Springs in the Architecture Series, low slung rather than towered, fitting a desert resort town. The city is the world capital of midcentury modern architecture, all clean lines, glass walls and Albert Frey homes against the San Jacinto Mountains, a look that suits the series' minimalist blue grey style perfectly. A desert getaway favorite, it is one of the more design literate cities in the run and a satisfying one to own.
San Diego#576993 · Architecture SeriesA 2006 Architecture Series mug, the restrained line that drew each city as one light skyline on white with a small fact panel behind. San Diego gives you near perfect weather, the sprawling Balboa Park with its Spanish Revival pavilions and world famous zoo, the historic Gaslamp Quarter, and Coronado's Hotel del Coronado. As the birthplace of California, it pairs a deep naval history with miles of Pacific beaches.
Canada#576994 · Architecture SeriesA national Canada edition rather than a single city, this Architecture mug bundles the country's icons into one band in the series light blue and grey. Expect the CN Tower silhouette and parliamentary and natural landmarks standing in for the whole nation, the format Starbucks used for country level pieces alongside the city ones. Country mugs read as a clever catch all and complete the North American sweep of this line nicely.
Fort Lauderdale#576995 · Architecture SeriesFort Lauderdale is the "Venice of America," laced with roughly 165 miles of navigable canals and famous for its long Atlantic beach and yachting harbor. This is the 2006 Architecture Series treatment, a light blue to grey waterfront profile on white with Florida city facts printed on the back. A breezy coastal entry that pairs naturally with the other Sun Belt cities in the run.
New York#576996 · Architecture SeriesThe New York Architecture Series mug, Manhattan's towers rendered in that clean blue grey line on white with the Empire State and Chrysler buildings leading the skyline. New York is one of several near identical NYC entries in this series, which gives completists a quiet headache of variants to chase. As the most iconic skyline on Earth, it is one of the higher demand cities in the whole Architecture run.
Miami#576997 · Architecture SeriesMiami's Architecture Series mug, the downtown and Brickell towers laid out in that signature blue grey line on white. The real Miami skyline is one of the densest in the country, glassy condo towers crowding Biscayne Bay, and at night many are washed in pastel light that nods to the city's Art Deco roots. A solid mid-tier collector piece, it pairs naturally with the separate Miami Beach mug for anyone building the Florida cities.
Vancouver#576999 · Architecture SeriesPart of the Architecture Series that ran from 2006 to 2012, this Vancouver piece renders the skyline as one continuous light blue and grey line wrapped around a white mug. You can read the city's real profile here, the glassy downtown towers rising against the Coast Mountains and the sails of Canada Place jutting into Burrard Inlet. The whole series spanned 64 mugs, and as a clean minimalist line drawing it has aged better than most of the busier travel lines.
Detroit#577000 · Architecture SeriesDetroit is the Motor City, birthplace of Ford's assembly line and the Motown sound, and its riverfront Renaissance Center towers anchor the skyline rendered here. Part of the 2006 Architecture Series with the city profile in light blue to grey on white and Detroit facts on the back. Rust Belt cities from this run turn up less often than the coastal ones, which is part of why I went after it.
2004, First LogoThe Architecture SeriesThe 2004 First Logo demitasse, carrying Starbucks' original brown 1971 siren, the bare-breasted twin-tailed mermaid drawn from a 16th century Norse woodcut. This is the heritage logo that only officially survives at the Pike Place flagship store, so any retail piece wearing it is a deliberate nod to the company's beginnings. On a tiny 3oz espresso cup it becomes a pocket-sized history lesson, and the original-logo pieces always draw collector attention.
2011, Starbucks Coffee, Brown MermThe Architecture SeriesA 2011 demitasse marked Starbucks Coffee with the brown mermaid. The 2011 date is significant, that was the company's 40th anniversary and the year of the big logo redesign that dropped the words Starbucks Coffee and the outer ring entirely. A 2011 cup still carrying the full brown wordmark siren sits right on the cusp of that transition, which makes it a neat little timestamp of the moment the branding changed.
2015, "The Gruffalo" in whiteThe Architecture SeriesA 2015 demitasse featuring The Gruffalo in white. The Gruffalo is Julia Donaldson and Axel Scheffler's beloved 1999 children's picture book monster, the terrible creature with knobbly knees and turned-out toes and a poisonous wart on the nose. A licensed Gruffalo Starbucks cup is an unusual and very British crossover, the sort of pop-culture tie-in that sits well outside the normal city-mug world and makes a fun oddity on the shelf.
ColumbusThe Architecture SeriesColumbus, Ohio in the Architecture Series, the state capital whose skyline centers on the LeVeque Tower and the riverfront, home to Ohio State and one of the fastest growing Midwestern cities. With no catalog text on file, this is the standard line drawing format in the series cool blue grey on white. A solid Midwest capital that completes the Ohio trio alongside Cincinnati and Cleveland.
Demitasse Athens 1The Architecture SeriesOne of a pair of Athens demitasse minis in my Greek group, espresso sized and tied to the city of the Parthenon and the Acropolis, the cradle of Western democracy and the 1896 first modern Olympics. With no catalog text recorded, this reads as part of the Greek demitasse run that turns up through European and licensed stores. Greek pieces travel less to the US market, so even a small Athens mini is a satisfying find.
Demitasse Athens 2The Architecture SeriesThe second Athens demitasse, the companion to the first, a paired or color variant in the same Greek espresso run. Collecting these in twos is the whole game, the two Athens minis side by side tell you the line was sold as a set. For a city as iconic as Athens, the home of the Acropolis and Plaka's marble streets, even the smallest cup carries real weight on the shelf.
Demitasse Deer In PinkThe Architecture SeriesA whimsical departure from the city mugs, this demitasse features a deer motif in pink, more decorative seasonal art than skyline geography. Animal and nature themed minis like this float outside the named architecture run and are easy to overlook, which is part of their charm when they surface boxed. It is the kind of odd, pretty little piece that breaks up a wall of grey skylines.
Fijian Style, Golden last logoThe Architecture SeriesA "Fijian style" demitasse carrying the golden last logo, the final full-name Starbucks Coffee ring before the 2011 switch to the standalone wordless siren. The gold logo and island-inspired styling make this a design-led collectible rather than a city piece, and the "last logo" label is the real draw, since it dates the mug to the end of an era in Starbucks branding. I keep it as a small marker of that logo transition.
Japan 2012The Architecture SeriesA 2012 Japan demitasse from the Starbucks Japan regional run, the year following the 2011 design and continuing the small-format city series sold only in Japanese stores. Dated Japan minis like this are valued by collectors precisely because they pin a specific year, and the domestic-only distribution kept them scarce abroad. A clean little time capsule of where Starbucks Japan's collectible program stood that year.
Niagara FallsThe Architecture SeriesNiagara Falls in the Architecture Series, and notably the catalog field is blank here so I am going off the series pattern rather than printed copy. The subject is unusual for a skyline line since Niagara is a natural wonder, three waterfalls straddling the US Canada border moving more water than almost any falls in North America. A scenery driven entry in a skyline series makes this one of the more distinctive mugs to track down.
PhoenixThe Architecture SeriesA 2006 Architecture Series mug, the understated line that wraps a single light blue and grey skyline around white porcelain with a short city blurb on the back. Phoenix is the largest capital in the Lower 48 and the heart of the Valley of the Sun, ringed by Camelback Mountain and saguaro desert, a city that grew on air conditioning and reinvents itself like the firebird it is named for.
Starbucks MugThe Architecture SeriesA generic Starbucks branded demitasse from the Architecture era, the unadorned three ounce format that anchored the espresso line before the city art was applied. Pieces like this are the baseline of the series, useful for understanding how the decorated cups were built on a common blank. Not flashy, but a sensible reference point for anyone tracing how the demitasse program evolved.
TucsonThe Architecture SeriesTucson in the blue grey Architecture Series line, the desert city framed by saguaro country and the Santa Catalina Mountains. Old Pueblo sits in the Sonoran Desert and is a UNESCO City of Gastronomy, the first in the United States. Collector blogs have documented this exact Tucson architecture mug, which helps confirm provenance, though it remains one of the more modestly priced Southwestern entries.
Washington D.C.The Architecture SeriesA tiny 3oz Washington D.C. demitasse, an espresso-sized companion to the full mug. Only around nine cities in the whole Architecture run ever got the mini treatment, so the little ones are genuinely scarcer than their full-size siblings and collectors hunt them to complete a city. At this scale the monument skyline becomes almost a miniature engraving you turn in your fingers.
White Bird with OrnamentThe Architecture SeriesA White Bird with Ornament demitasse, a holiday-leaning piece that breaks from the city skyline theme of the series. Rather than an urban profile it carries a decorative bird and ornament motif on the espresso-sized cup, the kind of seasonal oddity that collectors slot in alongside the architectural minis. Pieces like this are easy to overlook precisely because they are not a city, which is part of their charm.
Classification

The Skyline Series46 pieces

A full city panorama wrapped around a standard cup.
Tampa#455043 · Skyline SeriesTampa's 2002 Skyline Series mug captures a Gulf Coast city known for the silver minarets of the old Tampa Bay Hotel, now the University of Tampa, and the historic cigar district of Ybor City. The blue-grey wraparound suits the bayfront waterfront. A lesser-spotted Florida entry that fills a gap in the full Barista-era city run.
Houston#455044 · Skyline SeriesA 2002 Skyline Series One mug, blue and grey skyline on a white body with Houston running up the handle. Space City's profile leans on the JPMorgan Chase Tower, the tallest building in Texas, alongside the Williams Tower out in Uptown, while the real civic icon sits offsite at NASA's Johnson Space Center, home of Mission Control. I like that this series stays sober and graphic, just rooftops and air, no clip art mascots.
Toronto#455045 · Skyline SeriesToronto carries Canada's tallest icon into the 2002 Skyline Series, the CN Tower, which stood as the world's tallest free-standing structure from 1976 until 2007. The skyline of Ontario's capital sweeps along the Lake Ontario waterfront in the line's soft blue and grey. A clean cross-border piece stamped with the Barista era's "Pour Your Heart Into It."
St. Paul#455046 · Skyline SeriesSt. Paul, the quieter twin to Minneapolis, joined the 2002 Skyline Series anchored by its grand domed Minnesota State Capitol and the riverbluff Cathedral of Saint Paul. Pairing it with the Minneapolis mug completes the Twin Cities, which carries extra collector charge given how prized the early 1990s Minneapolis city mug became. A modest blue-grey piece with outsized appeal to set-builders.
New Orleans#455047 · Skyline SeriesA 2002 Skyline Series One mug, New Orleans in blue and grey on white with the name up the handle. Rather than tall towers, the Big Easy's identity lives in the French Quarter's wrought-iron balconies, the triple steeples of St. Louis Cathedral on Jackson Square, and the jazz that was born here. A characterful low-rise entry in a series otherwise full of glass-and-steel downtowns.
Cleveland#455048 · Skyline SeriesCleveland in the 2005 Skyline Series, the Lake Erie city in the line's blue and grey. The skyline suggests the Terminal Tower, the 1930 landmark that was among the tallest buildings outside New York for decades, with the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame on the lakefront. As a less glamorous Midwestern entry, the Cleveland mug is a quietly satisfying one to track down.
St. Louis#455049 · Skyline SeriesSt. Louis brings the unmistakable Gateway Arch to the 2002 Skyline Series, Eero Saarinen's 630-foot stainless steel curve completed in 1965 as the tallest monument in the country. The "Gateway to the West" framing fits the Mississippi riverfront perfectly. Captured in the line's signature blue-grey with the Barista-era "Pour Your Heart Into It" stamp.
Miami#455050 · Skyline SeriesFrom the 2002 Skyline Series One, Miami rendered in blue and grey on white, city name up the handle. The bayfront skyline is famous for its nighttime neon glow, the Freedom Tower that processed Cuban refugees, and the pastel Art Deco district along Ocean Drive in South Beach. A cool tropical-feeling piece that, like the rest of the run, lets the buildings do all the talking.
Indianapolis#455051 · Skyline SeriesFrom the 2002 Skyline Series One, Indianapolis in blue and grey on white with the city name up the handle. The skyline is anchored by Salesforce Tower, formerly Chase Tower, the tallest in Indiana, and the limestone Soldiers and Sailors Monument on Monument Circle, but the city's true fame is the Indianapolis Motor Speedway and its Indy 500. A clean, understated piece from a set collectors prize precisely because it never got loud.
Salt Lake City#455052 · Skyline SeriesThis Salt Lake City mug from the 2002 Skyline Series lands in the year the city hosted the Winter Olympics, which put its mountain-ringed skyline on the world stage. The genuine landmark is Temple Square and the six-spired Salt Lake Temple, the spiritual heart of the Mormon faith, set against the Wasatch Range. The cool blue-grey wrap is classic Barista-era restraint.
Dallas#455053 · Skyline SeriesDallas in the 2005 Skyline Series, drawn in the familiar blue and grey band. The signature element is Reunion Tower, the geodesic ball on a stalk that lights up at night, alongside the Bank of America Plaza outlined in green argon. Forever tied to 1963 and to the oil and cattle wealth of North Texas, Dallas brings a flashy modern profile to the line.
Napa Valley#455054 · Skyline SeriesConsidered one of the rarest in the whole 2002 Skyline Series One, and a clear departure from the skyline format: a panoramic vineyard in blue and grey with hot air balloons drifting above, Napa Valley up the handle, the words The Wine Country inside, and a little cluster of grapes by the date on the base. Napa is California's most famous wine region, and dawn balloon flights over the vines are a genuine local ritual. The non-skyline scene and its scarcity make this a real prize.
Austin#455055 · Skyline SeriesAustin in the 2005 Skyline Series, drawn in the line's blue and grey. The standout is the Texas State Capitol, deliberately built taller than the U.S. Capitol in Washington, paired with the University of Texas tower. Austin has exploded since this mug appeared, so the early-2000s skyline here is almost a period snapshot of the city before its tech boom reshaped the river.
Detroit#455056 · Skyline SeriesDetroit in the 2005 Skyline Series, the Motor City rendered in blue and grey. The riverfront skyline is dominated by the Renaissance Center, the cylindrical GM headquarters towers on the Detroit River looking across to Windsor, Canada. Birthplace of the auto industry and Motown, Detroit gives the line one of its most recognizable single-building silhouettes.
Montreal#455057 · Skyline SeriesOne of the Canadian entries in the 2002 Skyline Series One, Montreal in blue and grey on white with the name up the handle. The skyline is crowned by the cross atop Mont Royal, the hill that gives the city its name, with the Olympic Stadium's leaning tower and the dome of St. Joseph's Oratory nearby. A nicely European-feeling silhouette for North America's largest French-speaking city.
Baltimore#455059 · Skyline SeriesBaltimore in the 2005 Skyline Series, the Inner Harbor city rendered in blue and grey on white. The waterfront profile suggests the National Aquarium and the pentagonal World Trade Center on the harbor, with the historic USS Constellation moored below. This is the city of Fort McHenry, where the bombardment in 1814 inspired the Star Spangled Banner, a good deal of history packed behind one quiet skyline.
Las Vegas#455060 · Skyline SeriesThe oddball of the set, printed in bold red rather than the usual blue or grey, fitting for Las Vegas. This 2002 Skyline Series One mug wraps the Strip's fantasy skyline, the faux Eiffel Tower of Paris Las Vegas, the Luxor pyramid and the Stratosphere needle, none of them more than a generation old in a city that reinvents itself constantly. That red colorway makes it stand out on a shelf of otherwise cool-toned Skyline mugs.
San Francisco#455061 · Skyline SeriesSan Francisco is one of the marquee cities in the 2002 Skyline Series, its profile crowned by the Golden Gate Bridge, the Transamerica Pyramid, and the cable-car hills. The Bay city is also Starbucks lore in its own right, since the company's specialty-coffee roots trace partly to the Bay Area cafe culture of the 1960s. A perennial collector favorite in soft blue and grey.
Philadelphia#455062 · Skyline SeriesFrom the 2002 Skyline Series One, Philadelphia in light green and grey on white with the name up the handle. The skyline is marked by City Hall topped by William Penn, long the height limit until One Liberty Place broke the gentlemen's agreement, but the city's heart is Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell where the nation was founded. The green colorway gives this one a softer look than the blue mugs.
Boston#455063 · Skyline SeriesBoston in the 2005 Skyline Series, and like the nature entries it wears the green and grey palette rather than blue. The skyline leans on the John Hancock Tower and the Prudential, with the gold dome of the State House and the Custom House clock tower among the older landmarks. Cradle of the American Revolution and the country's oldest subway, Boston gives the line one of its most historically loaded profiles.
Alaska#455064 · Skyline SeriesAlaska in the 2005 Skyline Series, and note the green and grey palette that set the state and nature entries apart from the blue city mugs. This one carries the state nickname The Last Frontier, fitting for a place bigger than Texas, California and Montana combined. The Skyline run was an early 18oz collector line, and as a whole-state rather than single-city design it is a favorite for people chasing the full set.
Sacramento#455065 · Skyline SeriesSacramento joined Starbucks' 2002 Skyline Series, the line that wrapped a city's profile in soft blue and grey around the cup and carried the Barista era's "Pour Your Heart Into It" branding. California's capital is anchored by the gold-domed State Capitol and the old riverfront of Old Sacramento, where the Gold Rush and the transcontinental railroad both left their mark. A quiet entry that completists chase to round out the full city set.
Honolulu#455066 · Skyline SeriesPart of the 2002 Skyline Series One, the US and Canada wraparound run that Starbucks rolled out the year after the City Scenes line, this Honolulu cup carries an island silhouette in blue and grey on white. Honolulu means "sheltered harbor" in Hawaiian, and any honest skyline here is dominated by Diamond Head, the tuff cone crater above Waikiki, with the pink Royal Hawaiian and Aloha Tower clock down on the waterfront. The Skyline pieces print the city name vertically up the handle, a tidy signature of the set.
Calgary#455067 · Skyline SeriesCalgary in the 2005 Skyline Series, the Alberta city in the line's blue and grey. The unmistakable marker is the Calgary Tower, the slim observation spire that long defined downtown, set against the towers built on the city's oil and gas money. Calgary is also the home of the Stampede, the giant rodeo that bills itself as the greatest outdoor show on earth, a fun fact behind a sober skyline.
Victoria#455068 · Skyline SeriesVictoria, British Columbia's capital on Vancouver Island, brings its stately landmarks to the 2002 Skyline Series, namely the domed Parliament Buildings and the ivy-clad Fairmont Empress hotel on the Inner Harbour. The genteel, very British seaside city is a softer counterpoint to bustling Vancouver. A blue-grey Canadian piece that pairs naturally with its mainland sibling.
Lake Tahoe#455069 · Skyline SeriesA 2002 Skyline Series One, and a favorite quirk of mine: instead of a skyline it renders the alpine lake in blue, white and black, with Lake Tahoe up the handle and the word Stateline hidden inside the rim, a nod to the Nevada casino strip on the lake's southeast shore. Tahoe straddles the California to Nevada line and is the largest alpine lake in North America, famous for water so clear you can see dozens of feet down. The lake-not-skyline treatment makes this one of the more characterful cups in the run.
Washington D.C.#455070 · Skyline SeriesWashington D.C. gets the most distinctive treatment in the 2002 Skyline Series, its monuments rendered in grey beneath bursting fireworks, a nod to the Fourth of July spectacle over the National Mall. The Capitol dome and Washington Monument anchor the design. That fireworks detail makes it one of the more visually unusual mugs in the whole Barista-era run, and a favorite for collectors who notice the small variations.
Chicago#455071 · Skyline SeriesChicago in the 2005 Skyline Series, the birthplace of the skyscraper rendered in blue and grey on white. The profile is anchored by the Willis Tower, called Sears Tower when this mug was made, alongside the John Hancock Center with its distinctive crossbraces. Chicago invented the modern skyline after the 1871 fire, so no city wears this format more naturally.
Portland#455072 · Skyline SeriesFrom the 2002 Skyline Series One, Portland printed in light grey on white with the name up the handle. The Rose City skyline frames Mount Hood on the horizon, with the white Steel and Hawthorne bridges over the Willamette and the lit Portland Oregon stag sign downtown. A muted grey colorway that suits the famously cloudy, green-minded Pacific Northwest city.
Pittsburgh#455073 · Skyline SeriesA 2002 Skyline Series One mug, Pittsburgh rendered in light blue on white. The city sits at the confluence of three rivers, and its skyline is defined by the gleaming PPG Place crystal castle, the gold US Steel Tower, and the many yellow bridges that earned it the City of Bridges nickname. A handsome industrial profile from a town that reinvented itself from steel into medicine and tech.
New York#455075 · Skyline SeriesThe flagship of the 2002 Skyline Series One, New York in blue and grey on white. Released the year after 9/11, the skyline here is a poignant document of what the city chose to show in that moment, the Empire State Building, the Chrysler spire and the Brooklyn Bridge among them. This same Skyline run spawned a four-mug USA Scenic extension after the attacks, which makes the New York piece feel especially of its time.
San Antonio#455076 · Skyline SeriesSan Antonio's Skyline Series mug from 2002 nods to a city defined by the River Walk and the Alamo, the 1836 mission where the famous siege gave Texas its rallying cry. The Tower of the Americas, built for the 1968 HemisFair, still spikes the skyline rendered here in soft blue and grey. Part of the original Barista line stamped with "Pour Your Heart Into It."
Los Angeles#455077 · Skyline SeriesA 2002 Skyline Series One mug, LA in blue and grey on white with the name up the handle. The downtown profile centers on the US Bank Tower, for two decades the tallest building west of the Mississippi, though Los Angeles is really known for Hollywood, the sign in the hills, and the sprawl that earned it the City of Angels name. Restrained and architectural, exactly the tone this series was going for.
Canada#455078 · Skyline SeriesCanada in the 2005 Skyline Series, and instead of a city this national mug puts Niagara Falls front and center, the cataract drawn in light blue. It is a clever choice, the Horseshoe Falls on the Canadian side carries far more water than the American falls and is the country's most visited natural landmark. As the whole-country entry rather than a single city, it stands a little apart from the rest of the set.
Denver#455079 · Skyline SeriesDenver in the 2005 Skyline Series, the Mile High City in blue and grey on white. Denver sits exactly one mile above sea level, with a step on the State Capitol marking 5,280 feet, and the Rockies make a natural backdrop behind the downtown towers. As the gateway to the mountains, it is one of the more scenic profiles in a series built mostly from glass and steel.
Pike Place Market#455081 · Skyline SeriesA special one for any Starbucks collector. This 2002 Skyline Series One mug honors Pike Place Market in blue and grey on white, with Pike Place Market up the handle and the line The Birthplace of Starbucks Coffee printed across the back, since the very first store opened at the market in 1971. Pike Place is one of the oldest continuously operating public farmers markets in the country, home to the fish-throwing stalls and the brass piggy bank. The Starbucks-origin text makes this the sentimental cornerstone of the series.
Vancouver#455082 · Skyline SeriesVancouver's Skyline Series mug from 2002 frames a glass-towered city wedged between the Coast Mountains and the Pacific, with the sails of Canada Place and Stanley Park as defining sights. Often confused with Victoria across the strait, the two are easy to mix up in a set, so collectors prize having both. Rendered in the line's signature blue-grey wrap.
Seattle#455083 · Skyline SeriesSeattle is the home city, so this 2002 Skyline Series mug carries extra weight, rendered in light green rather than the usual blue to set the birthplace apart. The skyline pairs the Space Needle, built for the 1962 World's Fair, with the harbor where Starbucks opened its first store at Pike Place in 1971. The green wrap makes this one a quiet standout in the set.
San Diego#455084 · Skyline SeriesSan Diego earned its spot in the 2002 Skyline Series with a harbor city known for the Coronado Bridge, the USS Midway, and Balboa Park's Spanish Colonial towers. The blue-grey wraparound suits a place that practically invented perfect weather. A clean, sought-after California piece for anyone assembling the full Barista-era skyline run.
Atlanta#455085 · Skyline SeriesAtlanta in the 2005 Skyline Series, the city wrapped in that light blue and grey band on white. Atlanta's profile is dominated by the Bank of America Plaza spire, long the tallest building in the U.S. outside New York and Chicago. As the home of Coca-Cola, CNN and the 1996 Centennial Olympics, the city that rebuilt itself after the Civil War earns a confident skyline.
Minneapolis#455086 · Skyline SeriesA 2002 Skyline Series One mug, Minneapolis in blue and grey on white. Worth noting for collectors: this is the later Skyline piece, not the famously valuable early 1994 Minneapolis City Mug that trades for around two thousand dollars, so do not confuse the two. The skyline shows the IDS Center, the tallest tower in Minnesota with its Philip Johnson Crystal Court, in a city laced with skyways and known as the Mill City for its old flour empire.
Raleigh#455087 · Skyline SeriesA 2002 Skyline Series One mug, Raleigh in blue and grey on white with the name climbing the handle. North Carolina's capital is the City of Oaks, anchored by the domed State Capitol and the museums around its central squares, one point of the Research Triangle alongside Durham and Chapel Hill. A quieter Southern entry that rounds out the broad reach of this US and Canada set.
Starbucks Coffee Co#455088 · Skyline SeriesThis is the oddball gem of the 2002 Skyline Series, swapping a city for Starbucks itself, the SoDo headquarters building rendered in light brown rather than the usual blue. The Starbucks Center sits in Seattle's SoDo neighborhood in a former Sears warehouse, and the Barista-era "Pour Your Heart Into It" line on it doubles as the title of Howard Schultz's 1997 memoir. A self-referential piece collectors love precisely because it breaks the city pattern.
Palms Springs#455089 · Skyline SeriesA 2002 Skyline Series One mug for Palm Springs, distinctively printed in light green and grey on white rather than the usual blue. This desert resort town in the Coachella Valley is famous less for tall buildings than for its mid-century modern architecture, the Aerial Tramway climbing San Jacinto, and rows of windmills at the pass. The green colorway and low desert profile set it apart in the set.
Niagara FallsThe Skyline SeriesA Canadian-side entry in the 2002 Skyline Series One, Niagara Falls in blue and grey on white with the name up the handle. Instead of buildings the design gives you the falls themselves, the great curved Horseshoe Falls that straddle the Ontario to New York border and move more water than almost any waterfall on Earth. The Maid of the Mist tour boats have been nosing into that mist since 1846, which is the image this cup is chasing.
PhoenixThe Skyline SeriesA 2002 Skyline Series One mug, Phoenix in blue and grey on white with the city name climbing the handle. The Valley of the Sun's low desert skyline is backed by Camelback Mountain and saguaro country, in the hottest major city in the United States, named for a settlement that rose from the canals of the vanished Hohokam. A clean, sun-baked entry in the run.
Classification

Skyline GIANTS15 pieces

The oversized twenty-four ounce statement mugs.
