2000 Witch Bear#734002 · Barista BearsThe 2000 Witch Bearista, a Halloween-costume entry from the years when Starbucks began branching its annual bear into seasonal characters beyond Christmas. The witch hat and outfit make it one of the earlier dressed-up holiday Bearistas, predating the flood of themed bears that came later in the decade. Autumn and Halloween Bearistas had short selling windows, so a clean 2000 example is a satisfying early grab.
2001 LadyBug Bear#734003 · Barista BearsThe 2001 Ladybug Bearista, a spring-into-summer novelty bear in a red-and-black ladybug costume. These insect and animal costume bears show Starbucks experimenting with playful seasonal themes well outside the holiday calendar, and the ladybug is among the more charming early-2000s editions. As a single-year release it only turned up briefly in stores, making intact costumed examples the ones collectors hunt.
2002 Summer Beach Bear#734004 · Barista BearsThe 2002 Summer Beach Bearista, a warm-weather bear kitted out for the shore, part of Starbucks' push to give the plush line a year-round seasonal rhythm. Summer Bearistas are less common than the Christmas bears because they sold in a shorter, quieter window, so a beach-themed 2002 example is a nice off-season find. It is exactly the kind of bear that rounds out a collection beyond the predictable holiday entries.
2003 Chicken Bear#734005 · Barista BearsThe 2003 Chicken Bearista, a spring-season novelty with the bear tucked into a fluffy chicken costume, clearly aimed at the Easter window. Costume bears like this are the most fun corner of the Bearista world because the familiar plush face peeks out from an unexpected outfit. As a one-year barnyard oddity it is the sort of piece that makes people stop and ask what on earth they are looking at.
2003 Easter Rabbit Bear#734006 · Barista BearsThe 2003 Easter Rabbit Bearista, a bear in full bunny costume with ears, continuing the spring tradition that ran back to the late-1990s Easter editions. Starbucks leaned on rabbits and chicks every spring, so lining up the Easter bears year by year shows how the costumes evolved over time. Single-season release and soft costume ears mean clean, complete examples are the ones that hold their value.
2004 Gardener Bear#734007 · Barista BearsThe 2004 Gardener Bearista, dressed for the spring planting season as part of that year's seasonal lineup. The gardener theme is one of the gentler, everyday-life costumes Starbucks chose, a nice contrast to the holiday and animal getups. Springtime Bearistas sold in smaller numbers than the December bears, so a tidy 2004 gardener with its accessories intact is a quiet but rewarding catch.
2004 Lady Liberty Bear#734008 · Barista BearsThe 2004 Lady Liberty Bearista, a New York-themed bear styled after the Statue of Liberty with crown and torch, one of the location and landmark bears Starbucks produced alongside its city mugs. The Liberty bear ties straight into the brand's deep New York memorabilia tradition, which makes it a crossover favorite for collectors of both bears and city pieces. Original-tag examples are the ones to chase, since the costume details are what give it away.
2004 Little Bo Peep's Bear#734009 · Barista BearsThe 2004 Little Bo Peep Bearista, a storybook-themed bear dressed as the nursery-rhyme shepherdess, complete with her bonnet and crook. The fairy-tale costume bears are a charming niche within the line, showing Starbucks reaching into folklore for its 2004 seasonal characters. As a single-year release with delicate accessories, a complete Bo Peep with her staff intact is the version collectors actually want.
2005 Black Cat Halloween Bear#734010 · Barista BearsStarbucks launched the honey-colored Bearista in 1997, dressed in a tiny green apron, and by the mid-2000s the seasonal editions were arriving by the dozens each year. This 2005 Halloween bear comes costumed as a black cat, ears and all, part of the autumn run that collectors hunt to complete the spooky sub-theme. The annual Halloween bears are some of the more playful in the line, and intact tags meaningfully lift resale value.
2005 Boston Patriot Bear#734011 · Barista BearsA 2005 regional Bearista decked in colonial Patriot garb, a nod to Boston's Revolutionary War roots, the city of Paul Revere's ride, the Boston Tea Party, and the Freedom Trail. City and team-themed Bearistas were sold mostly in their home markets, so a Boston bear surfacing outside New England is a genuine find. Each carries an edition number on its hang tag, the detail collectors check first.
2005 Frog Bear#734012 · Barista BearsThis 2005 Bearista wears a full green frog costume, hood and all, one of the whimsical animal-suit bears Starbucks released alongside the city and holiday editions. The costumed-critter bears were never numbered like the flagship annual holiday Bearista, which makes documenting them on sites like bearista.org part of the fun. Condition is everything here since the soft costume fabric mats and fades with handling.
2005 Halloween Black Cat Bear#734013 · Barista BearsAnother entry in the 2005 Halloween group, this Bearista is dressed as a black cat, a near-twin to the season's other feline release and the kind of close variant that trips up collectors building a complete year set. Halloween Bearistas began appearing as the line exploded past dozens of editions a year in the mid-2000s. Mint tags and an unfaded costume are what separate a display piece from a flea-market find.
2005 Leopard Bear#734014 · Barista BearsA 2005 Bearista zipped into a spotted leopard suit, part of the animal-costume wave that ran parallel to Starbucks' city and holiday bears that year. These critter-suit editions lean into the plush novelty rather than the apron-clad barista look, and they tend to be cheaper than the numbered holiday flagship. Still, finding one with the costume's spots crisp and the hang tag attached is the collector's quiet victory.
2005 Thrive Bear#734015 · Barista BearsThis is not a retail bear at all. The 2005 Thrive Bearista was handed out to store managers at Starbucks' annual Leadership Conference, a cyclist bear promoting the company's Thrive employee wellness program. Because it never sold in stores, it is genuinely scarce in the collector market, and the conference-exclusive provenance is exactly the kind of inside-Starbucks story that makes a piece worth picking up. A 2006 soccer-themed Thrive bear followed.
2006 Chinese New Year Bear#734016 · Barista BearsReleased for the 2006 Year of the Dog, this Chinese New Year Bearista was an Asia-market exclusive, typically holding a red Chinese lantern and sold heavily in Taiwan. The CNY bears ran annually from 2006 onward and are some of the most collected in the whole line. Taiwan editions in new condition with mint tags have been listed near $249, so this is one of the more valuable bears in any 2006 set.
2006 Gardener Bear#734017 · Barista BearsThis 2006 Bearista plays gardener, a sweet everyday-occupation costume from the line's most prolific stretch. Starbucks began the Bearista in 1997 and by 2006 was releasing them to mark seasons, hobbies, cities, and causes, so themed bears like this filled out a busy yearly lineup. Like all the occupation bears, value rests almost entirely on condition and the presence of the original hang tag.
2006 Golfer Bear#734018 · Barista BearsA 2006 Bearista outfitted as a golfer, cap, club, and all, from the era when Starbucks was pushing past sixty new bear editions a year. The hobby and sport costume bears like this one were a relaxed counterpoint to the numbered holiday flagship and the prized Asia city releases. Collectors prize a clean tag and an intact pose, since the little accessories are easily lost.
2006 Monkey Bear#734019 · Barista BearsA 2006 Bearista dressed in a monkey costume, another of the animal-suit novelties that ran alongside the year's holiday and city editions. These costumed bears were never given the holiday flagship's edition numbers, so collectors lean on catalog sites to confirm year and identity. The plush monkey suit fades and mats easily, which makes a bright, tagged example the one worth owning.
2006 Valentine's Day Bear#734020 · Barista BearsValentine's Day Bearistas became a fixture in the seasonal rotation, and this 2006 release leans into the romance theme with hearts and red trim. The holiday-occasion bears like Valentine, Halloween, and Christmas form the backbone of the line and are the ones most people remember from the counter displays. A bear with its original tag and unfaded red details is what completes a holiday year set.
2007 Black Cat Bear#734021 · Barista BearsStarbucks returned to the black-cat costume for 2007, continuing a Halloween motif the brand revisited across several autumns. That recurrence is exactly why cataloging matters, since a 2007 cat and a 2005 cat look alike but are distinct year editions collectors track separately. Pulled from a season when the line was still cranking out dozens of bears, it is common enough to find but best with a crisp hang tag.
2007 Halloween Bat Bear#734022 · Barista BearsThis 2007 Halloween Bearista is costumed as a bat, wings spread, a fresh twist on the autumn lineup after years of cat and pumpkin themes. The Halloween bears are among the most characterful in the whole run, and the bat is a standout for its sculpted felt wings. As always with the seasonal plush, faded color and a missing tag are what knock down value, so a bright tagged one is the keeper.
2007 Vacation Bear#734023 · Barista BearsA 2007 Bearista dressed for holiday travel, sunglasses and beach-vibe outfit, from the lifestyle and hobby sub-themes that padded out the line's busiest years. Vacation and leisure bears were a light counterpoint to the numbered Christmas flagship and the sought-after Asia city editions. Collector value here is modest and tag-dependent, the kind of cheerful filler bear that rounds out a year more than it anchors a collection.
2008 Blue Yellow Butterfly Bear#734024 · Barista BearsThis 2008 Bearista wears blue and yellow butterfly wings, one half of a spring color pair Starbucks released that year. Pieces sold as twins or color variants are a known collector trap, since you need both the blue-yellow and the pink-yellow to truly complete the set. The springtime butterfly bears are bright and display well, with a clean tag again being the line between a keeper and a castoff.
2008 Bunny Bear#734025 · Barista BearsA 2008 Easter-season Bearista in a bunny costume, ears up, from the spring rotation that paired with the year's butterfly bears. Easter bunny Bearistas recur across multiple years like the Halloween cats, so collectors note the year carefully to avoid duplicate-looking editions. Soft and seasonal, its worth rides almost entirely on an unfaded costume and the original Starbucks hang tag.
2008 Pink Yellow Butterfly Bear#734026 · Barista BearsThe pink-and-yellow companion to 2008's blue-yellow butterfly Bearista, this is the other half of that spring color pair. Matched-variant releases like this are deliberately collectible, rewarding anyone who chases down both wings to finish the set rather than settling for one. A bright, tagged example of the harder-to-find color of a pair is exactly the small win that makes building a Bearista year worthwhile.
2009 Hawaii Bear#734027 · Barista BearsA 2009 Hawaii regional Bearista, an island-exclusive tied to Starbucks' long-running Hawaii collectibles that lean on aloha and tropical motifs. Hawaii Starbucks pieces have a devoted following of their own, which keeps demand for the local bears steady among completists.
2009 Japan Bear#734028 · Barista BearsThis 2009 Japan Bearista is the prized kimono-and-hakama design, an Asia exclusive sold as a boy-and-girl pair in traditional dress, often with an embroidered family-crest detail featuring a coffee cup. The craftsmanship on the kimono fabric makes this one of the most beautiful bears in the line.
2010 Japan Bear#734029 · Barista BearsA Bearista from the year Starbucks shipped more than sixty of these little plush mascots, the most the line ever ran. This Japan edition belongs to the destination wing of a series that began in 1997 and was eventually edition-numbered on a paper hang tag, and collectors stress that a bear without its intact tag loses most of its value. Japan was always one of the strongest Bearista markets, which is part of why the line survived in Asia long after it vanished from U.S. stores.
2010 Las Vegas Bear#734030 · Barista BearsPart of the 2010 Destination Series, the city-specific arm of the Bearista program where each plush wore a hometown costume. As with every Bearista, value lives in the paper hang tag, so I keep this one's tag fully intact.
2011 Green Puffer Jacket Bear#734031 · Barista BearsA 2011 winter Bearista bundled in a green puffer jacket, the house color worn as cold-weather gear. 2012 Nutcracker Bear#734032 · Barista BearsThis is the 107th Edition Bearista, the 2012 Nutcracker Soldier, dressed as the toy soldier from Tchaikovsky's Christmas ballet. Knowing the exact edition number matters here because the value guides track these bears by edition, and a tagged 107th is the genuine article.

Soccer-themed Bearistas from this era are uncommon, and the giving-back angle is exactly the kind of provenance I like documenting in the collection.
Arizona Diamond Backs Bear#734034 · Barista BearsOne of the MLB team Bearistas, this one in Arizona Diamondbacks colors. Arizona Diamondbacks Bear#734035 · Barista BearsA second Arizona Diamondbacks MLB Bearista in the collection, which is useful for spotting edition or series variants since these baseball bears ran across multiple printings. Lining two of the same team side by side is the only reliable way to catch a tag or uniform difference.
Atlanta Braves Bear#734036 · Barista BearsThe Atlanta Braves MLB Bearista, from the licensed baseball line Starbucks launched in 2003. The Braves are one of the sport's most storied franchises, owners of a record fourteen straight division titles in the 1990s and 2000s, and their bear wears the classic tomahawk-era colors. Baseball Bearistas are collected as a team set, so a tagged Braves fills a specific slot for set builders.
Barista Bear (With Brown Apron of#734037 · Barista BearsA Bearista wearing the brown apron, a deliberate nod to 1971, the year Starbucks opened at Pike Place Market when the original aprons were brown, not green. Collectors love pieces that reference the founding year, so the brown apron makes this one of the more meaningful bears to own and explain.
Barista (With Green Apron) Bear#734038 · Barista BearsThe core Bearista, a bear in the Starbucks green apron, which is the design that gives the whole line its name. Boston Red Sox Bear#734040 · Barista BearsThe Boston Red Sox MLB Bearista, and the Red Sox were one of the seven teams in the original 2003 first-edition baseball series alongside the Giants, Angels, Mariners, Cubs, Dodgers and Yankees. A tagged first-series Red Sox is a cornerstone for anyone assembling the baseball run.

Chinese New Year 2010 Tiger Bear#734043 · Barista BearsThis is the 90th Edition Bearista, the 2010 Year of the Tiger, one of the most recognizable of the Lunar New Year zodiac series. Chinese New Year 2014 Horse Bear#734044 · Barista BearsThe 2014 Year of the Horse Bearista, a later entry in the Lunar New Year zodiac line that ran from the mid-2000s into the 2010s. Chinese New Year Dragon Bear#734045 · Barista BearsThe Year of the Dragon Bearista, the most coveted sign in the entire zodiac because the dragon is the only mythical animal and the luckiest birth year in Chinese culture. Chinese New Year Pig Bear#734046 · Barista BearsPart of the Asia-market Chinese New Year run that marched through all twelve zodiac animals, this Bearista marks a Year of the Pig, the cycle's final and famously lucky sign tied to wealth and good fortune. Chinese New Year Rooster Bear#734048 · Barista BearsThe Rooster is the tenth animal of the Chinese zodiac, prized for confidence and a hardworking streak, and this Bearista belongs to the Asia-only Chinese New Year line. Holiday Bear#734052 · Barista BearsA core seasonal Bearista from the long-running holiday plush line that Starbucks released nearly every winter, dressed in scarf-and-sweater festive gear meant to sit by the register through December. Condition is everything here since so many were handled and loved, so a tagged, clean one stands out.
